nav_entries.description: On Worklittle, swipe to apply means you can skip, save, or start Apply with AI from the same card. Other swipe apps often stop at matching or saving. Worklittle’s job deck is swipe to apply on more than 3 million open jobs. You can skip a role, save it for later, or tap Apply to start Apply with AI, which fills and sends the employer’s own application. Open the deck at [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs), or read the public walkthrough at [Tinder for Jobs](https://worklittle.com/tinder-for-jobs). This page explains how that differs from swipe apps that mainly match or queue jobs.

nav_entries.label: Worklittle vs LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and AI tools
nav_entries.title: Worklittle vs LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and AI tools
nav_entries.description: How Worklittle compares to LinkedIn, Indeed, ZipRecruiter, and many other job search tools, plus AI chat like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

nav_entries.label: Saved jobs overview
nav_entries.title: Saved jobs overview
nav_entries.description: Your hiring pipeline in one place. Saved jobs is every role you are interested in, in one place. On a computer it opens as a list. You can switch to Grid when you want the column board.

nav_entries.label: Pipeline stages explained
nav_entries.title: Pipeline stages explained
nav_entries.description: Saved through Offer, plus Skipped and Viewed when you have passed on or looked at roles. Each column on your Saved board is a stage, representing how far along you are with that particular role.

nav_entries.label: Move jobs between stages
nav_entries.title: Move jobs between stages
nav_entries.description: Drag or pick a stage. Moving a job to a new stage takes a second, either by dragging the card or picking a stage from its menu.

nav_entries.label: Share your Saved board
nav_entries.title: Share your Saved board
nav_entries.description: Send a link to someone you trust. You can share a view of your Saved board with a mentor, career counsellor, or family member so they can see your search without needing your account.

nav_entries.label: Saved jobs on mobile
nav_entries.title: Saved jobs on mobile
nav_entries.description: Use the list on your phone. On a phone your Saved board becomes a scrollable list, so you can review and update your search from anywhere without pinching around a wide board.

nav_entries.label: Reorder columns
nav_entries.title: Reorder columns
nav_entries.description: Customize your board layout. You can rearrange the columns on your Saved board so the stages you check most often sit where you want them.

nav_entries.label: Skipped jobs
nav_entries.title: Skipped jobs
nav_entries.description: Find roles you passed on. Roles you skip are not deleted. They move to the **Skipped** column on your Saved board, so you can look back if you change your mind or skipped one by accident.

nav_entries.label: Share your job search history
nav_entries.title: Share your job search history
nav_entries.description: Send your board to someone, and read it yourself. Your Saved board is the record of your whole search. You cannot download it as a file, but you can send someone a link to it and you can read a lot from it yourself.

nav_entries.label: Chat basics
nav_entries.title: Chat basics
nav_entries.description: Start conversations and get career help. Chat is your free career assistant on worklittle.com, ready to answer questions, rewrite your resume, and walk you through a job search.

nav_entries.label: Chats and threads
nav_entries.title: Chats and threads
nav_entries.description: Find, rename, pin, share, and continue past conversations. Every conversation you have is saved as its own chat, so you can come back days later and pick up exactly where you left off.

nav_entries.label: Photos, files, and video in chat
nav_entries.title: Photos, files, and video in chat
nav_entries.description: Attach media to your messages. You can send photos, documents, and short videos to chat so it can read them and respond to what is actually in front of you.

nav_entries.label: Voice dictation
nav_entries.title: Voice dictation
nav_entries.description: Speak instead of type. Dictation lets you talk to chat instead of typing, which is handy on a phone, in the car park before an interview, or any time typing is slow.

nav_entries.label: Slash skills menu
nav_entries.title: Slash skills menu
nav_entries.description: Shortcuts for common AI actions. Typing a forward slash in the message box opens a menu of ready-made skills, so you can trigger a common task without writing out a long request.

nav_entries.label: Memories and favorites
nav_entries.title: Memories and favorites
nav_entries.description: What Worklittle remembers about you. Memories are the details Worklittle keeps between conversations, like the roles you want and the city you are searching in, so you stop repeating yourself.

nav_entries.label: Create or edit a resume in chat
nav_entries.title: Create or edit a resume in chat
nav_entries.description: Build application materials with AI. Chat can build a complete resume from a conversation, or take the resume you already have and sharpen it for a specific job.

nav_entries.label: Cover letters from chat
nav_entries.title: Cover letters from chat
nav_entries.description: Draft tailored cover letters. Chat writes cover letters that reference the actual posting, so each application reads like it was written for that employer rather than copied from a template.

nav_entries.label: AI headshots
nav_entries.title: AI headshots
nav_entries.description: Create a professional photo for applications. AI headshots turn an ordinary photo of you into a clean, professional-looking portrait you can use on applications and profiles.

nav_entries.label: Whiteboards
nav_entries.title: Whiteboards
nav_entries.description: Draw diagrams and brainstorm visually. A whiteboard is a blank canvas inside chat where you can sketch, map out ideas, and think through something visually instead of in paragraphs.

nav_entries.label: Documents in chat
nav_entries.title: Documents in chat
nav_entries.description: Create and edit docs from conversation. Documents give your resume, cover letter, or notes a proper editable page inside Worklittle, so you can format, download, and share them.

nav_entries.label: Report a chat
nav_entries.title: Report a chat
nav_entries.description: Flag something that feels wrong. If a response is harmful, wrong in a way that matters, or just plain strange, you can report a concern so the team can look into it. You can do this while signed out.

nav_entries.label: Tips for better answers
nav_entries.title: Tips for better answers
nav_entries.description: How to ask so chat helps faster. A few small habits make a big difference in how useful chat is, and most of them come down to giving it your real situation instead of a generic question.

nav_entries.label: What is Worklittle chat?
nav_entries.title: What is Worklittle chat?
nav_entries.description: What the career assistant on worklittle.com can help with. Worklittle chat is the AI career assistant on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). It helps with job search tasks: resumes, cover letters, interview prep, career quizzes, research, and more.

nav_entries.label: Connect with AI (voice)
nav_entries.title: Connect with AI (voice)
nav_entries.description: Talk with Worklittle using the Live AI voice orb, separate from typing dictation. Connect with AI starts a spoken conversation with Worklittle. A Live AI orb appears while you talk. This is different from the microphone that turns speech into text in the message box.

nav_entries.label: Attachment size and storage limits
nav_entries.title: Attachment size and storage limits
nav_entries.description: How large files can be, how many per message, and how long they are kept. Chat attachments have size, count, and storage limits so uploads stay reliable.

nav_entries.label: Chat and AI limits
nav_entries.title: Chat and AI limits
nav_entries.description: How free allowances, Instant, and pay as you go affect chat on worklittle.com. Chat, Apply with AI, dictation, Live AI, headshots, and similar features on worklittle.com share the same AI usage rules.

nav_entries.label: Search your chat history
nav_entries.title: Search your chat history
nav_entries.description: Find an older conversation from the sidebar search. You can search past chats from the same search experience that also finds jobs and companies.

nav_entries.label: How many chats can run at once?
nav_entries.title: How many chats can run at once?
nav_entries.description: Overlapping chat replies are fine; AI credit is the real limit. You can start several chat replies at once. There is no fixed concurrent chat count. Signed-in free AI credit (and Instant or a payment method when that runs out) is what stops new usage.

nav_entries.label: Share a chat link
nav_entries.title: Share a chat link
nav_entries.description: Copy a temporary link to a conversation, and what happens when it expires. You need to be signed in to create a share link. Job seeker links are public for anyone who has them. They last about 48 hours.

nav_entries.label: Delete a chat
nav_entries.title: Delete a chat
nav_entries.description: Remove a conversation from your sidebar permanently. Deleting a chat removes that conversation from your list. There is no separate archive option.

nav_entries.label: Chat as a guest
nav_entries.title: Chat as a guest
nav_entries.description: What works without an account, and what signing in unlocks. You can try chat on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) without signing in. Signing in keeps history and raises some limits.

nav_entries.label: Use chat on your phone
nav_entries.title: Use chat on your phone
nav_entries.description: Worklittle chat in a mobile browser, including the bottom navigation. There is no separate Worklittle Chat app in the App Store or Play Store. Use [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) in your phone browser.

nav_entries.label: Chat is slow or shows an error
nav_entries.title: Chat is slow or shows an error
nav_entries.description: What to try when replies stall, fail, or hit a limit. Most chat trouble comes from a flaky network, a busy generation, or an AI usage limit.

nav_entries.label: Headshot limits
nav_entries.title: Headshot limits
nav_entries.description: How many AI headshots you can create as a guest or signed in. AI headshots turn a photo of you into a professional-looking portrait. Creation is rate limited so the feature stays available for everyone.

nav_entries.label: How whiteboards are saved
nav_entries.title: How whiteboards are saved
nav_entries.description: One shared whiteboard per account or browser, not a new board for every chat. Worklittle keeps one whiteboard for you to draw on. Opening a board from different chats uses that same canvas rather than creating a separate board for each conversation.

nav_entries.label: Job seeker chat vs Business chat
nav_entries.title: Job seeker chat vs Business chat
nav_entries.description: Why your personal chats and work chats never mix. Job seeker chat on worklittle.com and Business chat on worklittle.com/business are separate lists.

nav_entries.label: Ask chat what it can do
nav_entries.title: Ask chat what it can do
nav_entries.description: How to discover features inside the product when you are unsure. If you are not sure whether Worklittle can help with a task, ask in plain language or open the slash skills menu.

nav_entries.label: What's new in chat
nav_entries.title: What's new in chat
nav_entries.description: Where to find product updates that affect worklittle.com chat. Worklittle publishes release notes in the docs. There is no separate in-chat changelog page.

nav_entries.label: Create an account
nav_entries.title: Create an account
nav_entries.description: Sign up with Google or an email address. There is no separate registration form. Worklittle does not have a signup page that is different from the login page, so creating an account and signing in are the same few taps.

nav_entries.label: Sign in with Google
nav_entries.title: Sign in with Google
nav_entries.description: The one-tap option, and what to do when the Google window misbehaves. Google sign-in skips the code-in-your-inbox step entirely and is the quickest way into Worklittle.

nav_entries.label: Sign in with an email code
nav_entries.title: Sign in with an email code
nav_entries.description: Get a six-digit code in your inbox and type it in. No password needed. If you would rather not use Google or set a password, Worklittle can email you a short code each time you sign in.

nav_entries.label: Sign in with a password
nav_entries.title: Sign in with a password
nav_entries.description: Set a password once so you do not have to check your email every time. A password is optional on Worklittle, but it makes signing in on a new device much quicker.

nav_entries.label: Switch between accounts
nav_entries.title: Switch between accounts
nav_entries.description: Keep up to three accounts signed in and move between them without logging out. Worklittle can hold up to three signed-in accounts at once, which is handy if you keep personal and work life separate. This switches which email you are signed in as, not which company workspace you are in.

nav_entries.label: Manage linked emails
nav_entries.title: Manage linked emails
nav_entries.description: How email addresses relate to your account, your device, and your profile. Worklittle uses email in three different ways, and knowing which is which clears up most confusion.

nav_entries.label: Work email vs personal email
nav_entries.title: Work email vs personal email
nav_entries.description: Which address to sign in with, and where your work address belongs. Short answer: sign in with a personal address if you are job hunting, and a work address if you are hiring.

nav_entries.label: Sign out
nav_entries.title: Sign out
nav_entries.description: How to sign out, and what stays behind on the device afterwards. Signing out ends the session on that device and leaves everything in your account untouched.

nav_entries.label: Delete your account
nav_entries.title: Delete your account
nav_entries.description: How to permanently delete your account, and the three-day window to change your mind. Deleting removes your account and everything in it, with a short grace period in case you have second thoughts.

nav_entries.label: Trouble signing in
nav_entries.title: Trouble signing in
nav_entries.description: Fixes for the problems that come up most often when logging in. Most sign-in trouble comes down to a missing email, an expired code, or a blocked popup, and all three are quick to sort out.

nav_entries.label: AI usage limits
nav_entries.title: AI usage limits
nav_entries.description: How much free AI you get, and what to do when you need more. Browsing and saving jobs are free. Chat, Apply with AI, resumes, and similar AI help use a free monthly AI amount. When that runs out, you can add Instant or keep going with a card.

nav_entries.label: Billing overview
nav_entries.title: Billing overview
nav_entries.description: Pay as you go, manage your card, and review invoices for your organization. Each organization (including your Personal workspace) has its own bill. Usage adds to amount owed. We charge your card on the 1st of each UTC month if you owe at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20. Balances under $0.50 wait. Manage everything on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).

nav_entries.label: Worklittle Instant
nav_entries.title: Worklittle Instant
nav_entries.description: The $9.99 plan with $20 of AI credit for Apply with AI, resumes, headshots, and chat on worklittle.com. Worklittle Instant is the paid plan for AI help while you job hunt on worklittle.com. It costs $9.99 per month and includes $20 of AI credit for each Instant billing period.

nav_entries.label: Invite friends and earn credit
nav_entries.title: Invite friends and earn credit
nav_entries.description: Share your invite from Refer. Instant members earn $5 when a friend buys Instant. Signed-in free accounts earn $0.50 when a friend joins, up to $20. Open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) while signed in. It is a full-screen overlay, same as [Plans](https://worklittle.com/plans). Close it with the X in the top right. Worklittle Instant members share a checkout invite. Signed-in accounts without Instant share a join invite. Full rules are in [Referral Terms](/help/account/referral-terms).

nav_entries.label: Gifting credits
nav_entries.title: Gifting credits
nav_entries.description: Buy usage credit for a friend. Unclaimed gifts refund after 30 days. Claimed credit expires after 365 days. You can gift Worklittle usage credit to a friend. They open the claim link, pick which Worklittle account the gift belongs to, then Accept it on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) onto whichever organization they want. This is separate from [referral rewards](/help/account/refer-friends).

nav_entries.label: Referral Terms
nav_entries.title: Referral Terms
nav_entries.description: Eligibility, rewards, limits, and clawback rules for Worklittle Instant referrals and join invites. These Referral Terms apply to Worklittle referral programs on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). By creating referral links, sending invites, or claiming referral credit, you agree to these terms. For a short how-to, see [Invite friends and earn credit](/help/account/refer-friends).

nav_entries.label: Donate to Worklittle
nav_entries.title: Donate to Worklittle
nav_entries.description: How donations work, tax receipts, and where to donate. You can support Worklittle with a one-time donation to Curastem, the nonprofit that operates it. Donations are separate from Instant, API usage, and Business billing. [curastem.org](https://curastem.org) is the nonprofit site.

nav_entries.label: Usage dashboard
nav_entries.title: Usage dashboard
nav_entries.description: See what you used and what it cost. The Usage page shows where your organization's amount owed came from, so you can understand the bill.

nav_entries.label: Spend limits
nav_entries.title: Spend limits
nav_entries.description: Cap your monthly spend and get an email before you hit it. A spend limit is a ceiling you set for the month. It protects you from a runaway script or an unexpectedly busy week.

nav_entries.label: Payment required messages
nav_entries.title: Payment required messages
nav_entries.description: What a payment error means and how to clear it. A payment error means Worklittle received your request but cannot complete it until the billing side is sorted out. There is nothing to "add credit" for. Fix the card or the monthly limit.

nav_entries.label: Pricing basics
nav_entries.title: Pricing basics
nav_entries.description: Where to read what things cost. Prices are published in the docs so you can check them before you build anything. This article points you to the right page.

nav_entries.label: Cancel Worklittle Instant
nav_entries.title: Cancel Worklittle Instant
nav_entries.description: How to cancel Instant, what happens to your credit, and when the last charge applies. You can cancel Worklittle Instant anytime. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the period you already paid for, so you keep Instant until then.

nav_entries.label: Add, change, or remove a payment method
nav_entries.title: Add, change, or remove a payment method
nav_entries.description: Manage the card or bank account Stripe uses for Instant and pay-as-you-go billing. Payment methods are managed through Stripe on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). Each organization (including Personal) has its own payment method.

nav_entries.label: Find past invoices
nav_entries.title: Find past invoices
nav_entries.description: Where Instant and pay-as-you-go invoices show up. Past charges appear on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) for the organization that was billed.

nav_entries.label: When Worklittle charges your card
nav_entries.title: When Worklittle charges your card
nav_entries.description: When Instant renews, and when pay-as-you-go AI charges hit your card. If you owe AI charges, we usually bill near the start of each month. If you owe $20 or more sooner, we may charge then. Instant’s $9.99 renews on the same day each month you signed up. Both show on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).

nav_entries.label: Free AI, Instant, and pay as you go
nav_entries.title: Free AI, Instant, and pay as you go
nav_entries.description: How free AI, Instant, and a Personal card work together on worklittle.com. You get free AI each month when you sign in. Instant gives you more AI credit for $9.99 a month. If you use more than that, a card on Billing covers extra AI use. Looking for jobs stays free.

nav_entries.label: Can I buy prepaid credits?
nav_entries.title: Can I buy prepaid credits?
nav_entries.description: Yes. Buy credit on Billing in whole dollars from $1 to $500. Yes. On [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), use **Buy credit** in the Credit balance box. That buys usage credit for the organization you have selected. Amounts are whole dollars from $1 to $500. Credit is used before your card is charged for additional usage.

nav_entries.label: Refunds and withdrawals
nav_entries.title: Refunds and withdrawals
nav_entries.description: What Instant credit means for refunds, and how EEA/UK/Switzerland withdrawal works. There is no self-serve refund button in the app. Instant AI credit is for usage only. It is not cash and is not refundable as spending money.

nav_entries.label: Can I transfer Instant to another account?
nav_entries.title: Can I transfer Instant to another account?
nav_entries.description: No. Instant stays on the account that subscribed. No. Worklittle Instant cannot be transferred to a different email or account. Subscriptions are not movable between people.

nav_entries.label: I see a charge I do not recognize
nav_entries.title: I see a charge I do not recognize
nav_entries.description: How to match a bank charge to Instant, pay as you go, or a donation. Most unrecognized charges are Instant renewals, pay-as-you-go collection, or a donation. Match the date and amount on Billing before disputing with your bank.

nav_entries.label: Why was my card declined?
nav_entries.title: Why was my card declined?
nav_entries.description: What to try when Stripe cannot charge your payment method. A declined card usually means the bank rejected the charge, the card expired, or there is not enough available credit. Worklittle cannot override a bank decline.

nav_entries.label: Why did Instant renewal fail?
nav_entries.title: Why did Instant renewal fail?
nav_entries.description: What happens when the $9.99 Instant charge does not go through. Instant stops when the $9.99 renewal does not succeed. Instant only stays on while Stripe shows the subscription as active. Fix the Personal payment method, then check Plans or Billing.

nav_entries.label: Which organization am I paying for?
nav_entries.title: Which organization am I paying for?
nav_entries.description: Personal vs company wallets, Instant, and why the wrong workspace looks like a wrong bill. Every organization has its own bill and payment method. Checking the wrong workspace is the most common billing confusion.

nav_entries.label: I forgot my password
nav_entries.title: I forgot my password
nav_entries.description: Use an email code to get back in, then set a new password. Worklittle does not send a separate “reset password” email. Sign in with a one-time email code, then create a new password.

nav_entries.label: Can I change my login email?
nav_entries.title: Can I change my login email?
nav_entries.description: No. Your sign-in email is fixed on that account. No. You cannot edit the email address on an existing Worklittle account. One email is one account.

nav_entries.label: Export your data
nav_entries.title: Export your data
nav_entries.description: Download a copy of your account data from Settings. You can export your account data anytime from Settings. Do this before you delete an account if you want a copy.

nav_entries.label: I deleted my account. Can I get it back?
nav_entries.title: I deleted my account. Can I get it back?
nav_entries.description: Yes for three days. After that, no. Yes, for three days. Sign in again with the same email to cancel the deletion. After that, no—the account is gone.

nav_entries.label: Keep your account secure
nav_entries.title: Keep your account secure
nav_entries.description: Practical steps that match how Worklittle sign-in actually works. Worklittle sign-in uses Google, a 6-digit email code, and an optional password. There is no passkey or authenticator-app MFA in the product today.

nav_entries.label: I received a login code I did not request
nav_entries.title: I received a login code I did not request
nav_entries.description: What an unexpected sign-in email means and what to do next. A 6-digit code from no-reply@worklittle.com means someone typed your email on the sign-in page. It does not mean they got into your account.

nav_entries.label: New device notification
nav_entries.title: New device notification
nav_entries.description: Why you might see a “new device logged in” notice. Worklittle can show an in-app notice when your account signs in from a device that looks new. It is an alert, not a separate security challenge.

nav_entries.label: Change your name on Worklittle
nav_entries.title: Change your name on Worklittle
nav_entries.description: Update the name on your job seeker profile in Settings. Your profile name is editable in Settings. That is the name used on your job seeker profile and related AI fills. It is separate from the email you use to sign in.

nav_entries.label: Edit your profile
nav_entries.title: Edit your profile
nav_entries.description: Name, dream job, school, and more. Your profile is the source of truth for everything Apply with AI types into employer forms.

nav_entries.label: Profile photo
nav_entries.title: Profile photo
nav_entries.description: Camera, upload, or default avatar. A photo shows up next to your name in chats and on your Worklittle account.

nav_entries.label: Upload or replace your resume
nav_entries.title: Upload or replace your resume
nav_entries.description: Keep applications ready. One resume on file keeps you ready to apply anywhere on Worklittle in a single tap.

nav_entries.label: Skills and interests
nav_entries.title: Skills and interests
nav_entries.description: Chips that describe you. The **Your favorite things** field is a quick list of what you are good at and what you enjoy.

nav_entries.label: Work authorization countries
nav_entries.title: Work authorization countries
nav_entries.description: Where you can work. Tell us which countries you can already work in so applications answer the sponsorship question correctly.

nav_entries.label: Social and portfolio links
nav_entries.title: Social and portfolio links
nav_entries.description: Add LinkedIn and sites. Employers ask for links constantly, so saving them once means never typing them again.

nav_entries.label: Email preferences
nav_entries.title: Email preferences
nav_entries.description: Alerts, events, announcements. You control exactly which emails Worklittle sends you, and you can change your mind at any time.

nav_entries.label: Instant job alerts
nav_entries.title: Instant job alerts
nav_entries.description: Emails based on the role you want. Job alerts email you new matching roles without you having to check the site every day.

nav_entries.label: Your dream role field
nav_entries.title: Your dream role field
nav_entries.description: The Job title field, with several roles and exclusions. The **Job title** field in your Settings is where you say what you want next, and it is the single biggest lever on the jobs Worklittle shows and emails you.

nav_entries.label: Driver's license info
nav_entries.title: Driver's license info
nav_entries.description: When applications ask for it. A simple yes or no about your license saves a pause on the many roles that require driving.

nav_entries.label: What is Worklittle Business?
nav_entries.title: What is Worklittle Business?
nav_entries.description: Employer workspace overview. Worklittle Business at worklittle.com/business is the side of Worklittle where companies post jobs and hire.

nav_entries.label: Create an organization
nav_entries.title: Create an organization
nav_entries.description: Set up your company. An organization is your company's shared workspace, holding your jobs, candidates, and teammates.

nav_entries.label: Verify a work email
nav_entries.title: Verify a work email
nav_entries.description: Required to post jobs. Employer features need an account tied to your company email address, which is how we keep job posts trustworthy.

nav_entries.label: Invite teammates
nav_entries.title: Invite teammates
nav_entries.description: Send invites by email. Bring recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers into your workspace so everyone works from the same pipeline.

nav_entries.label: Roles and permissions
nav_entries.title: Roles and permissions
nav_entries.description: What Owner, Full access, Can edit, Can comment, Can view, and Can chat can each do. Every teammate in Worklittle Business has a role. The role decides which pages they see, what they can change, and how much the chat assistant is allowed to know about your company.

nav_entries.label: Switch organizations
nav_entries.title: Switch organizations
nav_entries.description: Move between Personal and company workspaces. Every login has a Personal workspace, and you may belong to company organizations. You can be in **10** organizations at once, counting Personal. Switch between them without signing out.

nav_entries.label: Join requests
nav_entries.title: Join requests
nav_entries.description: Approve people who ask to join. Colleagues can ask to join your workspace, and someone with full access approves or declines.

nav_entries.label: Remove a teammate
nav_entries.title: Remove a teammate
nav_entries.description: Take someone off the org. When someone changes roles or leaves the company, remove them so your workspace stays current.

nav_entries.label: Transfer ownership
nav_entries.title: Transfer ownership
nav_entries.description: Hand the org to someone else. Ownership can move to another teammate when you change roles or leave the company.

nav_entries.label: Public company profile
nav_entries.title: Public company profile
nav_entries.description: What candidates may see. Your company page is what job seekers see when they come across one of your openings.

nav_entries.label: Notifications center
nav_entries.title: Notifications center
nav_entries.description: One place for hiring, document, survey, and team updates. The notifications panel collects everything that happened while you were away so you can catch up in one pass.

nav_entries.label: Search in Business
nav_entries.title: Search in Business
nav_entries.description: Find jobs, people, chats, and tools from anywhere in the app. Search is the fastest way to move around Worklittle Business. Instead of clicking through the sidebar, type what you are looking for.

nav_entries.label: Logo, banner, and brand color
nav_entries.title: Logo, banner, and brand color
nav_entries.description: Make your organization profile and job board look like your company. Your brand assets appear on your public job board, on shared job links, and inside Worklittle Business for your team.

nav_entries.label: AI brand images
nav_entries.title: AI brand images
nav_entries.description: Create or edit your logo or banner by describing what you want in chat. If you do not have a designer available, you can create a logo or banner from scratch, or describe a change to an existing one, and the assistant will produce a new version.

nav_entries.label: Organization details
nav_entries.title: Organization details
nav_entries.description: Legal name, job board address, website, and headquarters. The **Organization** page holds the facts about your company. Some of it is public on your profile and job board, and some is internal.

nav_entries.label: Privacy and terms links
nav_entries.title: Privacy and terms links
nav_entries.description: Show your own policies on your public organization profile. You can point candidates at your own privacy policy and terms of service. These links appear alongside your public profile and job board.

nav_entries.label: Business chat assistant
nav_entries.title: Business chat assistant
nav_entries.description: Ask the employer assistant to do the work for you. Chat is the first item in Worklittle Business sidebar. You can ask it questions about your data and ask it to make changes for you.

nav_entries.label: Worklittle Business FAQ
nav_entries.title: Worklittle Business FAQ
nav_entries.description: Short answers about setting up a company, inviting people, and how company billing works. Worklittle Business is the employer side of Worklittle at [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business). Companies hire, run HR, and connect tools there. You do not buy seats.

nav_entries.label: Do we buy seats for Business?
nav_entries.title: Do we buy seats for Business?
nav_entries.description: No. Worklittle Business bills as you go, not named seats. No. There are no Business seats to purchase. Each company has its own bill and payment method.

nav_entries.label: Why does my company bill look empty?
nav_entries.title: Why does my company bill look empty?
nav_entries.description: Personal Instant and company hiring use different bills. If Instant credit or a charge is missing, you are often looking at the wrong organization.

nav_entries.label: When is my company charged?
nav_entries.title: When is my company charged?
nav_entries.description: On the 1st of each UTC month (if you owe at least $0.50), or sooner at $20 owed. Usually on the 1st of each month (UTC). Usage during the month adds to amount owed. We charge the company card on the 1st of each UTC month if you owe at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20.

nav_entries.label: Cap company AI spend
nav_entries.title: Cap company AI spend
nav_entries.description: Set a monthly hard cap and budget alerts on the company organization. Full access and Owner can limit how much a company organization can spend in a month.

nav_entries.label: Who can see Usage and Billing?
nav_entries.title: Who can see Usage and Billing?
nav_entries.description: Billing, Usage, and Limits are for Full access and Owner. Not every teammate can open company spend pages. That is intentional.

nav_entries.label: Leave an organization
nav_entries.title: Leave an organization
nav_entries.description: How to leave a company workspace and what happens to your access. You can leave a company organization from the Organization page when other people are still on the team. You lose access right away. The organization’s jobs and records stay with the company.

nav_entries.label: Delete a company organization
nav_entries.title: Delete a company organization
nav_entries.description: Delete is for a solo Owner. Company data is scheduled for removal after about 24 hours. Delete is available when you are the Owner and the only remaining member. Remove teammates first if anyone else is still in the company.

nav_entries.label: What happens to data when someone leaves?
nav_entries.title: What happens to data when someone leaves?
nav_entries.description: Access ends for the person. Organization records stay with the company. When someone is removed or leaves, they lose access. Jobs, candidates, notes, and other organization records stay with the company.

nav_entries.label: Why did Full access take a minute?
nav_entries.title: Why did Full access take a minute?
nav_entries.description: Giving someone Full access, or transferring ownership, waits about a minute. Most role changes apply right away. Giving someone Full access, or making them the Owner, waits about a minute before it takes effect.

nav_entries.label: Give employees chat without hiring access
nav_entries.title: Give employees chat without hiring access
nav_entries.description: Use the Can chat role for everyday employees. Can chat is for people who should use Worklittle at work without seeing the hiring pipeline or company admin pages.

nav_entries.label: Do we verify our company domain?
nav_entries.title: Do we verify our company domain?
nav_entries.description: No domain claim. You still need a company work email, and impersonation is not allowed. No. You do not claim or verify ownership of your company website domain. You still must be affiliated with the company you represent.

nav_entries.label: Try the Business demo
nav_entries.title: Try the Business demo
nav_entries.description: Click around Worklittle Business using sample data before you set up your own company. You can try Worklittle Business without creating your own company. The demo is filled with sample data so you can click around safely.

nav_entries.label: Does Instant pay for my company?
nav_entries.title: Does Instant pay for my company?
nav_entries.description: No. Instant is the job-seeker plan on worklittle.com. Your company has a separate bill. No. Worklittle Instant pays for AI help while you job hunt on worklittle.com. It does not pay for hiring or your company workspace.

nav_entries.label: Business chat vs worklittle.com chat
nav_entries.title: Business chat vs worklittle.com chat
nav_entries.description: Employer assistant and job seeker chat are separate histories. Chat on worklittle.com and chat on worklittle.com/business never mix in the sidebar.

nav_entries.label: Share a Business chat with my team
nav_entries.title: Share a Business chat with my team
nav_entries.description: Organization-only share links for employer chats. Business chat share links are for people in your organization. They are not public the way job seeker chat links can be.

nav_entries.label: What's new in Worklittle Business
nav_entries.title: What's new in Worklittle Business
nav_entries.description: Where to find release notes that affect the employer app. Product updates are published in docs release notes rather than a separate Business-only changelog inside the app.

nav_entries.label: Post a job
nav_entries.title: Post a job
nav_entries.description: Write and publish an opening. Posting a job puts your opening in front of candidates on Worklittle and on your own company page.

nav_entries.label: Job description editor
nav_entries.title: Job description editor
nav_entries.description: Format the posting. The description editor gives you proper formatting so your posting reads well instead of arriving as a wall of text.

nav_entries.label: Locations, salary, and workplace
nav_entries.title: Locations, salary, and workplace
nav_entries.description: Set where and how people work. These three details are the first things candidates look for, and filling them in gets your job found.

nav_entries.label: Application fields and screening
nav_entries.title: Application fields and screening
nav_entries.description: Ask candidates the right questions. You decide what applicants have to provide, from the basics through to your own screening questions.

nav_entries.label: Publish, close, or delete a job
nav_entries.title: Publish, close, or delete a job
nav_entries.description: Control visibility. A job moves between draft, published, and closed depending on where you are in the process.

nav_entries.label: Jobs board and pipeline
nav_entries.title: Jobs board and pipeline
nav_entries.description: See all your openings. The Jobs page at worklittle.com/business is the overview of every role your company is hiring for.

nav_entries.label: Candidates overview
nav_entries.title: Candidates overview
nav_entries.description: Track everyone in your funnel. The Candidates page brings every person across every job into one place.

nav_entries.label: Candidate stages
nav_entries.title: Candidate stages
nav_entries.description: Sourced through Offer, and everything after. Stages are the steps of your hiring process, and every candidate sits in exactly one of them per job.

nav_entries.label: Move candidates between stages
nav_entries.title: Move candidates between stages
nav_entries.description: Update progress. Moving someone forward or out takes a couple of clicks from anywhere you see them.

nav_entries.label: Notes and bookmarks on candidates
nav_entries.title: Notes and bookmarks on candidates
nav_entries.description: Keep hiring context. Notes keep interview impressions and decisions attached to the person instead of buried in someone's inbox.

nav_entries.label: Stage email templates
nav_entries.title: Stage email templates
nav_entries.description: Auto messages per stage. Write an email once per stage, and candidates hear from you the moment they move.

nav_entries.label: Offers
nav_entries.title: Offers
nav_entries.description: Send and track offers. The Offer stage is where you prepare, send, and follow up on an offer without losing track of who is waiting on what.

nav_entries.label: People Search for hiring
nav_entries.title: People Search for hiring
nav_entries.description: Temporarily unavailable. Public People Search is temporarily turned off. The opt-in directory is still too small to offer as a public product. You can still hire from your own applicants and imports.

nav_entries.label: Import candidates
nav_entries.title: Import candidates
nav_entries.description: Bring people in from elsewhere. Move people you are already talking to into Worklittle so your whole pipeline lives in one place.

nav_entries.label: AI tools and hiring compliance
nav_entries.title: AI tools and hiring compliance
nav_entries.description: What Worklittle Business does and does not decide when you use AI in recruiting, and what your organization remains responsible for. Worklittle Business includes AI that helps draft, organize, and summarize hiring work. It does not decide who to hire. Your organization remains the employer and controller of candidate decisions. This page is a practical map of that split so you can stay defensible under U.S. and EU rules that regulate automated employment tools.

nav_entries.label: Employees overview
nav_entries.title: Employees overview
nav_entries.description: Your team roster in one table you can sort, filter, and edit. **Employees** is the roster of everyone who works at your organization. It looks like a spreadsheet, but every cell saves for your whole team the moment you change it.

nav_entries.label: Employee profiles
nav_entries.title: Employee profiles
nav_entries.description: View and update one person's details, pay history, and documents. A profile is the full page for one person on your team. It gathers their contact details, role, pay history, and paperwork in one place.

nav_entries.label: Calendar and attendance
nav_entries.title: Calendar and attendance
nav_entries.description: Track shifts, time off, and who is present each day. **Calendar** shows who is working, who is out, and when. You can view the whole team side by side or zoom into one person.

nav_entries.label: Approve schedule changes
nav_entries.title: Approve schedule changes
nav_entries.description: Accept or deny time off and shift edits that need a manager. Some calendar changes wait for approval instead of applying right away. This keeps schedules accurate when people update their own availability.

nav_entries.label: Surveys overview
nav_entries.title: Surveys overview
nav_entries.description: Ask your team or candidates questions and collect answers in one table. **Surveys** let you ask a group of people a set of questions and read every answer in one place. Use them for onboarding checklists, engagement pulses, exit interviews, or candidate screening.

nav_entries.label: Create a survey
nav_entries.title: Create a survey
nav_entries.description: Build questions, set which ones are required, and save a draft. Building a survey works like filling out a short form builder. No setup or code is needed.

nav_entries.label: Invite people to a survey
nav_entries.title: Invite people to a survey
nav_entries.description: Who you can share a survey with and how the link works. Sharing controls two things at once. It decides who is allowed to open the survey and how they receive the link.

nav_entries.label: View survey responses
nav_entries.title: View survey responses
nav_entries.description: Read results, spot patterns, and export answers. Every answer lands in a results table where one row is one person's submission and one column is one question.

nav_entries.label: Documents overview
nav_entries.title: Documents overview
nav_entries.description: Keep HR files, policies, and templates in one place. **Documents** is where you write, store, and send the paperwork your team needs. Offer letters, handbooks, policies, and signed forms all live here.

nav_entries.label: Create and edit documents
nav_entries.title: Create and edit documents
nav_entries.description: Write policies, letters, and handbooks in the built-in editor. The document editor works like a familiar word processor. Type, format, and your work saves automatically.

nav_entries.label: Document templates
nav_entries.title: Document templates
nav_entries.description: Start from a ready-made HR document instead of a blank page. Templates give you a complete first draft so you only need to adjust the details that are specific to your company.

nav_entries.label: E-sign documents
nav_entries.title: E-sign documents
nav_entries.description: Send a document for signature and track who has signed. You can collect a signature on a document without printing anything. The signer opens a link, signs on screen, and you get the completed copy back.

nav_entries.label: HR notifications
nav_entries.title: HR notifications
nav_entries.description: The alerts you may get about people, schedules, and paperwork. Worklittle tells you when something needs attention so you do not have to keep checking every page.

nav_entries.label: Bulk employee actions
nav_entries.title: Bulk employee actions
nav_entries.description: Update, email, or export many people at once. When a change affects a whole department, you do not need to edit one row at a time. Select several people and act on all of them together.

nav_entries.label: Automations overview
nav_entries.title: Automations overview
nav_entries.description: Repeat your hiring and HR workflows without doing them by hand. An automation is a set of steps that runs on its own. Something happens, such as a new application arriving, and Worklittle does what you told it to do next.

nav_entries.label: Create an automation
nav_entries.title: Create an automation
nav_entries.description: Build your first workflow on the canvas, step by step. You do not need to write anything technical. You pick a starting event, then add the steps that follow.

nav_entries.label: Plugins and connectors
nav_entries.title: Plugins and connectors
nav_entries.description: Extend Worklittle Business with the tools your team already uses. Plugins connect Worklittle to other services so the assistant can act on your behalf in those tools.

nav_entries.label: Notify other tools when hiring changes
nav_entries.title: Notify other tools when hiring changes
nav_entries.description: Use webhooks or automations to send events out of Worklittle Business. You can push hiring events to other systems without buying seats or a separate integration SKU.

nav_entries.label: Connect our own MCP server
nav_entries.title: Connect our own MCP server
nav_entries.description: Add a Custom MCP app from Business Plugins. Besides the plugin catalog, you can connect your own remote MCP server as a Custom app.

nav_entries.label: API keys
nav_entries.title: API keys
nav_entries.description: Create a key when an app or an AI agent needs to connect to Worklittle. An API key is a long password that lets a program use Worklittle on your behalf. Most people never need one. You only need a key if a developer or an AI tool asks for it.

nav_entries.label: When to use the API vs the apps
nav_entries.title: When to use the API vs the apps
nav_entries.description: Who needs keys and who can just use the website. Worklittle has two front doors. Most people should walk through the app. The API is for building something custom. For a short tour first, see [What is the Worklittle API?](/help/api/what-is-worklittle-api).

nav_entries.label: Service status
nav_entries.title: Service status
nav_entries.description: Check whether Worklittle is having a problem. If something is not loading, the status page tells you whether the problem is on our side before you spend time debugging your own setup.

nav_entries.label: REST vs MCP in plain English
nav_entries.title: REST vs MCP in plain English
nav_entries.description: Two ways developers and AI tools connect to Worklittle. You may hear these two words from a developer or an AI tool. Here is what they mean without the jargon.

nav_entries.label: What is the Worklittle API?
nav_entries.title: What is the Worklittle API?
nav_entries.description: The programming door into Worklittle jobs, hiring, and MCP tools. The Worklittle API lets software and AI tools use the same jobs and hiring data you see in the apps. Most people never need it. You only need it when someone is building a custom integration.

nav_entries.label: Share or rotate an API key
nav_entries.title: Share or rotate an API key
nav_entries.description: Keep keys private, give each system its own key, and replace a key safely. An API key is like a password for your organization. Share it carefully, and replace it if it might have leaked.

nav_entries.label: Why is my API key not working?
nav_entries.title: Why is my API key not working?
nav_entries.description: Fixes for invalid key, wrong organization, revoked keys, and missing permissions. When a key fails, the problem is usually a typo, a revoked key, the wrong organization, or a missing permission. Work through the checklist below before assuming the API is down.

nav_entries.label: Which organization does my API key belong to?
nav_entries.title: Which organization does my API key belong to?
nav_entries.description: Keys and API bills follow the Business organization where the key was created. Every API key belongs to one organization. Usage and billing for that key go to that same organization, not to a different workspace you happen to have open later.

nav_entries.label: What can my API key do?
nav_entries.title: What can my API key do?
nav_entries.description: Scopes and roles in plain English: what a key is allowed to access. An API key can only do what it is allowed to do. In Worklittle, that usually follows the permissions of the person who created the key in that organization.

nav_entries.label: Too many requests and rate limits
nav_entries.title: Too many requests and rate limits
nav_entries.description: What a 429 means, the default per-key limit, and what to do next. A 429 or “too many requests” response means Worklittle asked your integration to slow down, or a free monthly quota was used up. It is a guardrail, not a permanent ban.

nav_entries.label: Common API errors
nav_entries.title: Common API errors
nav_entries.description: Plain-English meanings for 401, 402, 403, 429, and similar failures. API errors look technical, but most of them point to a simple fix: key, permission, billing, or speed.

nav_entries.label: How does API usage get billed?
nav_entries.title: How does API usage get billed?
nav_entries.description: Keys are free. AI token usage accrues to the organization wallet. Creating an API key does not cost money. Some API actions are free within monthly quotas. AI-powered actions add to amount owed on the organization that owns the key.

nav_entries.label: What is free on the API vs what costs money?
nav_entries.title: What is free on the API vs what costs money?
nav_entries.description: Free monthly quotas versus AI token charges, without the full pricing tables. A lot of API traffic is free within monthly quotas. Paid meters are AI token usage, plus $0.01 hosted apply submits on Jobs. This page points you to the right docs instead of reprinting every number.

nav_entries.label: REST, SDK, CLI, or MCP?
nav_entries.title: REST, SDK, CLI, or MCP?
nav_entries.description: Pick the right way in based on who is calling Worklittle. One Worklittle key works across the main ways in. The choice is about convenience, not a different account.

nav_entries.label: Connect an AI tool without writing code
nav_entries.title: Connect an AI tool without writing code
nav_entries.description: Use MCP or the Jobs app in ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code when you do not want a custom integration. You do not always need a developer. Some AI tools can connect to Worklittle through MCP or a built-in Jobs experience, including ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, and your own applications.

nav_entries.label: What are webhooks?
nav_entries.title: What are webhooks?
nav_entries.description: How Worklittle can notify another system when hiring events happen. A webhook is a message Worklittle sends to your other software when something important happens, such as a candidate moving stages. You only need webhooks if another system should react automatically.

nav_entries.label: How do I give a developer access?
nav_entries.title: How do I give a developer access?
nav_entries.description: Create a key, share it securely, send the right docs, and set a spend limit. You can stay non-technical and still unblock a developer. Create the key in the right organization, hand it over safely, and point them at the docs.

nav_entries.label: Why does the API feel slow?
nav_entries.title: Why does the API feel slow?
nav_entries.description: Practical checks for latency, retries, AI calls, and outages. Slow responses usually come from the integration pattern, AI-heavy calls, retries, or an incident, not from a secret speed setting you forgot to flip.

nav_entries.label: Prompt guides overview
nav_entries.title: Prompt guides overview
nav_entries.description: Ready-to-copy prompts for the Jobs app and Worklittle Business. A prompt is just what you type to the assistant. These guides give you wording that works, so you can paste it in and edit the details.

nav_entries.label: Jobs prompt guide
nav_entries.title: Jobs prompt guide
nav_entries.description: Prompts for searching jobs, improving your resume, and getting apply help. Copy any of these into chat at [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) and swap the bracketed parts for your own details.

nav_entries.label: Business prompt guide
nav_entries.title: Business prompt guide
nav_entries.description: Prompts for posting jobs, reviewing candidates, and running surveys. Paste these into chat at [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business). Replace the bracketed parts with your own details.

nav_entries.label: Chat feature prompts
nav_entries.title: Chat feature prompts
nav_entries.description: Prompts for headshots, whiteboards, and documents. Chat can do more than answer questions. These prompts trigger the built-in tools for images, drawing, and writing.

nav_entries.label: Apply with AI prompt tips
nav_entries.title: Apply with AI prompt tips
nav_entries.description: How to describe yourself so applications go through smoothly. Upload your resume, tap Apply, and Worklittle fills out and sends the application in a cloud browser in chat. You can watch and take control anytime. Looking first is only if you turn Always submit off.

nav_entries.label: Keep answers honest
nav_entries.title: Keep answers honest
nav_entries.description: Ask chat to stick to real job data instead of guessing. AI assistants can sound confident about things they do not know. A few words in your prompt push the assistant to use real Worklittle data and admit when it has none.

nav_entries.label: Privacy overview
nav_entries.title: Privacy overview
nav_entries.description: How we talk about your data in plain words. This is a plain-language summary of how your information is used in Worklittle. The full detail lives in the privacy policy.

nav_entries.label: Compliance and security
nav_entries.title: Compliance and security
nav_entries.description: How Worklittle protects accounts, company data, and everyday access. Worklittle is built so people and companies can trust what they put in the product. This page is the plain-language version of how we think about security and responsible use.

nav_entries.label: Contact support
nav_entries.title: Contact support
nav_entries.description: How to reach a human and what to include. Email is the fastest route to a real answer.

nav_entries.label: Terms and policies
nav_entries.title: Terms and policies
nav_entries.description: Links to the legal pages that govern your use of Worklittle. These are the official documents. They apply to everyone using Worklittle.

nav_entries.label: Chat reports
nav_entries.title: Chat reports
nav_entries.description: Report an AI answer that is unsafe, wrong, or inappropriate. If the assistant says something harmful or clearly incorrect, tell us. Reports are reviewed by the team.

nav_entries.label: Report a job
nav_entries.title: Report a job
nav_entries.description: Flag postings that look like scams, spam, or closed roles. Worklittle collects jobs from many sources. If one looks wrong, reporting it helps everyone who searches after you.

nav_entries.label: Safety tips for job seekers
nav_entries.title: Safety tips for job seekers
nav_entries.description: Spot job scams before they cost you money or data. Real employers do not ask for money. Almost every job scam breaks that one rule somewhere in the process.

nav_entries.label: Data you control
nav_entries.title: Data you control
nav_entries.description: Your profile, your preferences, and deleting your account. Most of what Worklittle knows about you is something you can see and change yourself.

nav_entries.label: Marketing and ads privacy
nav_entries.title: Marketing and ads privacy
nav_entries.description: How Marketing measurement and Personalized marketing work in Settings. Worklittle does not show a cookie popup. You control Google Analytics, Clarity, and ads from Privacy in Settings.

nav_entries.label: Where are Worklittle’s legal policies?
nav_entries.title: Where are Worklittle’s legal policies?
nav_entries.description: Links to Privacy, Terms, security, access controls, and retention. These are the official Worklittle legal and security documents. Help articles summarize them in plain language.

nav_entries.label: How do I request a copy of my data?
nav_entries.title: How do I request a copy of my data?
nav_entries.description: Consumer privacy email export vs Business JSON download. You can request a copy of your data from Settings. The steps differ slightly on worklittle.com and Worklittle Business.

nav_entries.label: Delete my account for privacy
nav_entries.title: Delete my account for privacy
nav_entries.description: How account deletion works, including the three-day window. Deleting your account removes your profile and associated personal data from Worklittle after a short grace period.

nav_entries.label: Privacy rights requests
nav_entries.title: Privacy rights requests
nav_entries.description: How GDPR/CCPA-style rights map to Settings and privacy@. Depending on where you live, privacy law may give you rights to access, correct, delete, or opt out of certain sharing. Worklittle describes these in the Privacy Policy.

nav_entries.label: Does Worklittle train models on my chats?
nav_entries.title: Does Worklittle train models on my chats?
nav_entries.description: No. Worklittle does not train its models on your chats. No. Worklittle does not train its models on your chats, voice, Apply with AI, or other AI messages.

nav_entries.label: Who do I email for privacy, support, or security?
nav_entries.title: Who do I email for privacy, support, or security?
nav_entries.description: Which inbox to use for privacy@, support@, and contact@. Different questions go to different addresses so the right team sees them.

nav_entries.label: How long is my data kept?
nav_entries.title: How long is my data kept?
nav_entries.description: How long account data and chat files stay, and how you can delete things yourself. Worklittle keeps your information while you use the product, and for as long as the law or our policies require. You can also delete many things yourself.

nav_entries.label: Report harmful AI or a bad job
nav_entries.title: Report harmful AI or a bad job
nav_entries.description: When to use chat reports vs job reports. Use Report in the app when an AI answer or a job posting looks harmful, fake, or wrong.

nav_entries.label: Is Worklittle HIPAA or FedRAMP certified?
nav_entries.title: Is Worklittle HIPAA or FedRAMP certified?
nav_entries.description: No. Worklittle does not claim HIPAA or FedRAMP certification. No. Worklittle does not claim HIPAA or FedRAMP certification, and Help does not present SOC 2 as a product badge either.

nav_entries.label: Put our company’s privacy policy on our job board
nav_entries.title: Put our company’s privacy policy on our job board
nav_entries.description: Link your own privacy and terms on a Worklittle Business public profile. Company organizations can publish their own privacy policy and terms links next to Worklittle’s policies on their public board.

nav_entries.label: What age can use Worklittle?
nav_entries.title: What age can use Worklittle?
nav_entries.description: You must be at least 13 (or 16 in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland). You must be at least 13. In the EEA, UK, or Switzerland you must be at least 16, or the lower online-services age where you live if the law sets one.

nav_entries.label: Can I trust AI answers on Worklittle?
nav_entries.title: Can I trust AI answers on Worklittle?
nav_entries.description: Chat drafts are for you to review. Apply with AI fills and sends applications from your resume. For chat, treat answers like a draft. For Apply with AI, Worklittle fills and sends real applications from your resume.

nav_entries.label: Is the Business demo real customer data?
nav_entries.title: Is the Business demo real customer data?
nav_entries.description: No. The demo uses sample data, not your real company. No. The Business demo uses sample data so you can click around. It is not your real company workspace.

nav_entries.label: Who is responsible for activity on my account?
nav_entries.title: Who is responsible for activity on my account?
nav_entries.description: You are responsible for activity under your login. Do not share codes or keys. Your Worklittle account is yours. You are responsible for activity that happens while signed in as you.

nav_entries.label: Browse the docs site
nav_entries.title: Browse the docs site
nav_entries.description: Pills at the top, sidebar on the left, search everywhere. This site holds several different sets of pages. The navigation is built so you can tell which one you are in.

nav_entries.label: Copy code blocks
nav_entries.title: Copy code blocks
nav_entries.description: Grab an example without selecting text by hand. Every code example on this site has a copy button, including the prompt templates in the prompt guides.

nav_entries.label: Copy a whole page
nav_entries.title: Copy a whole page
nav_entries.description: Share a full docs page with a teammate or an AI assistant. **Copy page** puts the entire page on your clipboard as plain text, which makes it easy to hand to someone else or paste into an AI assistant.

nav_entries.label: Docs chat
nav_entries.title: Docs chat
nav_entries.description: Ask questions without leaving the page you are reading. Docs chat answers questions about Worklittle using the documentation. You do not need to sign in to use it.

nav_entries.label: What's new
nav_entries.title: What's new
nav_entries.description: Release notes for every product update. The release notes page lists what changed and when, newest first, across the job search app, Worklittle Business, the API, and the docs.

nav_entries.label: Help Center vs API reference
nav_entries.title: Help Center vs API reference
nav_entries.description: Everyday help on one side, developer pages on the other. Both live on this site, and they are written for different readers. Picking the right one first saves time.

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: Pick the Worklittle integration pattern that matches what you are shipping: job discovery, apply automation, an embedded careers board, ATS sync, sourcing, or an agent that combines several of them. Every pattern on this page runs on the same base URL and the same sk-wl-api01 key. The differences are which scopes you …

pages.title: Worklittle MCP
pages.description: Install Worklittle MCP in Cursor, Claude, VS Code, and other clients. Full tool catalog and authentication.

pages.title: Worklittle MCP
pages.description: Install Worklittle MCP in Cursor, Claude, VS Code, and other clients. Full tool catalog and authentication.

pages.title: Job search assistant
pages.description: Build a search UI or conversational assistant on Worklittle's market-wide index: title search, commute search, filter, paginate with cursors, enrich with details and keywords, and stay inside monthly search quotas. Job search is free within monthly quotas. Still keep limit and caching intentional so agents do not burn…

# Overview

Pick the Worklittle integration pattern that matches what you are shipping: job discovery, apply automation, an embedded careers board, ATS sync, sourcing, or an agent that combines several of them.

Every pattern on this page runs on the same base URL and the same sk-wl-api01 key. The differences are which scopes you enable, which endpoints you call, and how much of the flow a model drives.

Worklittle is job discovery, auto-apply, swipe-to-apply style card UIs, and commute search on an interactive job map, over one API. **Jobs** is the market-wide index plus candidate-facing apply and document tools. **Business** is your own hiring workspace: postings, ATS pipeline, employees, HR docs, and webhooks. Most integrations sit squarely in one of them, and the interesting ones bridge both.

## Who these pages are for

| Audience | What you are usually building | Start with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Product engineers** | A job board, careers site, search UI, or candidate dashboard on top of Worklittle data | [Job search assistant](/use-cases/job-search-assistant), [Embedded job board](/use-cases/embedded-job-board) |
| **AI agent builders** | A copilot that searches, tailors documents, and applies on a user's behalf | [Agent Quickstart](/use-cases/agent-quickstart), [Agent patterns](/use-cases/agent-patterns) |
| **ATS integrators** | Two-way sync between Worklittle and an HRIS, CRM, or internal tool | [ATS automation](/use-cases/ats-automation), [Webhooks reliability](/use-cases/webhooks-reliability) |
| **Recruiting and GTM teams** | Pipeline automation, market sizing | [ATS automation](/use-cases/ats-automation), [Alerts and market data](/use-cases/alerts-and-market) |

If you are not sure which product tree you belong to, ask one question: does the data you need belong to **every employer** or **only your employer**? Market-wide is [Jobs](/jobs/get-started/overview). Employer-scoped is [Business](/business/get-started/overview).

## Pick a pattern

| You want to | Pattern | Core calls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Answer "what jobs match me?" | [Job search assistant](/use-cases/job-search-assistant) | `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/:id`, `search_jobs` |
| Commute search / interactive job map | [Interactive job map](/use-cases/interactive-job-map) | `GET /jobs/map`, `GET /companies` |
| Auto-apply (fill and send employer forms) | [Apply with AI](/use-cases/apply-with-ai) | `POST /v1/apply-with-ai`, `start_apply_with_ai` |
| Generate a tailored resume or cover letter | [Resumes and cover letters](/use-cases/resume-cover-letter) | `POST /v1/resumes`, `POST /v1/cover-letters` |
| Put a careers page on your own domain | [Embedded job board](/use-cases/embedded-job-board) | `GET /job-boards/:company/board` (no key) |
| Move candidates, add notes, schedule interviews | [ATS automation](/use-cases/ats-automation) | `/candidates`, `update_candidates`, webhooks |
| Run surveys, HR docs, and attendance from code | [Org operations](/use-cases/org-ops) | `/platform/surveys`, `/platform/documents`, `/attendance` |
| Chart the market | [Alerts and market data](/use-cases/alerts-and-market) | `GET /stats` |

## How the sections here are organized

The remaining pages are grouped by the kind of problem they solve, not by endpoint.

1. **Use cases** (this section) describe end-to-end product shapes with the calls in order.
2. **[Agent Quickstart](/use-cases/agent-quickstart)** is the install-and-route page for coding agents (Jobs and Business on one page). **[Agent patterns](/use-cases/agent-patterns)** cover architecture once a model is in the loop: REST versus MCP, tool sequencing, extraction, pagination, and conversation state.
3. **[Prompting](/use-cases/prompting)** gives system-prompt language you can paste and adapt, plus [grounding rules](/use-cases/grounding) that keep a model from inventing salaries.
4. **[Reliability](/use-cases/reliability)** is what you read before launch: backoff, closed jobs, webhook idempotency, and an [eval checklist](/use-cases/eval-checklist).
5. **Reference** holds the [glossary](/use-cases/glossary) and the [capability map](/use-cases/capability-map), which is the fastest way to go from a product goal to the exact endpoint.

## One key, two products

You do not need separate credentials per pattern. A single `sk-wl-api01-...` key created on [**API keys**](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys) works for REST at `https://api.worklittle.com` and MCP at `https://mcp.worklittle.com`. What changes between patterns is the **scope set**:

| Pattern | Scopes |
| --- | --- |
| Search and detail | `jobs:read` |
| Apply and Apply with AI | `jobs:apply` |
| Resumes and cover letters | `agent:tools` |
| Posting and ATS | `jobs:post`, `jobs:applications` |
| Event sync | `webhooks:manage` |

Grant the narrowest set that makes your integration work. A missing scope returns **403**, not a silent empty result, so failures are loud during development. Balance and per-route spend show up on [**Usage**](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) in the [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business).

| Doc | Why |
| --- | --- |
| [Search jobs](/jobs/api/search-jobs) | Filters, cursor pagination, detail fetch |
| [Apply for jobs](/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs) | Hosted apply, Apply with AI, public boards |
| [Worklittle MCP](/jobs/mcp) | Tool names, install, and auth |
| [Jobs pricing](/jobs/get-started/pricing) | What each call costs |

Business side: [Business overview](/business/get-started/overview), [Manage candidates](/business/api/manage-candidates), [Webhooks](/business/webhooks/overview).

## Tool catalog

- search_jobs: Search Worklittle's job listings by keyword, company, location, job type, seniority, or recency. Use for ANY industry (retail, finance, healthcare, tech, etc.). Search matches title and filter text (substring / FTS), not vector embeddings. Role / title text goes in query (+ optional keywords). The API matches job TITLE substrings only for that text — it does not mix company names into the same field. Preserve negative title terms with a leading dash, e.g. 'software…

- get_job_details: Fetch detailed information about a specific job, including full responsibilities, qualifications, and company details. Use this after search_jobs or get_recent_jobs when a user wants to know more about a particular job. Requires the job's ID from a previous search result.

- get_job_keywords: Get only the skill and technology keywords extracted from a job description — stripped of all narrative prose, responsibilities copy, and boilerplate clutter. Use this as the focused input when tailoring a resume or cover letter to a specific role: getting the full job description degrades resume/cover letter quality because the extra words are too confusing. These keywords are the distilled skill/tech surface area of the role. Also useful for skill-overlap assessment and…

- get_market_overview: Returns aggregate statistics about the current job market as indexed by Worklittle. Use this when a user asks broad questions like 'what jobs are available?', 'how many remote jobs are there?', 'which companies are hiring the most?', or 'what does the job market look like overall?'. Also useful for enterprise users who want hiring trend data or sourcing signals. No parameters required — just call it.

- create_resume: Create a hiring-manager-ready one-page resume (no placeholders). Uses only real facts from optional resume/profile/job context; omits unknowns. Optional formats: html, pdf (one-page pdf-lib), docx. Omit formats for default html+pdf. Alias format=html|pdf|docx. For a draft that may leave [] when details are missing, use create_draft_resume. Billed AI tokens only.

- create_cover_letter: Create a hiring-manager-ready one-page cover letter (no placeholders). Same formats/format options as create_resume (default html+pdf). For a draft that may leave [] when details are missing, use create_draft_cover_letter. Billed AI tokens only.

- create_draft_resume: Create a one-page draft resume: when details are missing, the model may leave [] markers such as [Company] instead of inventing facts. Same formats/format as create_resume (default html+pdf). For no-placeholder hiring-ready output, use create_resume.

- create_draft_cover_letter: Create a one-page draft cover letter: when details are missing, the model may leave [] markers instead of inventing experience. Same formats/format as create_cover_letter (default html+pdf). For no-placeholder output, use create_cover_letter.

- get_company: Read the company identity and canonical company profile for the caller's Worklittle platform account.

- set_company: Set or update the single company identity for the caller's Worklittle platform account. Requires a verified work email. Changing company identity closes existing public jobs.

- update_company_profile: Update canonical company metadata for the caller's verified company. The account email domain must match the company domain.

- list_company_organizations: List internal organizations or teams within the employer company, including hiring goals.

- set_company_organizations: Create or update an internal company organization or team with hiring goals.

- delete_company_organizations: Delete an internal company organization or team.

- list_posted_jobs: List jobs posted through Worklittle ATS for the caller's platform account.

- create_job_listing: Create a candidate-facing Worklittle ATS job listing.

- update_job_listing: Update a candidate-facing Worklittle ATS job listing.

- delete_job_listing: Close a Worklittle ATS job listing so it no longer accepts applications.

- create_job: Create an internal HR job. Set open_to_candidates true to make it candidate-facing.

- update_connected_email_prefs: Update connected account email notification prefs (job_alerts, local_events, announcements). Job Cards You overlay. Requires jobs:apply.

- remove_connected_profile_photo: Remove the connected account's uploaded profile photo and reset to a default avatar. Job Cards You overlay. Requires jobs:apply.

- start_apply_with_ai: Start an Apply-with-AI session for a job where apply_with_ai_eligible is true (AI tokens only; no flat browser fee). Personal API keys also open a watch-only worklittle.com chat for the key owner (chat_url with ?account=). Company keys do not create a consumer chat. Returns session_id and live_view_url. No per-user concurrent cap; when global browser slots are full the session is queued (Waiting). Always submit is on by default; pass auto_submit false to require…

Only status completed means the application was submitted — awaiting_submit means the form is ready (approve_apply_submit / Always submit), not success yet. - continue_apply: Continue an Apply-with-AI session with answers to stuck questions (HITL).

- stop_apply: Stop an Apply-with-AI Browser Run session.

The API matches job TITLE substrings only for that text — it does not mix company names into the same field. Preserve negative title terms with a leading dash, e.g. 'software…
