# Sign in with Google

The one-tap option, and what to do when the Google window misbehaves.

Google sign-in skips the code-in-your-inbox step entirely and is the quickest way into Worklittle.

## How to do it

On a desktop browser, Google may show a sign-in prompt in the top-right of [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) or [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) before you open the login panel. Pick an account to sign in. Closing that prompt hides it for a while.

You can always sign in from the panel:

1. Open **Log in or sign up** on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) or [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).
2. Tap **Continue with Google**.
3. Pick the Google account you want to use in the window that opens.
4. You are returned to Worklittle, already signed in.

If it is your first time, the account is created right then. There is no extra form.

## Why Gmail addresses are pointed at Google

If you type a gmail.com address into the email field, Worklittle asks you to **use Continue with Google for this email address** instead of sending a code.

Google already verifies that inbox better than an emailed code can, and it is faster for you. It is the same account either way.

## What Worklittle sees

Your email address, your name, and your profile photo. That is it.

Worklittle never receives your Google password and has no access to your Gmail, Drive, or calendar.

## Using a different Google account

The Google window shows every account signed in on that browser. Pick the one you want, or choose **Use another account** to sign in with one that is not listed.

If you want both a personal and a work account available in Worklittle at once, see [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts).

## If the Google window does not appear

Almost always a blocked popup. Look for a small blocked-popup icon at the right edge of your address bar and allow popups for worklittle.com, then try again.

Still nothing? Use the email code route in [Sign in with an email code](/help/account/email-code), or work through [Trouble signing in](/help/account/trouble-signing-in).

# Sign in with an email code

Get a six-digit code in your inbox and type it in. No password needed.

If you would rather not use Google or set a password, Worklittle can email you a short code each time you sign in.

## How to sign in with a code

1. On the **Log in or sign up** panel, type your address into **Email address** and press **Continue**.
2. Worklittle shows **Check your inbox** and sends a six-digit code.
3. Open the email, copy the six digits into the **Code** field, and press **Continue**.

On a phone your keyboard will usually offer the code above the keys so you can tap it in without switching apps.

## Codes expire after 15 minutes

Once a code is 15 minutes old it stops working and you will see **Code expired. Request a new code to log in**.

That is not a problem, just request another one. Codes are also single use, so the one from yesterday will not work today.

## Getting a new code

On the code screen, choose **Resend email** or **Send a new code**. The button briefly changes to **Email sent** to confirm.

Requesting several in a row is fine, but if you hammer it you will be asked to wait a minute before trying again. When more than one code has arrived, always use the newest email.

## If the code does not arrive

- Check your spam or junk folder, and the Promotions tab in Gmail
- Make sure the address you typed is the one you actually meant
- Give it a minute, since some corporate mail servers hold messages briefly
- Try again from a normal browser window if you are in private or incognito mode

Corporate email filters are the usual culprit. See [Work email vs personal email](/help/account/work-email-vs-personal) and [Trouble signing in](/help/account/trouble-signing-in).

## Tired of waiting on email?

You have two faster options. Set a password once and skip the inbox from then on, described in [Sign in with a password](/help/account/password-sign-in), or use [Sign in with Google](/help/account/sign-in-with-google) if your address supports it.

# Sign in with a password

Set a password once so you do not have to check your email every time.

A password is optional on Worklittle, but it makes signing in on a new device much quicker.

## Create a password

Sign in the usual way with an email code first. On the code screen, choose **Continue with password**, then **Create a password** and pick one.

Once it is set, the password works everywhere you sign in, on both [worklittle.com and worklittle.com/business](/help/getting-started/consumer-vs-business).

## Sign in with it

1. Enter your email and press **Continue**.
2. On the code screen, choose **Continue with password**.
3. Type your password and press **Continue**.

No inbox, no waiting. Let your browser or password manager save it and the whole thing becomes one tap.

## Switching between a password and a code

Setting a password does not turn off email codes. Both keep working, so pick whichever suits the moment.

On the code screen the link reads **Continue with password**. On the password screen it reads **Sign up with a one-time code** to send you back the other way. Signing in with Google also stays available.

## Choosing a good one

Long beats complicated. Three or four unrelated words are easier to remember and harder to guess than a short string of symbols.

Do not reuse a password from another site, and let your browser or a password manager generate and store it for you.

## If you forget it

Nothing is lost. Sign in with an email code as usual, which always works, then set a new password from the same **Continue with password** screen.

If the code is not arriving either, see [Trouble signing in](/help/account/trouble-signing-in).

# Switch between accounts

Keep up to three accounts signed in and move between them without logging out.

Worklittle can hold up to three signed-in accounts at once, which is handy if you keep personal and work life separate. This switches which email you are signed in as, not which company workspace you are in.

## Account switcher vs organization switcher

| Switcher | What it changes | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Switch accounts** | Which email/login you are | Up to **3** signed-in accounts on this device |
| **Switch organizations** | Personal vs company workspace inside one login | Every organization you belong to |

If you only need Personal ↔ company on the same email, use [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization) instead.

## Why you might want this

A few common cases:

- A personal email for job hunting on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) and a work email for hiring on [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business)
- A recruiter who keeps separate logins for different clients
- Two people sharing a laptop

Each account keeps its own saved jobs, chats, resume, organizations, and settings. Nothing is shared between them.

## Where to open it

- On [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com), open your account menu, then **Switch accounts**.
- On [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business), open your profile (the account row at the bottom of the left sidebar), then **Switch accounts**.
- You can also find **Switch accounts** under **Account** in settings on either surface (below **Manage billing** and **View usage** on worklittle.com).

## Add another account

Open **Switch accounts** and choose **Add account**.

You will get the normal **Log in or sign up** panel. Sign in with the second email as described in [Create an account](/help/account/create-account). The first account stays signed in the whole time.

## Switch between them

Open the same **Switch accounts** menu, where every signed-in email is listed, and tap the one you want. The switch is instant and no password or code is needed.

Your current account is marked in the list so you always know who you are acting as.

## The three account limit

Three is the maximum on each device. Trying to add a fourth shows **Log out of an account to continue** with a note that you have reached your limit of logged-in accounts.

Sign out of whichever one you use least, then add the new one. See [Sign out](/help/account/sign-out).

## Removing an account from the list

Switch to that account and sign out. It disappears from the switcher and the others stay untouched.

Signing out is not the same as deleting. The account and all its data are still there next time you sign in. See [Delete your account](/help/account/delete-account) if you actually want it gone.

# Manage linked emails

How email addresses relate to your account, your device, and your profile.

Worklittle uses email in three different ways, and knowing which is which clears up most confusion.

## One email signs in to one account

Your account is identified by the email you signed in with. There is no way to merge two accounts into one or to add a second sign-in address to an existing account.

If you sign in with a second address, that is a separate account with its own saved jobs, chats, and resume.

## Emails signed in on this device

A single browser can hold up to three signed-in accounts at once, listed under **Switch accounts** in your settings. That list is what most people mean by their linked emails.

It is per device, so signing in on your laptop does not add anything to the list on your phone. Full details in [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts).

## The work email on your profile

Separately from sign-in, your job seeker profile has a field for a work email. This is contact information that goes onto applications. It has nothing to do with how you log in and changing it will not change your sign-in address.

See [Work email vs personal email](/help/account/work-email-vs-personal) for which address belongs where.

## Changing the email on an account

An account's sign-in address cannot be edited. If you need to move to a new address, sign in with the new one to create an account there and set your profile up again.

Before you abandon the old account, export your data from settings so you keep a copy of what was in it. See [Delete your account](/help/account/delete-account) for where the export lives.

## Emails Worklittle sends you

Sign-in codes always go to the address you are signing in with.

Everything else, including job alerts, local events, and announcements, is controlled under **Emails** in your settings and requires being signed in. Turn any of them off there at any time.

# Work email vs personal email

Which address to sign in with, and where your work address belongs.

Short answer: sign in with a personal address if you are job hunting, and a work address if you are hiring.

## If you are looking for a job, use a personal address

Three good reasons.

- **Privacy.** Many companies can read employee mailboxes. A job search does not belong in one.
- **You keep the account.** When you change jobs, the work address disappears and the account attached to it becomes unreachable.
- **Delivery.** Corporate spam filters block sign-in codes far more often than personal ones do.

A Gmail address also gets you the one-tap [Sign in with Google](/help/account/sign-in-with-google) route.

## If you are hiring, use your work address

On [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) your account represents you inside your company, so a work address is the right choice. It is what teammates recognize when they invite you to the organization.

If your company uses Google Workspace, **Continue with Google** works with your work address the same way it does with a personal one.

## Where your work email goes on a job seeker profile

Your profile has its own field for a work email. That is contact information used on applications, kept separate from the address you sign in with.

You can sign in with a personal address and still list a work address there, or leave it blank. See [Manage linked emails](/help/account/linked-emails).

## Doing both at once

Plenty of people hire on one side and quietly look around on the other. Sign in with your work address for [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) and your personal address for the job seeker app, then move between them with [account switching](/help/account/switch-accounts).

Nothing you do in one account is visible from the other.

## If you already signed up with a work address

You can keep using it, but consider moving to a personal one before you leave that job, since sign-in codes go to the work inbox and you will lose access to it.

Sign-in addresses cannot be changed, so this means creating an account on the personal address. Export your data from settings first so you have a copy of what you built up.

# Sign out

How to sign out, and what stays behind on the device afterwards.

Signing out ends the session on that device and leaves everything in your account untouched.

## On worklittle.com

Open the **You** tab on a phone or your settings on a computer, then go to [worklittle.com/settings](https://worklittle.com/settings). In the **Account** section choose **Log out**.

A confirmation asks whether you are sure and shows which email you are logging out of, so you cannot sign out of the wrong account by accident.

## On worklittle.com/business

Open your settings from the profile area of the sidebar. **Log out** sits in the same group as **Export all data** and **Delete my account**.

## When several accounts are signed in

Signing out only affects the account you are currently using. Any others in the **Switch accounts** list stay signed in and you land on one of them.

To clear the device completely, sign out of each one in turn. See [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts).

## What stays on the device

Signing out does not wipe the browser. Some general browsing state, such as jobs you skipped, may remain locally and reappear as guest activity.

If you are on a shared computer and want nothing left behind, sign out and then clear that browser's site data for worklittle.com, or use a private window next time.

## Signing out is not deleting

Your account, saved jobs, pipeline, chats, and resume are all waiting when you sign back in. Nothing is removed.

If you want the account itself gone, see [Delete your account](/help/account/delete-account).

Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Delete your account

How to permanently delete your account, and the three-day window to change your mind.

Deleting removes your account and everything in it, with a short grace period in case you have second thoughts.

## Export your data first

In the same settings section as the delete button there is Export all data. Use it before you delete anything. It opens an email request to privacy@worklittle.com from your account address. See [Export your data](/help/account/export-my-data).

Your saved jobs, pipeline, profile, and chats are the sort of thing that is annoying to rebuild, and this is your chance to keep a copy.

## How to delete

1. Go to [worklittle.com/settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), or your settings on [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).
2. Find the **Account** section.
3. Choose **Delete my account**.
4. Confirm in the **Delete account** dialog.

You are signed out immediately and the account stops working.

## You have three days to change your mind

Deletion is not instant. If you sign in again with the same email within three days, the deletion is cancelled and your account comes back exactly as it was.

After three days it is permanent and there is nothing anyone can restore.

## What gets deleted

Your account details, chat history, saved jobs and pipeline, profile, and resume.

Applications you already submitted are a separate matter. Those went to the employer's own system and are not Worklittle's to delete, so contact the company directly if you want them removed.

## Consider signing out instead

If you just want to step away for a while, sign out and leave the account alone. There is no cost to keeping it and nothing happens while you are gone.

Only want fewer emails? Turn off job alerts under **Emails** in your settings and keep the account. See [Sign out](/help/account/sign-out).

Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Trouble signing in

Fixes for the problems that come up most often when logging in.

Most sign-in trouble comes down to a missing email, an expired code, or a blocked popup, and all three are quick to sort out.

## The code never arrives

Work through these in order.

1. Check spam or junk, and the Promotions tab if you use Gmail.
2. Confirm the address you typed. A typo sends the code somewhere you cannot read it.
3. Wait a full minute. Corporate mail servers sometimes hold messages.
4. Choose **Resend email** for a fresh code.
5. Try a personal address instead. Company filters block sign-in codes more often than personal inboxes do.

See [Sign in with an email code](/help/account/email-code) and [Work email vs personal email](/help/account/work-email-vs-personal).

## The code says it expired

Codes last 15 minutes and can only be used once. When you see **Code expired. Request a new code to log in**, just request another.

If several codes are sitting in your inbox, use the newest. Older ones stop working as soon as a new one is issued.

## You are asked to wait before trying again

Requesting codes very quickly in a row trips a short cooldown that protects inboxes from being flooded.

Wait about a minute and try once more. In the meantime, [Sign in with Google](/help/account/sign-in-with-google) is unaffected if your address supports it.

## The Google window does not open

This is a blocked popup nearly every time. Look for a blocked-popup icon at the right end of your address bar and allow popups for worklittle.com.

Also worth trying: disable a strict ad blocker for this site, or use a regular window instead of private browsing, which some browsers restrict. Otherwise fall back to the email code.

## You are signed in as the wrong person

More common than you would think on a shared computer or after using Google sign-in with the wrong profile selected.

Open **Switch accounts** in your settings and pick the right email, or sign out and back in. See [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts) and [Sign out](/help/account/sign-out).

## Nothing loads or the page looks broken

Refresh first. If that does not help, try a different browser or your phone to work out whether the problem is the site or that one browser.

An old extension or a very outdated browser version is the usual cause. Updating the browser fixes most of these.

## Still stuck

You do not need an account to browse. Keep swiping jobs at [worklittle.com/jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) as a guest and sign in when you want to save roles to your account.

See [Browsing as a guest vs signing in](/help/getting-started/guest-vs-signed-in).

# AI usage limits

How much free AI you get, and what to do when you need more.

Browsing and saving jobs are free. Chat, Apply with AI, resumes, and similar AI help use a free monthly AI amount. When that runs out, you can add Instant or keep going with a card.

## What uses free AI

These use your free monthly AI amount:

- Chat
- Apply with AI
- Resume help, cover letters, voice, and dictation

Looking through jobs, saving them, using Maps, and moving cards on Saved do not.

## How much free AI you get

- **Not logged in.** Limited guest AI. When it runs out, Send opens **Log in for higher usage** (not the generic **Log in or sign up** heading). Sign in for the signed-in free monthly amount and the API.
- **Signed in.** A free monthly AI amount on Personal ($0.50). Company organizations on [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business) get **$0.10** of free monthly AI credit. When it runs out, open [Plans](https://worklittle.com/plans) or add a card on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).
- **Instant.** $20 of AI credit each month you stay subscribed. See [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).

Your chats, saved jobs, and resume stay either way.

## Ways to keep going

- Subscribe to [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).
- Or add a card on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) for pay as you go.

If you run out of free AI on worklittle.com and you do not have Instant, we send an announcement email about two minutes later with **Upgrade to Instant**. Company organizations do not get this email. Turn it off from Manage alerts or Unsubscribe.

More detail: [Free AI, Instant, and pay as you go](/help/account/free-instant-payg) and [Pricing basics](/help/account/pricing-help).

## When it resets

Free monthly AI resets at the start of your next calendar month. Unused free AI does not roll over.

Instant’s $20 credit refreshes once per month while Instant is active. Canceling and signing up again in the same month does not give you another $20.

If you had used up that monthly amount, Usage on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) shows **Usage limit reset** when the new month’s credit is granted. About an hour later we send an announcement email. Referral gifts and other credit are not this email.

# Chat basics

Start conversations and get career help.

Chat is your free career assistant on worklittle.com, ready to answer questions, rewrite your resume, and walk you through a job search.

## Start your first chat

1. Go to [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com).
2. Type a question in the message box at the bottom of the screen.
3. Press **Enter** (or tap the arrow button on your phone) to send.

You do not need an account to try it. Signing in keeps your history, so your chats are waiting for you on your next visit and on your other devices.

## What you can ask for

Chat is built around real job hunting tasks, not just trivia. A few things people ask every day:

- **Resume help.** "Rewrite my resume for a customer service role."
- **Interview prep.** "Ask me five questions a nurse manager would ask."
- **Career quiz.** "Give me a career quiz" or "quiz me for a store manager interview."
- **Job research.** "What does a claims adjuster actually do all day?"
- **Outreach.** "Write a short message to a recruiter about this posting."
- **Money questions.** "Is $24 an hour reasonable for a warehouse lead in Ohio?"

You can paste a job posting straight into the message box and ask chat to tailor your materials to it.

## Keep the conversation going

Chat remembers what you said earlier in the same conversation, so you can refine instead of starting over. Try follow-ups like "make it shorter," "sound less formal," or "now write the cover letter version."

When you want a clean slate, start a new chat instead of switching topics mid-conversation. See [Chats and threads](/help/chat-ai/chat-threads) for how to find and reopen older conversations.

## Where to go next

- [Tips for better answers](/help/chat-ai/chat-tips) for getting more useful replies on the first try.
- [Create or edit a resume in chat](/help/chat-ai/resumes-from-chat) to turn a conversation into a finished document.
- [Swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck) when you are ready to start applying.

# Chats and threads

Find, rename, pin, share, and continue past conversations.

Every conversation you have is saved as its own chat, so you can come back days later and pick up exactly where you left off.

## Find an older chat

Chats are listed under **Recents** in the sidebar. Newest activity is near the top. Pinned chats stay above the rest. Apply with AI chats that need your attention float to the top with an orange indicator, and unread chats float above quieter ones until you open them. Opening a chat clears those dots and they stay cleared after a reload until something new needs you (for example a later Finish application step, or a new reply).

1. Open the sidebar using the menu button in the top left.
2. Scroll the list, or use search to look for a word you remember using.
3. Select a chat to reopen the full conversation.

On a phone, the sidebar slides in from the left. Swipe it away or tap outside it to close.

Job seeker chats live on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). Business chats live on [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business). The two lists never mix - a work chat will not show in the job seeker sidebar, and the other way around.

## How chats get their names

Most chats get a short emoji title from your first message after that reply finishes, so "Help me apply to the Delta ramp agent job" is easy to spot later. If the first reply searches jobs and shows listings, the name switches to a search emoji plus your query as soon as a job card appears (for example **🔍 marketing**), without waiting for the rest of the reply. That works while you are a guest too. The title stays in this browser until you sign in. Apply with AI chats keep names like **AI Apply** or **Apply with AI** plus the company and role, and only get an emoji added.

To rename:

1. Open the menu (⋯) next to the chat in the sidebar, or open the chat menu in the toolbar.
2. Choose **Rename**.
3. Enter a clearer title and save.

Clear titles make a long list much faster to scan.

## Pin important chats

Pin a chat so it stays at the top of your sidebar while you keep working on it.

1. Open the menu (⋯) next to the chat.
2. Choose **Pin**. Choose **Unpin** when you no longer need it pinned.

Pinned chats sync with your account when you are signed in.

## Share a chat

You can copy a link to a conversation from the chat menu or from **Share** on a message.

| Surface | Who can open the link | Link shape | How long it lasts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Job seeker ([worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com)) | Anyone with the link | `worklittle.com/chat/...` | About 48 hours |
| Business ([worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business)) | People in your organization | `worklittle.com/business/chat/...` | About 48 hours |

Sharing refreshes the expiry window. After it expires, create a new share link from the same menu if you still need it.

Only share chats you are comfortable others seeing. Need to flag a bad response instead? See [Report a chat](/help/chat-ai/report-chat).

## Continue, start fresh, or clean up

- **Continue** an old chat when the new question builds on it, like revising a resume you already worked on.
- **Start a new chat** when the topic changes. Answers stay sharper when a conversation stays on one subject.
- **Delete** chats you no longer need from the menu next to a chat in the sidebar. Deleting is permanent, so export anything you want to keep first.

Signed-in chats sync across your devices. If you were browsing as a guest, your history lives only in that browser. See [Saving jobs as a guest](/help/finding-jobs/guest-saves) for how guest data behaves.

# Photos, files, and video in chat

Attach media to your messages.

You can send photos, documents, and short videos to chat so it can read them and respond to what is actually in front of you.

## Attach something

1. Select the paperclip or plus button next to the message box.
2. Choose a file from your device, or take a photo on your phone.
3. Add a sentence explaining what you want, then send.

You can also drag a file onto the chat window on a computer, or paste a screenshot straight from your clipboard.

## What to send and what to ask

| You attach | Try asking |
| --- | --- |
| Your resume as a PDF | "Rewrite this for a dental assistant role." |
| A screenshot of a job posting | "What are the three must-have requirements here?" |
| A photo of a paper job flyer | "Turn this into a job I can search for online." |
| A short video walkthrough | "What is going wrong in this process?" |

Attaching your resume once at the start of a conversation saves a lot of retyping later.

## Good to know

- Attachments stay with the chat, so reopening the conversation later brings them back.
- Large files may take a moment to upload on a slow connection. Wait for the thumbnail to appear before sending.
- Limits: about 10 MB per file, up to 10 files per message, about 1 GiB storage when signed in, about 90 days retention. Details: [Attachment size and storage limits](/help/chat-ai/attachment-limits).
- Only attach documents you are comfortable storing in your account. Redact anything sensitive, like a full Social Security number, before uploading.
- Need to flag something that went wrong with a response? See [Report a chat](/help/chat-ai/report-chat).

# Voice dictation

Speak instead of type.

Dictation lets you talk to chat instead of typing, which is handy on a phone, in the car park before an interview, or any time typing is slow.

## Start dictating

1. Select the microphone button next to the message box.
2. Allow microphone access the first time your browser asks.
3. Speak normally. Each take stops automatically after about **3 minutes** and the transcript is added to the message box. Tap the microphone again if you want to keep going.
4. Or tap the check to stop early, review the text, then send.

Nothing is sent until you press send, so you always get a chance to fix a word first.

The same microphone on [About](https://worklittle.com/about), [Research](https://worklittle.com/research), and research articles transcribes into that search box. Send still opens chat on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com).

## Get cleaner results

- Speak at a normal pace in complete sentences rather than short bursts.
- Say punctuation out loud when you need it, for example "period" or "new line."
- Reduce background noise where you can. Wind and music are the usual culprits.
- Spell out unusual company names, then fix the spelling in the box before sending.

For longer stories, use a few 3-minute takes back to back. Talking through your last job is often faster than typing it, and chat can shape it into resume bullet points afterwards.

## If the microphone will not start

- Check that your browser has permission to use the microphone. On most browsers this is in the padlock or settings icon in the address bar.
- On a phone, close other apps that may be holding the microphone, such as a call or voice recorder.
- Try a different browser if the button stays greyed out.

Dictation is a convenience, not a requirement. Typing works exactly the same way.

Want a live spoken conversation instead of text in the box? See [Connect with AI (voice)](/help/chat-ai/connect-with-ai).

# Slash skills menu

Shortcuts for common AI actions.

Typing a forward slash in the message box opens a menu of ready-made skills, so you can trigger a common task without writing out a long request.

## Open the menu

1. Select the message box.
2. Type **/** as the first character.
3. A list of skills appears above the box.
4. Keep typing to filter, then use the arrow keys or a tap to pick one.

Press **Escape** to close the menu and go back to normal typing.

## What skills do

A skill is a shortcut that tells chat exactly how to handle a common job search task, so you get a consistent result every time. Typical examples include writing a resume, drafting a cover letter, preparing interview answers, and summarising a job posting.

After you pick a skill, add your own details on the same line. "/cover-letter for the barista job at Blue Bottle downtown" gives a far better result than the skill on its own.

## When to skip the menu

Skills are a head start, not a limit. If nothing in the list matches what you need, just describe the task in plain language. Chat handles open-ended requests the same way.

Related reading: [Tips for better answers](/help/chat-ai/chat-tips) and [Create or edit a resume in chat](/help/chat-ai/resumes-from-chat).

# Memories and favorites

What Worklittle remembers about you.

Memories are the details Worklittle keeps between conversations, like the roles you want and the city you are searching in, so you stop repeating yourself.

## What gets remembered

When something looks like a lasting fact about your search, it can be saved as a memory. Common examples:

- The job titles you are aiming for.
- Where you want to work, and whether remote is fine.
- Your years of experience and key skills.
- Preferences about tone, like "keep my writing casual."

Memories apply across your chats. Ask for a cover letter in a brand new conversation and it already knows your target role.

## Add, change, or remove a memory

1. Tell chat directly. "Remember that I only want night shifts" adds a memory.
2. To correct one, say what changed. "I moved to Austin, update my location."
3. To clear one, ask chat to forget it, or remove it from your settings.

Reviewing your memories every month or so is worth the minute it takes. Stale details, like an old target salary, quietly shape every answer you get.

## Your favorite things

In [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), Your favorite things is where personal facts and preferences live (the same memories chat can save). Edit or remove bullets there when something changes.

Pin important chats from the sidebar if you want them at the top of the list. That is separate from memories. For saving jobs, see [Heart and save a job](/help/finding-jobs/heart-save).

# Create or edit a resume in chat

Build application materials with AI.

Chat can build a complete resume from a conversation, or take the resume you already have and sharpen it for a specific job.

## Create resume from a job

On a job page, tap **Create resume**. If you have not uploaded a resume yet, the same upload window as [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/resume-gate) appears. Upload successfully once, and Create resume continues automatically with a tailored document for that role.

You can also open [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) or any job detail, then use Create resume from there.

## Start from what you already have

1. Attach your current resume to a chat message. See [Photos, files, and video in chat](/help/chat-ai/attachments).
2. Paste the job posting you are targeting, or its link.
3. Ask for what you want, for example "rewrite this resume for that posting and keep it to one page."

Chat pulls your history out of the file so you are editing rather than starting from a blank page.

## Start from scratch

No resume yet? Answer the questions chat asks, in whatever order you like:

1. Your most recent job, employer, and rough dates.
2. What you actually did day to day, in your own words.
3. Anything you improved, sped up, saved, or sold.
4. Schools, certificates, or licences.

Plain speech is fine. "I ran the register and trained the two new people" becomes a proper resume bullet point.

## Refine and export

Ask for changes one at a time so you can see the effect:

- "Cut this to one page."
- "Use stronger verbs in the second job."
- "Add numbers where you can, and mark anything you guessed."

When it looks right, open it as a document to format, download, or print. See [Documents in chat](/help/chat-ai/docs-in-chat).

Always read the final version yourself. You know your history best, and hiring managers can tell when nobody proofread.

# Cover letters from chat

Draft tailored cover letters.

Chat writes cover letters that reference the actual posting, so each application reads like it was written for that employer rather than copied from a template.

## Write one in three steps

1. Paste the job posting, or its link, into chat.
2. Attach your resume so the letter matches your real history.
3. Ask for the letter: "Write a short cover letter for this role, friendly but professional."

If you already discussed the job earlier in the same conversation, you can skip straight to step three.

## Make it sound like you

The first draft is a starting point. Push it closer to your voice with follow-ups:

- "Shorter. Three paragraphs maximum."
- "Less corporate, more like how I actually talk."
- "Open with why I want to work at this specific company."
- "Mention that I am switching from retail into healthcare."

Adding one honest, specific detail, like a shift you covered or a problem you fixed, does more than any amount of polish.

## Before you send

- Check the company name and role title appear correctly and are spelled right.
- Remove any claim you cannot back up in an interview.
- Drafts skip a "Dear Hiring Manager" greeting and lead with the role, company, and proof from your resume. If the posting asked for a named contact, add that in a follow-up.
- Save the final version as a document so you can reuse the structure next time. See [Documents in chat](/help/chat-ai/docs-in-chat).

Pair the letter with a tailored resume from [Create or edit a resume in chat](/help/chat-ai/resumes-from-chat).

# AI headshots

Create a professional photo for applications.

AI headshots turn an ordinary photo of you into a clean, professional-looking portrait you can use on applications and profiles.

## Create a headshot

1. Attach a clear photo of yourself to a chat message.
2. Ask for a headshot, and say what you want: "Make this a professional headshot with a plain background."
3. Review the result, then ask for adjustments such as a different background or a more casual look.
4. Download the version you like.

Attaching a photo and asking what it is gets a description. Chat only makes a headshot when you ask for one.

Guests get 2 headshots per device per day. See [Headshot limits](/help/chat-ai/headshot-limits).

## Pick a good source photo

The starting photo matters more than the instructions. Look for:

- Your face clearly visible, facing roughly forward.
- Even lighting, ideally near a window. Avoid harsh shadows.
- No sunglasses, hats, or heavy filters.
- Just you in frame, not a cropped group photo.

A recent phone selfie in daylight usually beats an old photo from an event.

## Using it well

A headshot helps most on profiles and networking sites. Many employers do not want a photo on the resume itself, and in some places including one can work against you, so check what is normal for your industry and country.

Keep it recognisable. The point is to look like a well-photographed version of yourself, not a different person.

# Whiteboards

Draw diagrams and brainstorm visually.

A whiteboard is a blank canvas inside chat where you can sketch, map out ideas, and think through something visually instead of in paragraphs.

## Open a whiteboard

1. Ask chat for a whiteboard, or pick it from the create menu.
2. A canvas opens beside your conversation.
3. Draw, add text boxes, and move things around.
4. Close it when you are done. You have one shared whiteboard to come back to, not a separate board for every chat. See [How whiteboards are saved](/help/chat-ai/one-whiteboard).

## What people use it for

- Career mapping. Lay out where you are now and the roles between here and the job you want.
- Interview prep. Sketch the process you are about to be asked to explain.
- Comparing options. Put two offers side by side and list what matters.
- Planning your week. Block out applications, follow-ups, and interviews.

You can ask chat about what is on the board. Describe your sketch and ask for gaps you may have missed.

## Tips

- Start rough. A messy board you can rearrange beats a tidy list you never revisit.
- Clear or rearrange the canvas when you switch topics so it stays readable.
- Take a screenshot before a big rearrangement if you might want the old layout back.

# Documents in chat

Create and edit docs from conversation.

Documents give your resume, cover letter, or notes a proper editable page inside Worklittle, so you can format, download, and share them.

## Turn a chat answer into a document

1. Ask for something written, such as a resume or a letter.
2. Open it as a document from the option shown with the answer.
3. The document opens in an editor beside your chat.

Anything long enough to print is usually better as a document than as a chat message.

## Edit and format

Inside the editor you can:

- Type and edit directly, like any word processor.
- Apply headings, bold, italics, and bullet lists.
- Reorder sections by cutting and pasting.
- Keep asking chat for changes while the document is open.

Edits save as you go, so there is no save button to remember.

## Download, print, or share

Use the document toolbar to download a copy or print it. A PDF is the safest format to send to an employer because it looks the same on every device.

Give each document a clear name, like "Resume - warehouse - March," so the right version is easy to find later. Lasting preferences about your search live in [Memories and favorites](/help/chat-ai/memories).

Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Report a chat

Flag something that feels wrong.

If a response is harmful, wrong in a way that matters, or just plain strange, you can report a concern so the team can look into it. You can do this while signed out.

## How to report

1. Open the chat containing the response.
2. Open the chat menu, usually shown as three dots near the top of the conversation.
3. Choose **Report**.
4. In **Report a concern**, pick the reason that fits best (including **Not relevant to me**).
5. Submit.

You will not get a reply to every report, but every one is read.

## What is worth reporting

- Advice that could hurt someone, or that encourages something unsafe.
- Confident answers that are factually wrong about pay, rights, or a legal process.
- Offensive, biased, or discriminatory language.
- Anything that looks like a scam or asks you for money or sensitive details.

Small annoyances, like an answer being too long, are better handled by simply asking for a shorter version.

## Stay safe in the meantime

Treat chat as a well-read helper, not a lawyer, doctor, or accountant. For decisions with money or legal consequences, check with a qualified person.

Never send payment or bank details to an employer you have not verified. If a posting asks for that, report the job as well. See [When a job is closed](/help/finding-jobs/closed-jobs) for how listings get removed.
page_text./help/chat-ai/chat-tips:
Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Tips for better answers

How to ask so chat helps faster.

A few small habits make a big difference in how useful chat is, and most of them come down to giving it your real situation instead of a generic question.

## Say who you are and what you want

Compare these two requests:

- "Write a cover letter."
- "I have three years in retail, I am applying to be a receptionist at a dental clinic, and I want a warm three paragraph cover letter."

The second gets a usable draft on the first try. Include your experience level, the role, and the tone you want.

## Give it the real material

- Paste the actual job posting rather than describing it.
- Attach your real resume instead of summarising it.
- Share the exact email you received when you want help replying.

Chat can only work with what it can see. See [Photos, files, and video in chat](/help/chat-ai/attachments) for how to attach things.

## Ask for the format you need

Say how you want the answer shaped: a bullet list, a table, five options, under 100 words, or ready to paste into an email. It is faster than reshaping a long paragraph afterwards.

If you want choices, ask for them. "Give me three different opening lines" beats getting one and asking again.

## Iterate instead of restarting

When an answer is close but not right, say exactly what to change rather than rewriting your question from scratch. "Keep the second paragraph, redo the first, and cut the closing" gets you there in one step.

Start a new chat only when the topic genuinely changes. See [Chats and threads](/help/chat-ai/chat-threads).

Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Swipe to apply

Find roles one card at a time, then hand them to Apply with AI to submit for you.

The Jobs tab shows one role at a time so you can move through openings quickly, pass on what does not fit, and start an application without leaving the card. The public walkthrough is [Tinder for Jobs](https://worklittle.com/tinder-for-jobs).

## How the cards work

Open [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs). Each card is one job: the title, the company, the location, and whatever else we know, such as pay and how recently it was posted.

- **Skip** takes the role out of your browsing.
- **Apply** means Apply with AI. Worklittle fills and sends the form for you. Open Chat if you want to watch.
- **Heart** saves it for later without removing it from the deck.
- Select the card to read the full posting. While you still have AI credit, Worklittle can write a structured summary. After you run out, you still see the employer's original description.

Roles you have already moved into In progress, Applied, Interview, Offer, Rejected, Withdrawn, or Skipped on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) stay off the deck (and the homepage). A heart alone does not.

On a phone you can swipe. On a computer, use the buttons. See [What is Apply with AI?](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai).

## Apply on a card

On a card, **Apply** means Worklittle fills and sends the form for you. Leave **Always submit** on unless you want to review before it sends. Apply with AI works on **more than 3 million** open jobs.

## Get better roles in front of you

What you see is shaped by what you tell us and what you do with the cards.

1. Set **Job title** in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings). That is the role you want next, and it takes more than one, separated by commas. You can also rule titles out with a minus sign. See [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field).
2. Skip the roles that are clearly wrong instead of scrolling past them.
3. Heart the ones you like even when you are not ready to apply.

There is no separate location box in Settings. While you are signed out with no job title, [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) and the [home page](https://worklittle.com/) show a mix of recent roles from your US state, or from your country outside the US, not the nearby 50 to 250 km ladder. On the home page, choose **Distance** (or Newest or Salary) when you want nearby cards. After you sign in, or after you set a [Job title](https://worklittle.com/settings), cards follow that title and location. Worklittle does not ask for location permission on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs). To grant or refresh precise location, open [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) and use current location.

## When you run out of cards

The deck keeps the next page of jobs loading in the background so you can skip quickly without staring at a spinner. Roles you already skipped or applied to are dropped on your device from those pages, then the next page loads. When the deck says **You're caught up. Try changing your job title.**, you have seen everything matching what you are looking for right now. Tap that message to open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and update **Job title**, or come back later since new roles arrive throughout the day.

Nearby cards mix different employers when enough companies are hiring in range. A company that just posted many roles at once will not fill the whole stack when other employers are in that same recency window.

You can also browse a different way with [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) or [Search jobs, companies, and chats](/help/finding-jobs/global-search).

# Tinder for Jobs

Find one job at a time, then Apply with AI.

Tinder for Jobs is how you find jobs on Worklittle. You see one job at a time, skip what does not fit, save what you like, and tap Apply so Apply with AI does the application from your resume.

## Start on Worklittle

Go to [Worklittle](https://worklittle.com), or read the public page at [Tinder for Jobs](https://worklittle.com/tinder-for-jobs).

Swipe the job, or tap **Skip** or **Apply**.

## What you can do

- **Skip** takes that job out of what you see next. The employer never sees it. You can still find it later under Skipped on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).
- **Apply** starts [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) on more than 3 million jobs.
- **Save** keeps it on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).
- Tap the job to read the full posting.

More detail: [Swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck) and [Tinder for Jobs vs other swipe to apply apps](/help/finding-jobs/tinder-for-jobs-vs-other-swipe-apps).

## Get jobs that fit

Change your job title in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) to your dream role. Use commas for more than one title, and a minus sign to rule a title out.

Jobs on the home page and [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) follow your US state (or your country outside the US) while you are signed out with no job title. Choose **Distance** on the home page when you want nearby cards. After you sign in, jobs follow your location from [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) or an approximate network location. Worklittle does not ask for location permission until you use Maps.

## Same jobs in ChatGPT and Claude

Ask ChatGPT or Claude to find jobs on Worklittle and you get the same jobs, Maps, and Saved list. See [Worklittle in ChatGPT and Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app).

# Job detail pages

Read the full posting.

The job detail page is the full picture of a role: the complete description, the pay if it is listed, the location, and the buttons to save or apply.

## What you will find

| Section | What it tells you |
| --- | --- |
| Summary | A short plain-English overview of the role |
| Description | The employer's full posting text |
| Location | Where the work happens, including remote roles |
| Pay | The salary or hourly range when the employer shares it |
| Company | Who is hiring, with a link to their page |

If pay is missing, the employer did not publish it. That is common and does not mean anything is wrong with the listing.

## Links to a job

A job has two shareable addresses.

| Link | What opens |
| --- | --- |
| [worklittle.com/jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) plus the job id, for example `/jobs/abc` | The [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) swipe deck with that card on top |
| `/job/abc` | The same posting on the home page |

Share from Jobs and you get the `/jobs/…` link. Share from home and you get `/job/…`. Both load the card you already had, without waiting for the rest of the feed.

Search engines only index a recent subset of job URLs (listed in the [sitemap](https://worklittle.com/sitemap.xml)). The swipe board at [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) is not indexed. Agents can request `Accept: text/markdown` or append `.md` to a job URL to read the original posting text.

## What you can do from here

- **Apply with AI** to have Worklittle fill out and send the employer's form for you (cloud browser in chat; take control anytime). See [Which jobs support Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/eligibility).
- **Heart** to save the role for later. See [Heart and save a job](/help/finding-jobs/heart-save).
- **Share** to send the posting to someone else. This copies the job link. When your device allows it, the system share sheet opens too. In [ChatGPT or Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app) the sheet is often blocked, so you get the copied link without leaving the card.
- **Ask chat about it** to get the requirements summarised or a tailored cover letter.

From a job card, use [quick actions](/help/finding-jobs/quick-actions) to save, share, find similar roles, or open the original listing. On this page, hold the title or meta row for the same menu. Select and copy the description freely. With the posting open, Cmd/Ctrl+A selects just this panel (not the rest of the app), unless you are typing in chat - then it selects the composer as usual.

Copying the description into chat and asking "am I qualified for this?" is a fast way to decide whether to spend time applying.

## Reading a posting well

- Separate the must-haves from the wish list. Most postings mix them together.
- Look for the working pattern: shifts, weekends, travel, on-site days.
- Note anything you would need to arrange, like a licence or a certificate.

You rarely need every listed requirement. If you meet most of the must-haves, applying is usually worth it.

Save, share, find similar roles, or open the original listing without opening the full job page.

Works on home, [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs), chat results, [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps), search, and company pages. | **Find similar** | Sends that job into chat and opens the chat (even if you were on Maps, Jobs, or another page). |

You do not need to open the full job page first.

# Heart and save a job

Keep roles you like.

The heart button saves a job to your Saved list so you can come back to it, compare it with others, and track it through to an offer.

## Save a job

Select the heart icon on a job detail page, or open [quick actions](/help/finding-jobs/quick-actions) on any job card and choose **Save**. The heart fills right away. Select it again, or choose **Saved** from the menu, to remove the job. If the save cannot reach your account (for example in [ChatGPT or Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app) when Connect fails), the heart empties again after a few seconds.

You can save from a job card, from search results, from Maps, and from a company page. Everything lands in the same place.

## Where saved jobs go

Saved roles appear on your [Saved board](https://worklittle.com/saved), which doubles as a pipeline from first interest through to an offer. Open it from the sidebar, or go straight there.

From there you can move a role along as things progress, add it to a stage, and see everything you have in flight at once. See [Saved jobs overview](/help/saved-jobs/overview).

Hearting a role keeps it on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) and the homepage until you skip it or move it into a later stage such as In progress or Applied.

## Saving without an account

Saving and the [Saved board](https://worklittle.com/saved) need an account. If you are signed out, the heart, **Save** in [quick actions](/help/finding-jobs/quick-actions), and **Saved** in the sidebar open sign in instead of writing a guest list.

Once you are signed in, every save lives on your account and shows up on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) on any device you use. See [Saving jobs as a guest](/help/finding-jobs/guest-saves).

# Skip vs Apply

What each button on a job card does.

Skip and Apply are the two buttons on every job card, and they do quite different things.

## Skip

Skip takes the role out of your browsing. You will not keep bumping into it as you go.

Nothing about a skip reaches the employer. They never find out. It is only a signal for what we show you next.

Skips are also recoverable. Every one lands in the **Skipped** column on your [Saved board](https://worklittle.com/saved), so a role you passed on a second too early is easy to get back. See [Skipped jobs](/help/saved-jobs/skipped-jobs).

In [ChatGPT or Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app), Skip keeps your place in the deck if you reload. When your Worklittle account is connected there, skips also land in the same **Skipped** column.

## Apply

Apply on a card starts **Apply with AI** for that role. Worklittle opens the company's real application in a cloud browser in chat, fills it from your resume, and sends it. You can watch and take control anytime.

Apply with AI works on **more than 3 million** open jobs. See [Which jobs support Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/eligibility).

A few jobs posted directly on Worklittle show **Easy apply** on the job page once the in-product form is ready. Until then the button says **Apply**. That form stays on the posting itself, separate from the Apply button on a card.

Either way, have a current resume on file first. See [Resume required before applying](/help/apply-with-ai/resume-gate). [Create or edit a resume in chat](/help/chat-ai/resumes-from-chat) can sort one out in a few minutes.

In [ChatGPT or Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app) you can search and skip without signing in. **Apply** is when you may be asked to connect Worklittle, then shown the resume upload window if you need one.

## Not sure yet?

You do not have to choose immediately. Heart the job instead and decide later with a clear head. See [Heart and save a job](/help/finding-jobs/heart-save).

A good rhythm for a browsing session:

1. Skip anything obviously wrong, quickly.
2. Heart anything interesting.
3. Apply properly to your hearted list afterwards, when you can give each one attention.

# Worklittle in ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code

Swipe the same Jobs you use on worklittle.com, right in chat or VS Code.

Ask ChatGPT, Claude, or VS Code to find jobs and Worklittle can open inside the chat. Same cards, same Maps, same Saved list as [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). Tap Apply to run Apply with AI on more than 3 million open jobs. You can also connect MCP to your own applications.

## What you get

Same Jobs as [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). Swipe roles, Maps, Saved, and your profile. The bottom navigation stays on screen the whole time. When you are signed in, it is the same account as the website.

When you tap **Apply** on a card, Worklittle opens the company’s form, fills it from your resume, and sends it for you. You can watch the cloud browser or take control anytime. See [What is Apply with AI?](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai).

## Add Worklittle in ChatGPT

You need a paid ChatGPT plan (Plus or higher).

1. Add Worklittle as a connector and sign in.
2. Start a new chat and turn Worklittle on for that chat.
3. Ask it to find jobs on Worklittle.

You can swipe, save, open Maps, and run Apply with AI. If you asked for a city, every card in that deck stays in that area. Worklittle does not fill the rest of the stack with the same job title in other cities. **Open Worklittle** in the widget header opens [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com/jobs) already signed in. Step-by-step setup: [Jobs MCP guide → ChatGPT](/jobs/mcp#installation-chatgpt).

## Add Worklittle in Claude

Add Worklittle as a connector, sign in, enable it in a chat, and ask it to find jobs. Setup details: [Jobs MCP guide](/jobs/mcp#mcp-server).

## Add Worklittle in VS Code

Install Worklittle MCP in VS Code, sign in with your key, and ask the assistant to find jobs. You get the same Jobs app for swipe, Maps, Saved, and Apply with AI. Step-by-step setup: [Jobs MCP guide](/jobs/mcp#mcp-server).

## Your own applications

MCP also works in Cursor and other clients, and in products you build. REST, the SDK, and the CLI use the same catalog. See [Jobs MCP](/jobs/mcp) and [Search jobs](/jobs/api/search-jobs).

## Signing in

You can search and skip without signing in. **Apply** may ask you to connect your Worklittle account first.

To switch accounts, open **You** and choose **Log out**. **Disconnect** removes Worklittle from ChatGPT or Claude completely.

## If the app does not open

Make sure Worklittle is enabled for that chat, mention Worklittle in your prompt, or reconnect and try again. Full troubleshooting: [Jobs MCP guide](/jobs/mcp).

# Company pages

See who an employer is and every role they have open.

A company page gathers what we know about an employer and lists all of their current openings, so you can judge the company rather than just the one posting you landed on. The public URL (for example [worklittle.com/company/stripe](https://worklittle.com/company/stripe)) is what search engines index.

## Open a company page

Select the company name from any job card, job detail page, or search result. On [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps), type a company name or pick a company suggestion to open the same page over the map at a URL like [worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe](https://worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe). Walkthrough: [Companies on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/companies-on-maps). You can also search for a company directly. See [Search jobs, companies, and chats](/help/finding-jobs/global-search).

## What you may see at the top

We show what we have, and no company has all of it.

- A description of what the company does, and their logo
- **Company size**, **Headquarters**, **Founded**, **Industry**, and **Type**
- **Total funding** on startups
- Small link pills for whichever of these the company has: Website, LinkedIn, HuggingFace, GitHub, X/Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, Crunchbase, Glassdoor, and TikTok

A missing row just means we do not have that detail for this employer yet. It is not a sign that anything is wrong with the company or the job.

## Their open roles, grouped by department

Underneath the profile is every current opening we have for that employer: roles from their own careers site in the Worklittle index, plus any jobs they posted on Worklittle. They do not need a Worklittle-hosted board for the page to load. [worklittle.com/company/openai](https://worklittle.com/company/openai) is an index page like that.

On [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com/jobs) we surface titles that match your [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) search or the desired role in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) first, then the rest of the board by distance and recency. There is also a search box on the board itself for filtering to a title within that one employer.

If a company has several similar openings, look closely at the differences in level and location. Applying to the one that actually matches you beats applying to all of them.

## Use it before you apply

A few minutes here makes your application and your interview noticeably better:

1. Read what the company actually does, in your own words.
2. Note one thing that genuinely interests you and mention it in your cover letter.
3. Check whether they are growing in your area.

You can also paste the company description into chat and ask for likely interview questions.

# Search jobs, companies, and chats

Find things quickly.

Search looks across jobs, companies, and your own conversations at once, so you can jump straight to whatever you had in mind.

## Open search

Select the search icon, or press **Cmd + K** on a Mac or **Ctrl + K** on Windows.

Start typing and results appear as you go, grouped by type so you can tell a job from a company from one of your chats.

## Homepage search suggestions (desktop)

On a computer, the composer on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com/) also works like a search bar. Click it to see up to ten suggestions: the first message of a chat that found jobs (not later follow-ups in that same chat), titles that match your desired role in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), the city nearest you when it is not already in those recents (that city takes one title slot), popular roles, and a small set of household-name companies with logos. Company suggestions only include employers that currently have open jobs in the catalog.

The same composer sits on [About](https://worklittle.com/about) in place of Search jobs, including the same suggestions. On a phone, that composer stays fixed at the bottom of [About](https://worklittle.com/about), [Research](https://worklittle.com/research), and research articles.

With an empty search box, company rows stay limited to those mega brands that have open jobs. Type a name to search employers that have openings, including smaller employers and local boards.

If nothing matches, the suggestions hide and the bar looks normal again. Choosing a row sends that search the same way a suggestion chip would. This typeahead is desktop-only for now. On a phone the homepage composer stays fixed at the bottom as a normal chat bar.

To narrow Near you / Top picks or the map by date, experience, type, visa, or sort, use the chips above the homepage job cards or [Filter jobs on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/maps-filters). **Sort by** defaults to Relevance (the usual matching). Distance, Salary, and Newest keep that order as you tap Show more. Salary uses listed pay when we have it. Roles without pay sit at the end.

**Top picks for you** on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com/) starts with ten jobs when you are browsing as a guest, and fifteen when you are signed in. Tap **Show more** to keep going. Extra matches that were already fetched stay ready, then more load as you scroll.

## What you can search for

| Type | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Job titles | "forklift operator" |
| Companies | "Trader Joe's" |
| Skills | "phlebotomy" |
| Places | "Tucson" |
| Recents (your chats) | "cover letter for the clinic" |

Searching your own chats is often the quickest way back to a draft you wrote last week.

## Search tips

- Use the words that appear in job postings. "Customer service representative" finds more than "phone person."
- Try two or three variations of a title. Employers name the same role differently.
- Shorter queries return more. Add words only when there is too much to read.

For a location-first approach instead, use [Worklittle Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/what-is-maps).

# Similar jobs and suggestions

Discover related roles.

When you open a job, Worklittle can show a few related openings at the bottom of that job page.

## Where suggestions appear

- At the bottom of a [job detail page](/help/finding-jobs/job-detail) (the job panel, not the [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) swipe deck), under **About the company**.
- **Similar jobs** shows after **About the job** is on screen (AI structured description or the employer raw text). It does not appear while that section is still loading. Three placeholders show until the related cards load.
- Those cards work like other job cards. Click one to open it as another overlay. Use the back button in the top left to return to the job you were on. Hover, right-click, or press and hold for the same quick actions as the homepage.
- Under those cards, the same **Find similar** button from chat (search icon) sends "Find similar jobs" with that posting attached.

Suggestions match related titles, not only that employer. Only openings from the last 7 days are included. At most one of the three is from the same company. Which three you see is shuffled from that title's result page so two Software Engineer postings do not always show the same cards. Roles you already saved, viewed, skipped, or moved in your [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) pipeline stay hidden on your device.

You can also use [quick actions](/help/finding-jobs/quick-actions): right-click or press and hold a job, then choose **Find similar**. Chat still has **Find similar** under a list of job cards.

## Use them to widen your search

Similar roles are the easiest way to discover job titles you did not know to look for. Someone searching for "receptionist" often finds "patient coordinator" or "front office assistant" this way, and those postings are frequently better paid.

When a suggested title keeps appearing, add it to your search terms and see what comes back.

## Shape what you get

Your saves, views, and skips stay on this device and keep those jobs out of the three-card strip. Being decisive helps:

1. Heart the roles that genuinely appeal, not just the ones you might apply to.
2. Skip the clear mismatches instead of scrolling past them.
3. Keep the **Job title** field in Settings pointed at what you actually want next. See [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field).

# Saving jobs as a guest

Log in to track your jobs. See jobs you viewed, saved, and applied for in one place.

You can browse jobs without an account. Saving them, and opening your Saved board, needs you to sign in so viewed, saved, and applied jobs live on your account at [worklittle.com/saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).

## What works as a guest

- Swiping through job cards and using Maps.
- Reading full job detail pages.
- Trying chat.

Heart, **Save** in quick actions, and **Saved** in the sidebar ask you to sign in instead of keeping a list only in this browser.

## Why sign in to save

Saves are stored on your account, not in the browser. That way they follow you if you:

- Clear browsing data.
- Use another browser, phone, or computer.
- Come back later on the same device.

They also feed your pipeline on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).

## Keep your saves

1. Select the heart, **Save**, or **Saved**, then finish sign in.
2. Heart the roles you want. They appear on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) right away.
3. Open that page from the sidebar anytime you are signed in.

See [Saved jobs overview](/help/saved-jobs/overview) to organise them.

# High demand and busy moments

What to do when Apply is waiting.

At busy times you may see Waiting or a short retry message. Your saved jobs and chats are fine.

## What to do

1. If you see **Waiting**, leave it open. Worklittle can run **up to 200** Apply browsers at once. Yours starts when a slot frees.
2. If free AI is used up, sign in or upgrade. See [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits).
3. If you see **Please try again**, wait a minute and try once.
4. Heart the job if you want to come back later.

More detail: [Retries and high demand](/help/apply-with-ai/retries).

# When a job is closed

Why a role disappears.

Postings come down when the employer stops hiring for them, so a job you saved may show as closed the next time you look.

## Why roles close

- The employer filled the position.
- The posting reached its end date.
- The role was put on hold or cancelled.
- The employer removed it from their own careers site.

Worklittle follows the employer. When they take a posting down, it stops appearing here too.

## What happens to your saved copy

A closed job stays on your [Saved jobs board](/help/saved-jobs/overview) and is marked as closed. It keeps its place in your pipeline so your history stays intact.

If you already applied, keep it. A closed posting does not mean you were rejected, and employers do sometimes come back to earlier applicants.

## What to do next

1. Open the [company page](/help/finding-jobs/company-pages) and check for a similar current opening.
2. Look at [similar jobs](/help/finding-jobs/similar-jobs) for the same title elsewhere.
3. Move the closed role to the appropriate stage on your board so your active list stays honest. See [Move jobs between stages](/help/saved-jobs/move-jobs).

# Saved jobs overview

Your hiring pipeline in one place.

Saved jobs is every role you are interested in, in one place. On a computer it opens as a list. You can switch to Grid when you want the column board.

## Open Saved

Go to [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved), or select **Saved** in the sidebar on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). You need to be signed in. If you are signed out, those paths open sign in instead of an empty board.

Every role you have hearted appears here, along with roles you opened long enough to read (Viewed) and roles you skipped while browsing.

On a computer the default view is a **list** of job cards, with stage filters at the top. Long lists load a page at a time as you scroll.

## List and Grid

**Grid** and **List** sit in the top-right of [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved), to the right of Share.

- **List** is the default. Filter by stage, then press and hold or right-click a card to move or delete it.
- **Grid** is the column board. Drag cards between stages, and drag column headings to reorder them.

This browser remembers which view you last used. You can also open Grid directly at [worklittle.com/saved?=grid](https://worklittle.com/saved?=grid).

## Why it beats a spreadsheet

- Cards arrive automatically when you heart a job, with the details already filled in.
- Roles you open for about a second show up under Viewed if they are not already elsewhere on the board.
- You can see all your applications at once instead of hunting through email.
- Roles that go quiet are obvious, which is your cue to follow up.
- It is on every device you sign in on.

For how the columns work, see [Pipeline stages explained](/help/saved-jobs/stages).

## A simple weekly routine

1. Move anything that progressed into its new stage.
2. Follow up on applications older than a week with no reply.
3. Add fresh roles by [swiping to apply](https://worklittle.com/jobs).
4. Move anything dead into Rejected or Withdrawn.

Fifteen minutes a week keeps the board trustworthy, and a trustworthy board is the one you will actually use.

# Pipeline stages explained

Saved through Offer, plus Skipped and Viewed when you have passed on or looked at roles.

Each column on your Saved board is a stage, representing how far along you are with that particular role.

## The seven columns you always see

| Stage | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Saved | You are interested but have not applied yet |
| In progress | An application is started but not finished |
| Applied | Your application is in and you are waiting |
| Interview | A conversation is booked or has happened |
| Offer | You have an offer to consider |
| Rejected | They said no |
| Withdrawn | You pulled out, or you no longer want the role |

Every job starts in Saved when you heart it. You choose when it moves. Open the board at [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).

## Skipped

There is also a **Skipped** column for every role you passed on while browsing. It is not hidden behind a setting. It simply will not show until you save or apply for a job, then it fills with the roles you skipped so your active stages stay easy to scan.

You can drag the Skipped column anywhere among your other stages. It is worth checking now and then. See [Skipped jobs](/help/saved-jobs/skipped-jobs).

## Viewed

**Viewed** is for roles you opened long enough to read (about a second) that are not already on your board elsewhere. Quick peeks do not count. Skipping on the jobs deck does not add a Viewed card either - that goes to Skipped only.

The column stays hidden until it has at least one job. It starts last on the board by default, and you can drag the column anywhere you like. You can drag cards into or out of Viewed the same way as other stages. Hearting or applying moves the role into the normal pipeline and takes it out of Viewed.

## Using stages honestly

The board only helps if it reflects reality. Two habits make the difference:

- Move a card the same day something changes, while you remember the detail.
- Move dead roles into Rejected or Withdrawn rather than leaving them in Applied indefinitely.

A board full of stale Applied cards hides the two roles that actually need a follow-up today.

## Reading your own pipeline

The shape of your board tells you where to put effort:

- Lots in **Saved**, few in **Applied**: you are researching more than applying.
- Lots in **Applied**, few in **Interview**: your resume and cover letter probably need work. Try [Create or edit a resume in chat](/help/chat-ai/resumes-from-chat).
- Reaching **Interview** but stopping there: focus on interview practice.

Next: [Move jobs between stages](/help/saved-jobs/move-jobs).

# Move jobs between stages

Drag or pick a stage.

Moving a job to a new stage takes a second, either by dragging the card or picking a stage from its menu.

## Drag and drop

On a computer, select **Grid** in the top-right of [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) (to the right of Share), then:

1. Press and hold a job card.
2. Drag it to the column you want.
3. Release. The card settles into its new stage.

If a column is off screen, drag the card towards the edge of the board and the view scrolls with you.

On the **list** view, press and hold or right-click a card instead, then pick a stage. See [Saved jobs overview](/help/saved-jobs/overview).

## Pick a stage from the menu

Dragging is fiddly on a small screen, so there is a simpler route:

1. Open the menu on the job card.
2. Choose **Move to** or the stage picker.
3. Select the stage.

This is the same action, just without the dragging. See [Saved jobs on mobile](/help/saved-jobs/mobile-saved).

## When to move a card

- **Saved to In progress** when you start an application you have not finished.
- **In progress to Applied** the moment you submit, not later.
- **Applied to Interview** as soon as a conversation is booked.
- **Interview to Offer** when you have something in writing.
- **Anything to Rejected or Withdrawn** when it ends, whether they said no or you walked away.

Moving a card out of your active columns does not delete it. Your history stays, which is useful when you want to see how the search actually went. See [Share your job search history](/help/saved-jobs/download-history).

# Share your Saved board

Send a link to someone you trust.

You can share a view of your Saved board with a mentor, career counsellor, or family member so they can see your search without needing your account.

## Create a share link

1. Open [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).
2. Select **Share** in the top-right corner. **Grid** / **List** sits to the right of Share. On desktop, these sit where Sign in appears when you are logged out.
3. The link is copied for you, and your phone may offer to pass it straight to a message.
4. Send it to the person you want to show.

The link is a public web address, so anyone who has it can open the board without signing in. They can look, but they cannot move your cards or change anything.

## Who to share with

- A mentor or coach who can suggest better-fitting roles.
- A friend who might know someone at one of the companies.
- A career adviser or caseworker tracking your progress.
- A partner who wants to know how it is going without asking every night.

Because the link works for anyone who has it, only send it to people you actually trust, and avoid posting it publicly.

## How long a link lasts

There is no switch that turns a share link off on demand. What you can count on instead:

- **It expires.** Each link is good for about a month, and opening **Share** again refreshes it.
- **Viewers can only look.** Nothing they do changes your board.
- **It shows your board as it is now**, not a snapshot from the day you shared it.

Because you cannot revoke a link the moment you change your mind, treat it like anything else you paste into a message. It is for a mentor or a friend, not for posting somewhere public.
