# Saved jobs on mobile

Use the list on your phone.

On a phone your Saved board becomes a scrollable list, so you can review and update your search from anywhere without pinching around a wide board.

## Getting around

1. Open **Saved** from the menu.
2. Scroll through your jobs.
3. Switch stages using the tabs or the stage selector at the top.
4. Tap a job to open the full posting.

Everything syncs with the board on your computer, so a change made on the bus is there when you sit down at home.

## Update a job on the go

Tap the menu on a job card to:

- Move it to a different stage.
- Open the original posting.
- Share it.
- Remove it from your saved list.

Picking a stage from the menu is much easier than dragging on a small screen. See [Move jobs between stages](/help/saved-jobs/move-jobs).

## Make the most of small moments

Phone time is best for quick maintenance rather than deep work:

- Move cards forward right after a phone interview.
- Heart interesting roles while you are out and apply properly later.
- Check who has gone quiet while you wait for a bus.

Save the longer tasks, like rewriting a resume, for a bigger screen.

# Reorder columns

Customize your board layout.

You can rearrange the columns on your Saved board so the stages you check most often sit where you want them.

## Move a column

Column order is for **Grid** view. On a computer, select **Grid** in the top-right of [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) (to the right of Share), or open [Grid](https://worklittle.com/saved?=grid).

1. Press and hold a column heading.
2. Drag it left or right.
3. Release to drop it in place.

The board saves the new order for you, on every device you sign in on.

## Layouts that work well

- **Left to right by progress.** The default. Best for seeing the whole journey.
- **Active work first.** Put Interview and Applied on the left when you have a lot in flight and want them without scrolling.
- **Research mode.** Keep Saved on the left when you are still gathering roles rather than applying.

There is no wrong order. Whichever column you open most should be the easiest to reach.

## Reset

Until you rearrange them, columns that have jobs sit first so you are not scrolling past empty stages. After you drag a column, that order is yours - it syncs to your account so desktop and other signed-in devices match.

Drag columns back toward the usual progress order anytime: Saved, In progress, Applied, Interview, Offer, Rejected, Withdrawn, then Skipped and Viewed when those columns are visible. Viewed starts last by default, and both Viewed and Skipped can sit anywhere you drag them. See [Pipeline stages explained](/help/saved-jobs/stages) for what each one covers.

# Skipped jobs

Find roles you passed on.

Roles you skip are not deleted. They move to the **Skipped** column on your Saved board, so you can look back if you change your mind or skipped one by accident.

## See what you skipped

Open [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved). The **Skipped** column is not hidden behind a setting. It simply will not show until you save or apply for a job, then every role you passed on while browsing lands there.

Skipping never also puts the role in Viewed. A job lives in one column at a time. This is the place to go when you remember a job a second too late, which happens to everyone browsing quickly.

## Bring a job back

1. Find the role in the skipped list.
2. Open it to read the full posting again.
3. Heart it to move it into Saved, or apply directly from [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs).

Nothing you did while skipping counts against you, and the employer never sees a skip.

## Why skipping is still worth doing

Skipping is how Worklittle learns what to stop showing you. Passing on the roles that are genuinely wrong means the next batch is closer to what you want.

If your skipped list is enormous and the cards still feel off, your **Job title** in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) is probably too broad. Narrowing it, or ruling out a level with a minus sign, fixes things faster than skipping ever will. See [Swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck) and [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field).

# Share your job search history

Send your board to someone, and read it yourself.

Your Saved board is the record of your whole search. You cannot download it as a file, but you can send someone a link to it and you can read a lot from it yourself.

## There is no file to download

Worklittle does not turn your Saved board into a spreadsheet or a PDF. If you were hoping for an export button on the board, that does not exist today.

Two things do exist and cover most of what people want:

- A **share link** to the live board, described below.
- **Export all data** in [account settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), which is an account-wide copy rather than a tidy report of your applications.

## Share a link instead

1. Open [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).
2. Select **Share**.
3. The link is copied for you.
4. Send it to whoever needs to see it.

Anyone with the link can open the board in a browser without signing in, and nobody can change anything. Links last about a month. Full detail in [Share your Saved board](/help/saved-jobs/share-pipeline).

For a coach, a mentor, or a family member, a live link is usually better than a file anyway, because it stays current.

## If someone needs proof of applications

Some agencies and programmes ask for evidence that you have been applying. Send the share link, and take screenshots of the board if they need something they can file.

Your **Applied** column and its dates are the part they usually care about, so it is worth keeping cards moved over promptly. See [Move jobs between stages](/help/saved-jobs/move-jobs).

## Learn from your own board

Read it now and then with honest eyes:

1. How many applications turned into interviews?
2. Which industries replied fastest?
3. Which roles went quiet, and what did they have in common?

Describe what you see to chat and ask what to change. It is one of the most useful conversations you can have mid-search. See [Tips for better answers](/help/chat-ai/chat-tips).

# What is Apply with AI?

Apply for jobs with one click. Upload your resume, tap Apply, and Worklittle fills out and sends the application for you.

Apply for jobs with one click. Upload your resume once. Tap Apply. Worklittle opens the company’s real application in a cloud browser in chat, fills it in, and sends it for you. You never have to answer questions or click Submit.

## How it works

That is the whole idea.

1. Upload your resume (the first time).
2. Pick a job and tap **Apply with AI** (or plain **Apply** on a job card).
3. A cloud browser opens in chat so you can see the company’s form as Worklittle fills it in.
4. Worklittle sends the application (Always submit is on).
5. The job shows as **Applied** on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).

You can watch the whole time. You can take control anytime. You do not have to do either. It works on **more than 3 million** open jobs.

From [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs), that Apply starts the application for the card you tapped. It does not search for other roles.

## See it and take control anytime

The apply runs in a **cloud browser inside chat**. That is a live window of the real company page.

- Open the chat (or tap the Applying with AI pill) anytime to watch every click and typed answer as it happens.
- Tap **Take control** anytime if you want to click or type yourself. Tap **Continue with AI** when you want Worklittle to pick up again.
- Want Worklittle to wait before it sends? Turn **Always submit** off. Worklittle still fills everything else. You click Submit on the live page, or turn Always submit back on and tap **Continue with AI**.

More detail: [Watching the browser panel](/help/apply-with-ai/watching-browser).

## Started from the API

If you start Apply with AI with a **personal** API key (REST, MCP, CLI, or SDK), the same chat appears in Recents on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) — job chip, live browser, Saved **In progress**. It does **not** show in the floating Applying with AI pill at the top of the screen. That pill is only for applies you start in the app (Apply on a job card or in chat), not keys used from an outside client.

That chat is for watching and talking. Stop, take control, and submit stay in your API client. Company API keys do not open a consumer chat.

See [Apply for jobs](https://docs.worklittle.com/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs).

## Want to look before it sends?

There is one button for that, **Always submit**.

- **On** (the normal setting). Worklittle sends the application for you. You do not need to do anything else.
- **Off**. Worklittle fills the form, then waits so you can change things and press **Submit** yourself.

Leave it on unless you want that extra look. See [Start an Apply with AI session](/help/apply-with-ai/start-apply).

## What it uses about you

It uses the resume you uploaded, plus anything already on your profile (name, phone, school, and similar).

Most recent employer and the title you held there come from that resume. If those lines are missing (a thin resume, or a test account with no work history), Worklittle still fills the required boxes with **N/A** so **Always submit** can send instead of stopping to ask you.

You can fill more in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) if you want. You do not have to answer questions during apply. See [Upload or replace your resume](/help/profile-alerts/resume-upload).

## What it will not do

- It will not invent jobs or degrees you never had.
- It will not apply to jobs you did not pick.
- It will not make you fill the employer form yourself on the **3 million+** jobs that support Apply with AI. See [Which jobs support Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/eligibility).

## Next steps

- Apply with AI vs autofill: [Worklittle vs autofill browser extensions](/help/apply-with-ai/apply-with-ai-vs-autofill)
- Add a resume: [Resume required before applying](/help/apply-with-ai/resume-gate)
- Start applying: [Start an Apply with AI session](/help/apply-with-ai/start-apply)

# Which jobs support Apply with AI

Apply with AI works on more than 3 million open jobs. Here is how to spot them.

Apply with AI works on **more than 3 million** open jobs on Worklittle. You do not need to guess which boards qualify. We mark them for you.

## How many jobs

Right now **more than 3 million** open roles support Apply with AI. That number moves as new postings appear and others close, and it grows when more employer forms can be filled and sent automatically.

On those jobs, upload your resume, tap Apply, and Worklittle fills out and sends the company’s form for you.

## Where you can tell

On a **job page**, roles with Apply with AI show an **Apply with AI** option next to the apply button.

On a **job card**, the button always just says **Apply**, and that means Apply with AI. See [Swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck).

You do not need to check the company or the job board. If you see **Apply** or **Apply with AI**, Worklittle can fill and send that company’s form for you.

Some postings only have a regular apply link. Those are not Apply with AI. Use the button on the job, not the URL.

We sometimes pause Apply with AI for a whole job board when the employer site starts blocking automated browsers. Those roles keep a normal apply link until we turn it back on. Trust the button on the job.

# Resume required before applying

Upload a resume before Apply or Create resume.

Apply with AI and Create resume need a resume on file first, so Worklittle can use your real experience.

## What you will see

The first time you tap **Apply** or **Create resume** without a resume, a window asks you to upload one. Pick your file and wait while we read it.

When the spinner finishes, the action continues on its own. You do not need to tap again.

We save the resume so Apply with AI and Create resume can use it. You can review what we put on your profile in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings). Apply with AI still needs you to [log in](https://worklittle.com).

## What happens to the file

Your resume does double duty:

- It gets attached to employer applications.
- We pull out your name, school, past roles, contact details, and skills to fill in your profile, but only for fields you left blank. Anything you typed yourself stays exactly as you wrote it.

You can review and correct everything afterwards in [Edit your profile](/help/profile-alerts/edit-profile).

## Accepted files and common problems

- Standard resume files work best. A PDF exported from your word processor is the safest choice.
- Scanned images of a printed page are hard to read, so text may come through incomplete.
- If the upload fails, the window offers **Try again**. A second attempt usually works.
- Very large files can time out. Trim extra pages or export a smaller version.

To swap your resume later, see [Upload or replace your resume](/help/profile-alerts/resume-upload).

## From ChatGPT or Claude

In [ChatGPT or Claude](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app) you can search and skip without a Worklittle login. When you tap **Apply**, you may be asked to connect your Worklittle account first. After that, Apply works the same way as on the website.

# Start an Apply with AI session

Launch from a job card or detail.

Sign in, open a job, and tap Apply. Worklittle fills and sends the form. AI use counts toward your free monthly AI, or Instant if you have it.

## From a job card

1. Sign in on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) if you have not already.
2. Open [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs).
3. Find a role you want.
4. Tap **Apply** on the card (same as Apply with AI).
5. Stay on Jobs, or open Chat anytime to watch.

Apply with AI works on **more than 3 million** open jobs. See [Which jobs support Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/eligibility).

## From a job page

1. Sign in if you have not already.
2. Open the job.
3. Choose **Apply with AI**.
4. Upload a resume if asked.
5. Worklittle fills the form and sends it. Open Chat if you want to watch.

If the employer also asks for a writing sample, portfolio file, or similar extra upload, Apply writes a one-page hiring-manager PDF from the applicant profile and attaches it on any Apply with AI board (Greenhouse, Breezy, and the others). The leftover-field agent can find extra file inputs even when the form script has not mapped that control yet. Resume and cover letter stay on their own create/upload path.

## Watch or take control

Every run shows a live company page in chat. You can watch, or tap **Take control** to click yourself, then hand control back. You do not have to. See [Watching the browser panel](/help/apply-with-ai/watching-browser).

## Always submit

**Always submit** is on by default, so Worklittle sends the application for you. While it is on, the cloud browser shows **Take control** and **Cancel** (not **Submit**) — Worklittle clicks Submit for you.

Turn it off only if you want to look first, then press **Submit** yourself.

If automatic submit cannot finish (for example a spam check), the status asks you to **Take control** so you can finish on the live page.

## What it costs

There is no set fee per job. Apply with AI uses a little of your AI allowance, usually about **1 to 3 cents**. Free monthly AI covers many applies. Instant or a card covers more. See [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits).

## How many at once

Worklittle can run **up to 200** Apply with AI browsers at once. There is no per-account session cap. Usage also follows [AI credit](/help/account/daily-ai-limits) (free monthly, Instant, or a card). If you see **Waiting**, leave it open. It starts when a browser slot is free.

Guests need to sign in first. See [Browsing as a guest vs signing in](/help/getting-started/guest-vs-signed-in).

## While it runs

You can keep browsing. An **Applying with AI** pill shows progress. Tap it to open the chat, or **Stop** to cancel. Reloading the page does not cancel a run that already started. Finished applications land on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved).

# Watching the browser panel

A cloud browser in chat shows every step. You can watch anytime and take control anytime.

Apply with AI shows a cloud browser in chat. That is a live window of the real company application. You can always see what it is doing as it does it, and you can take control anytime.

## What you are looking at

- The live company page is inside the Apply chat.
- You see it scroll and type as Worklittle fills it in.
- A short **status pill** on the browser says what the page is doing (Getting ready, filling, Take control). That pill is not the chat message.
- Chat text is written by the assistant and stays in the thread. When submit succeeds, a new line confirms it. When something fails, a new line explains why.
- If the company flags the automated browser as spam, the panel keeps a screenshot of that page so you can see it, and chat explains what happened.

Open Chat, or tap the **Applying with AI** pill, anytime you want to look.

## Take control anytime

Tap **Take control** whenever you want. The page unlocks so you can click and type yourself.

When you are in control, the pill says **You're in control** with **Stop** and **Continue with AI** (not **Submit**). Worklittle stays in that mode until you tap **Continue with AI**. Then it finishes leftover fields from where you left off, and it clicks Submit only if **Always submit** is on.

When **Always submit** is on and you are not in control, the pill shows **Take control** (not **Submit**) — Worklittle sends for you. If automatic submit cannot finish, you get **Finish application?** with **Finish myself** (opens the company’s real posting in a new tab) and **Continue with AI** (let Worklittle keep filling). That chat shows an orange dot in Recents until you finish.

Email or text verification codes: Worklittle tries to fill those itself when **Always submit** is on. A Google reCAPTCHA logo in the footer is not a block. A real checkbox or image challenge still needs you. If chat says spam but the form looks normal, that was a false alarm on submit retries — tap **Continue with AI** if you want it to keep going.

If required questions remain that Apply cannot finish from your resume (identity, SSN, one-time codes, and similar), chat asks those questions **before** Submit — you answer in chat, then Apply continues. Empty most-recent employer or title fields are filled with **N/A** instead of waiting.

You never have to take control. It is there if you want it.

## If you step away

If you are reviewing the form and do not click, type, or scroll for **five minutes**, Apply with AI pauses so the cloud browser does not stay open. Scroll or click and the timer starts over.

Your filled answers stay on the page. Open the same chat to continue. If the live page had to reload, Worklittle puts those answers back before you submit.

## If the live view will not load

Sometimes the window stays blank. That is okay.

- Wait a few seconds.
- Refresh the page. The apply keeps going.
- Try another browser if you want to watch.

A blank panel does not stop the application from finishing and sending.

## Stopping early

Tap **Stop** if you want to cancel. Nothing more gets sent. The job stays on Saved as in progress so you can try again later. See [Finish an incomplete apply](/help/apply-with-ai/finish-incomplete).

# Do I have to answer questions?

No. Upload your resume and tap Apply. Looking things over is only if you turn Always submit off.

No. You never have to answer anything. Upload your resume, tap Apply, and Worklittle fills the form and sends it. Looking it over first is only if you turn one button off.

## The normal way

1. Upload your resume.
2. Tap **Apply** or **Apply with AI**.
3. Leave **Always submit** on.
4. Done. You do not need to type answers or press Submit.

## If you want to look first

Turn **Always submit** off in the cloud browser in chat. Worklittle still fills the form. Then you can change anything you like on the live page and click Submit there yourself.

Or leave Always submit on, watch the cloud browser, and tap **Take control** anytime if you want to fix one field yourself. Tap **Continue with AI** when you want it to finish (and send, if Always submit is on).

Turn Always submit back on anytime for the hands-off path.

## Codes and logins

If a company sends a one-time code by email or phone, Worklittle handles that for you in the session.

If a site forces you to sign into an account they made, take control in the cloud browser, finish that step, then hand control back. Most applies do not need this.

## Optional profile extras

You can save things like work authorization, driver’s license, and links in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) so forms fill even more smoothly. That is helpful, not required for Apply to run.

# Retries and high demand

What to do if Apply is waiting.

Sometimes Apply shows Waiting. Leave it open and it starts soon.

## Waiting

If you see **Waiting**, your apply is next in line. Nothing is lost. Leave the page open. It starts when a browser slot is free (Worklittle runs up to 200 at once). Busy days stay in this line instead of failing.

## Out of free AI

If you are out of free AI for the month, you will see a sign-in or Instant prompt. Your resume and saved jobs are fine. See [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits).

## Please try again

If you see **Please try again**, wait a minute and try once more. Retrying does not double submit an application that never started.

## More help

See [Apply with AI troubleshooting](/help/apply-with-ai/troubleshooting-apply).

# Finish an incomplete apply

Pick up where you left off.

If you stopped, closed the tab, or lost signal, the application is still waiting for you.

## Find the session again

1. Open the chat list on worklittle.com.
2. Look for the chat named after the role, for example "Apply to Product Designer at Northwind".
3. Open it. The browser panel comes back with the application in the state you left it.

Sessions that were running, paused, stopped, waiting on you, or waiting to submit can all be resumed.

If the session paused because you stepped away, the form still has what was already filled in.

## Resuming from your saved jobs

Jobs you started show as **In progress** on your saved jobs board. Open the job from there and choose to continue. If the original session has expired, starting again is safe. Employers see one application, not two, as long as the first one never got submitted.

## Starting again

If a session already finished or you cancelled it, open the job and start a fresh Apply with AI run. Finished applications stay on your [Saved board](https://worklittle.com/saved) as **Applied**.

# Apply with AI troubleshooting

Common fixes.

Normally you upload a resume and tap Apply. Apply with AI works on more than 3 million open jobs. Use this page if something looks stuck mid-run.

## Quick fixes

| What you see | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A window asks for a resume | Upload one. See [Resume required before applying](/help/apply-with-ai/resume-gate). |
| Verification step on the employer form | Stay in the session. Worklittle handles phone and email codes. |
| Blank browser panel | Refresh if you want to watch. The apply can still finish and send. |
| Same status for a while | Give it a minute. |
| Apply stopped and chat suggests applying on the company site | Their job board stalled. Use the link in chat to apply on the employer page. |
| Waiting | Leave it open; it starts when a browser slot frees. |
| Log in / Upgrade to Instant | Sign in or upgrade to keep applying. See [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits). |
| Want to change answers before it sends | Turn **Always submit** off, edit, then press **Submit**. See [Do I have to answer questions?](/help/apply-with-ai/answer-questions). |

## Wrong details on the form

The agent copies what is on your account, so a wrong phone number on the form means a wrong phone number on your profile. Fix it once in [Edit your profile](/help/profile-alerts/edit-profile) and future applications pick up the correction.

If you spot a mistake mid session, take control, correct the field on the page, and hand control back.

## Still need help

Note the job title, the company, and what the status line said, then reach out through the help option in the app. Those three details are usually enough for us to see exactly where the session ended.

# Edit your profile

Name, dream job, school, and more.

Your profile is the source of truth for everything Apply with AI types into employer forms.

## Open your profile

1. Go to [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and sign in.
2. Open the **Profile** section.

Changes save as you go. There is no separate save button to hunt for.

## What each field is for

| Field | What to put there |
| --- | --- |
| **Name** | Your full legal name, the way you want it on applications. |
| **Job title** | The role you want next, not the one you have. Several titles separated by commas all count, and a minus sign rules a word out. |
| **School** | Your degree and school, for example "BS Computer Science, Ohio State". |
| **Phone** | Pick your country, then the number. |
| **Links** | LinkedIn, portfolio, GitHub, and anything else worth sharing. |
| **Work authorization** | Countries where you can already work. |
| **Driver License** | Whether you hold a valid license. |
| **Your favorite things** | Skills, interests, and hobbies. |

## Let your resume do the typing

Upload a resume and we fill in the blanks for you, including your name, school, past roles, and contact details. We only touch fields you left empty, so nothing you wrote gets overwritten. See [Upload or replace your resume](/help/profile-alerts/resume-upload).

## Why it matters

Your resume is enough to start [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai). Filling more of your profile is optional and can make forms even smoother. The **Job title** field does double duty, steering both your [instant job alerts](/help/profile-alerts/job-alerts) and the roles you see while browsing. See [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field) for how to use commas and exclusions in it.

# Profile photo

Camera, upload, or default avatar.

A photo shows up next to your name in chats and on your Worklittle account.

## Add or change your photo

1. Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and find your avatar at the top of the Profile section.
2. Click the avatar to open the photo menu.
3. Choose one of:
   - **Upload photo** to pick an image from your device.
   - **Take photo** to use your camera right there.
   - **Remove** to go back to the default avatar.

## Using your camera

The camera option asks your browser for permission the first time. If nothing happens, check that your browser is allowed to use the camera for worklittle.com, and that no other app is holding it open.

You will see a live preview before anything is saved, so you can retake as many times as you like.

## Picking a good image

- Square images look best, since the avatar is a circle.
- Keep your face roughly centred so nothing important gets cropped.
- Standard image files work. Very large photos are resized automatically.

## Removing your photo

**Remove** clears the image and puts back the default avatar with your initial. Employers never require a photo, and removing it has no effect on your applications.

# Upload or replace your resume

Keep applications ready.

One resume on file keeps you ready to apply anywhere on Worklittle in a single tap.

## Upload your first resume

1. Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), then **Profile**.
2. Choose **Upload resume**.
3. Pick your file and wait a few seconds while we read it.

You can upload before you sign in. We still save the file to Worklittle cloud on this device and read your experience so Create resume and profile fields can use it. When you log in later, that resume moves onto your account.

You can also upload during your first application. See [Resume required before applying](/help/apply-with-ai/resume-gate). Apply with AI itself still needs you to [log in](https://worklittle.com).

## Replace an older version

Upload again and the new file takes over. The old one is no longer sent to employers.

One thing to know: reading a new resume only fills profile fields that are still empty. If you changed jobs and your profile still shows the old title, update that field by hand in [Edit your profile](/help/profile-alerts/edit-profile).

Uploading the exact same file again (same contents) reuses the analysis we already have, so you do not wait on a second full read.

## What we read from it

- Name and contact details
- School, degree, and graduation
- Recent roles and companies
- Skills and interests

That information fills your profile and gets reused on every application, which is why keeping the file current pays off.

## File tips

- A PDF exported from your word processor reads most reliably.
- Avoid scans and screenshots, since text in an image is hard to extract.
- Keep it to the pages you actually want employers to see, because the same file is what gets attached.

# Skills and interests

Chips that describe you.

The **Your favorite things** field is a quick list of what you are good at and what you enjoy.

## Adding them

1. Open **Settings**, then **Profile**.
2. Find **Your favorite things**.
3. Type each skill, interest, or hobby on its own line.

Keep entries short. "React", "Spanish", "Trail running", and "Financial modelling" all work better than full sentences.

## Where they show up

- Applications that ask about skills, languages, or interests get better answers.
- Job recommendations lean on them to find roles you would actually enjoy.
- Chat uses them for context when you ask for advice on a role or a resume.

## Editing and removing

Delete a line to remove it. Backspace on an empty line clears it cleanly, so you can tidy the list quickly. Uploading a resume can suggest skills for you, and you are free to delete anything that does not fit.

# Work authorization countries

Where you can work.

Tell us which countries you can already work in so applications answer the sponsorship question correctly.

## Set your countries

1. Open **Settings**, then **Profile**.
2. Find **Work authorization**.
3. Search for a country and select it. Add as many as apply.

Include every country where you have citizenship, permanent residency, or a valid work permit.

## Why applications ask

Almost every employer form has a version of "Are you authorized to work in this country?" and "Will you require sponsorship now or in the future?". With your countries saved, [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) fills those in for you from your profile.

## Keeping it accurate

- Only list places you can genuinely work today. A pending application is not the same as authorization.
- Update it when your status changes, such as a new permit or a new citizenship.
- Leaving it blank is fine. Apply still runs from your resume. Saving this just helps forms fill more completely.

# Social and portfolio links

Add LinkedIn and sites.

Employers ask for links constantly, so saving them once means never typing them again.

## Add a link

1. Open **Settings**, then **Profile**.
2. Go to **Links**.
3. Paste the full address, including the https:// part.
4. Repeat for each profile or site you want to share.

Common ones are LinkedIn, a personal website or portfolio, GitHub, and Hugging Face.

## What good links look like

- Point at your public profile page, not a page only you can see when signed in.
- Check the link opens in a private window. If it asks for a login, employers will not see it either.
- Skip anything you would not want a hiring manager reading.

## How they get used

When a form asks for LinkedIn, GitHub, or a portfolio, [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) can fill those from what you saved. Links are optional. You do not have to answer during apply.

# Email preferences

Alerts, events, announcements.

You control exactly which emails Worklittle sends you, and you can change your mind at any time.

## The three switches

| Setting | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Instant job alerts** | New roles that match the job title on your profile. |
| **Local events** | Meetups, hiring events, and things happening near you. |
| **Announcements** | Occasional product news and new features, including the welcome email about an hour after you sign up. |

## Change them

1. Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings).
2. Scroll to the email section.
3. Flip any switch. It saves right away.

Turning everything off is completely fine. You will still get essential account email, such as sign in codes.

## Unsubscribing from an email

Every marketing email has an unsubscribe link at the bottom, including Instant and join invite emails. **Manage emails** opens the same switches, plus **Unsubscribe** under them. Unsubscribe is its own control. It stays on while you still want Worklittle emails, including invites from friends. Turn it off to unsubscribe. That also turns the other switches off. Turn it back on to subscribe to Instant job alerts, Local events, and Announcements again. Turning those three off yourself does not unsubscribe you, and friends can still send you invites.

If you got an invite and do not have a Worklittle account yet, Manage emails still lets you turn **Announcements** on, and **Unsubscribe** off to stop future invites. Instant job alerts and Local events appear after you create an account.

If you would rather keep alerts and drop announcements, flip only **Announcements**. You will still get essential account email, such as sign in codes.

For details on how alerts choose jobs, see [Instant job alerts](/help/profile-alerts/job-alerts).

# Instant job alerts

Emails based on the role you want.

Job alerts email you new matching roles without you having to check the site every day.

## Turn them on

1. Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings).
2. Switch on **Instant job alerts**.
3. Make sure the **Job title** field on your profile says the role you actually want.

Both pieces matter. The switch turns on the email, and the job title decides what goes in it.

## What decides your matches

Everything comes from the **Job title** field in Settings, which is the role you are searching for rather than the one you have.

- List several titles, separated by commas, to match any of them.
- Put a minus in front of a word to rule it out, for example `-Senior`.

That is it. There is no separate alert to build or maintain. Change what is in that field and the emails follow along. See [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field).

## How often they arrive

- We check for new matches through the day.
- An email only goes out when there are at least five new roles worth showing, so you are not pinged over a single posting.
- You will never get more than three alert emails in one day.

## Not getting any?

- Confirm **Instant job alerts** is on. See [Email preferences](/help/profile-alerts/email-preferences).
- Confirm your **Job title** is filled in. See [Your dream role field](/help/profile-alerts/dream-job-field).
- Try a broader title, or add a second one. "Designer" finds far more than "Senior Design Systems Lead".
- Check whether an exclusion is doing too much work. `-Lead` quietly removes a lot of postings.
- Check your spam folder and mark the message as not spam so future ones land properly.

# Your dream role field

The Job title field, with several roles and exclusions.

The **Job title** field in your Settings is where you say what you want next, and it is the single biggest lever on the jobs Worklittle shows and emails you.

## Forward looking, not backward looking

Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and find **Job title**. The hint inside it reads "Add your dream job". That wording is deliberate. Put the role you want to be hired into, not the one on your business card.

If you are a support specialist aiming to move into product, write "Product Manager", not "Support Specialist".

Your real work history is separate and comes from your resume, so employers still see what you have actually done. Pointing this field at your goal costs you nothing.

## You can list more than one role

Separate titles with commas and we look for jobs matching **any** of them:

```text
Software Engineer, Product Manager
```

This is the right move when you are genuinely open to two or three paths. It is not the place to list ten loosely related things, because everything you add widens what you see.

## Rule things out with a minus sign

Put a minus in front of a word and any job title containing it is left out:

```text
Software Engineer, Product Manager, -Senior
```

That says: show me software engineering and product roles, but nothing senior. The common shorthands are handled for you, so `-Senior` also catches "Sr." and "Sr".

Exclusions are the quickest fix when your results are consistently one level off, in either direction.

In chat, the same leading-minus pattern works for **employers** when you say you do not want a company (or a group of them). The assistant puts those in the company filter as slugs such as `-lucid-motors`, not in this Job title field.

## Room to work with

The field holds around 200 characters, which is plenty for several titles plus a couple of exclusions. Keep it readable rather than cramming it, since a shorter honest list beats a long one.

## What it drives

- The roles in your **job alert emails**. See [Instant job alerts](/help/profile-alerts/job-alerts).
- The jobs you see while you [swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck).
- The framing chat uses when you ask for advice on your search.

One thing it does not control is **where**. There is no location box in Settings. Nearby search uses your device location when it is already allowed, otherwise an approximate network location. To grant or refresh precise location, use current location on [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps).

# Driver's license info

When applications ask for it.

A simple yes or no about your license saves a pause on the many roles that require driving.

## Set it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Profile**.
2. Find **Driver License**.
3. Choose **Valid license** or **No license**.

There is no place to enter a license number, and Worklittle never asks for one.

## Where it comes up

Delivery, field service, healthcare visits, sales territories, trades, and plenty of hybrid roles all ask about driving. With this saved, [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) can fill that in for you.

## If you are not sure what to pick

Choose **Valid license** only if yours is current and unrestricted for normal driving. Otherwise leave it as **No license**. Apply still runs from your resume either way.

# What is Worklittle Business?

Employer workspace overview.

Worklittle Business at worklittle.com/business is the side of Worklittle where companies post jobs and hire.

## Two sides, one account

| Surface | Who it is for | What you do there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| worklittle.com | Job seekers | Search jobs, apply, track applications |
| worklittle.com/business | Employers | Post jobs, review candidates, manage your team |

You sign in with the same Worklittle account on both, and switching between them does not require a second login.

## What you can do as an employer

- **Post jobs** and publish them to your company board.
- **Track candidates** through stages from Sourced to Offer.
- **Work as a team**, with teammates, roles, and shared notes.
- **Search for talent** beyond the people who applied.
- **Send stage emails** automatically as candidates move forward.

## Getting started

1. [Create an organization](/help/business-basics/create-organization) for your company.
2. [Verify a work email](/help/business-basics/work-email) so you can publish jobs.
3. [Invite teammates](/help/business-basics/invite-teammates) who will help you hire.
4. [Post a job](/help/hiring/post-a-job).

Billing is pay as you go per organization, not seats. See [Worklittle Business FAQ](/help/business-basics/what-is-worklittle-business-faq) and [Do we buy seats?](/help/business-basics/no-seats-payg).

# Create an organization

Set up your company.

An organization is your company's shared workspace, holding your jobs, candidates, and teammates.

## Personal vs company

Every account has a **Personal** workspace for individual use (chat, plugins, API keys for job search, and its own billing wallet). Personal is not a company.

Hiring tools (jobs, candidates, employees, surveys, HR documents, calendar, webhooks) and the matching employer API, SDK, MCP, and agent tools only work in a **company** organization.

Switch between Personal and company from your profile (account row at the bottom of the left sidebar). See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization). If you keep separate emails for job seeking and hiring, that is [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts) (up to three signed-in emails).

## Create yours

1. Go to [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization) and sign in with your work email.
2. Choose **Create organization**.
3. Enter your company name and website.
4. Save.

You become the **Owner**, which is the role with full control over everything in the workspace.

You can be in **10** organizations at once, counting your Personal workspace. That means at most **9** company organizations. Leave one to create or join another.

## Before you start

You need an account on a work email address rather than a personal one. If you signed up with a personal address, add your work address first. See [Verify a work email](/help/business-basics/work-email).

## Finish the setup

- Add your logo and a short description so candidates recognise you.
- Check the website link, since it appears on your public company profile.
- Invite the people who will help you hire.

Your details show up on job posts and on your company page. See [Public company profile](/help/business-basics/org-profile-public).

## Already have one?

If someone at your company set the workspace up before you, ask them to invite you instead of creating a second organization. You can also ask to join from the organization screen, which is covered in [Join requests](/help/business-basics/join-requests).

# Verify a work email

Required to post jobs.

Employer features need an account tied to your company email address, which is how we keep job posts trustworthy.

## Why it is required

Employer features need a verified company email (not a personal inbox like Gmail). That helps keep job posts trustworthy. It is not a claim that you own your company website domain. You must still be affiliated with the company you represent. Impersonation and fake affiliation are not allowed under the [Terms of Use](https://worklittle.com/terms-of-use).

See also [Do we verify our company domain?](/help/business-basics/work-email-not-domain-claim).

## Add and verify yours

1. Go to [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).
2. Sign in, or create an account using your company address.
3. Enter the six digit code we email you.
4. Your address is verified straight away.

If you see the message "Work email required", this is the step to complete.

## Which addresses work

- Addresses on your company's own domain are ideal.
- Personal addresses from consumer email providers are not accepted for employer features.
- Small company without a custom domain? Reach out through the help option and we will sort it out with you.

## Code never arrives

- Check your spam and quarantine folders.
- Corporate filters sometimes hold outside mail, so ask your IT team to allow email from Worklittle.
- Request a new code. Old codes stop working once a new one is sent.

Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Invite teammates

Send invites by email.

Bring recruiters, hiring managers, and interviewers into your workspace so everyone works from the same pipeline.

## Send an invite

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Choose **Invite**.
3. Enter their work email address.
4. Pick a role for them.
5. Send.

They get an email with a link that adds them to your organization.

## Picking the right role

Give people the least access that lets them do their job. **Can edit** suits most recruiters and hiring managers. **Can comment** works well for interviewers who only need to leave feedback. **Can chat** is right for everyday employees who should not see the pipeline.

Full details of what each role can open, edit, and ask chat about are in [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions).

You can change someone's role later without re-inviting them.

## Pending invites

Invited people appear in your member list marked as pending until they accept. If someone never sees the invite, ask them to check spam, then resend it. Double check the address for typos, since invites go exactly where you typed.

## They already have an account

That is fine. Accepting simply adds your organization to their account. People can belong to more than one company, and they choose which one they are working in. See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization).

Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Roles and permissions

What Owner, Full access, Can edit, Can comment, Can view, and Can chat can each do.

Every teammate in Worklittle Business has a role. The role decides which pages they see, what they can change, and how much the chat assistant is allowed to know about your company.

## The six roles at a glance

| Role | In one sentence |
| --- | --- |
| **Owner** | Full control of the company workspace, including handing ownership to someone else. |
| **Full access** | Runs the team, billing, settings, and hiring data. Same day-to-day power as Owner except ownership transfer. |
| **Can edit** | Posts jobs, moves candidates and employees, edits calendars and documents, runs hiring workflows. |
| **Can comment** | Sees hiring and people data, leaves notes and suggestions, but cannot publish or overwrite most records alone. |
| **Can view** | Read-only across jobs, candidates, employees, and related pages. |
| **Can chat** | A personal employee experience: chat, own profile, own calendar, own documents, and internal job openings - not the hiring pipeline. |

## What each role can open

These are the main areas of [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business):

| Area | Can chat | Can view | Can comment | Can edit | Full access / Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chat, You (profile), Plugins, Automations | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Calendar (own) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Documents (own files / signing) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Jobs, Candidates, Employees, Surveys | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization) page | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| API keys | No | View | View | Manage | Manage |
| Webhooks | No | No | No | Yes | Yes |
| Billing, Usage, Limits | No | No | No | No | Yes |

If a page is hidden for someone's role, it is not a bug. The sidebar only shows what that role is allowed to use.

## Can chat keeps company data private

**Can chat** is built for everyday employees, not recruiters.

- They do **not** see Jobs, Candidates, Employees, Surveys, or Organization in the sidebar.
- Business chat for Can chat is a **personal assistant**. It can help with their own profile, PTO and employment details that belong to them, and internal openings at their company.
- It **cannot** pull the candidate pipeline, employee lists, billing, org settings, or other people's private records - even if they ask in chat.
- They can apply to **internal** roles their company has posted.

That is intentional. Giving someone Can chat lets them use Worklittle at work without opening hiring or HR data to them.

## Calendars and who can edit whom

- **Can chat** can manage **their own** calendar (availability, sick, PTO, and similar self entries).
- They cannot freely rewrite other people's schedules. Editing someone else's calendar needs **Can edit** or higher.
- In larger companies (more than about 15 people on the roster), Can chat usually only sees teammates in **their own department** on the team calendar. If they have no department set, they may only see themselves.
- In smaller companies, Can chat may see the whole team calendar for awareness, still without edit rights on other people's days.
- **Can view** and above can see the wider roster. **Can comment** can propose some changes. **Can edit** and above can make the changes stick.

## Hiring and notes

- **Can view** can read jobs and candidates but not change them.
- **Can comment** can leave notes and propose updates that an editor accepts.
- **Can edit** can post and publish jobs, move candidates through stages, edit employees, and send stage emails.
- **Full access** and **Owner** can also manage members, join requests, branding, billing, and spend limits.

## Documents

- Everyone from **Can chat** up can open Documents for their own uploads and for papers shared with them to sign.
- Creating and editing organization HR documents needs **Can edit** or higher.

## Choosing a role for someone

- Everyday employee who needs chat, PTO, and internal jobs - **Can chat**
- Leader who should see the pipeline but not change it - **Can view**
- Interviewer who leaves feedback - **Can comment**
- Recruiter or hiring manager running the process - **Can edit**
- Ops lead who also handles billing and invites - **Full access**
- The person ultimately responsible for the company account - **Owner**

Give people the least access that still lets them do their job. You can raise a role later in one click.

## Change someone's role

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Find them in the member list.
3. Open their row and pick a new role.

Most changes apply right away. Giving someone Full access, or transferring ownership, waits about a minute. See [Why did Full access take a minute?](/help/business-basics/role-change-delay). If they already have the app open, they may need to refresh before the sidebar updates.

Only Full access and Owner can change roles. Transferring the company to someone else is Owner only. See [Transfer ownership](/help/business-basics/transfer-ownership) and [Invite teammates](/help/business-basics/invite-teammates).

# Switch organizations

Move between Personal and company workspaces.

Every login has a Personal workspace, and you may belong to company organizations. You can be in **10** organizations at once, counting Personal. Switch between them without signing out.

## Organization switcher vs account switcher

| Switcher | What it changes | When to use it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Organization switcher** | Personal vs company workspace inside this login | Same email, different company or Personal billing |
| **Account switcher** | Which email you are signed in as (up to **3**) | Separate personal and work logins |

See [Switch between accounts](/help/account/switch-accounts) if you need a different email.

## Switch

You can switch from any Manage page, or from your profile in the sidebar.

**From a Manage page** (same control on each):

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization), [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys), [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage), [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), or [Webhooks](https://worklittle.com/business/webhooks).
2. Under the page title, open the organization switcher (active organization name with a chevron).
3. Pick **Personal** or the company you want.

**From your profile:**

1. On [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business), look at **your profile** - the account row at the **bottom of the left sidebar** (your name with the active organization under it).
2. Tap the organization name under your name to open the workspace switcher.
3. Pick **Personal** or the company you want.

The whole workspace reloads into that organization. Jobs, candidates, teammates, usage, and billing all change to match.

Manage members and invites on [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).

## On every Manage page

The same organization switcher appears under the title on [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization), [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys), [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage), [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), and [Webhooks](https://worklittle.com/business/webhooks), so you can change workspace without leaving the page you are on.

## Personal workspace

**Personal** is always listed. It is for you as an individual (chat, plugins, job-search API keys, and its own wallet). It is not for hiring.

Switch to a company organization from your profile before posting jobs, managing candidates, or using employer API/MCP tools.

## Billing follows the organization

Each organization has its own amount owed and card. Check [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) only after you are in the right workspace. See [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview).

## Knowing where you are

The active organization name shows under your name on your profile in the left sidebar. Check it before you post a job, email a candidate, or open Billing, since everything you do applies to the organization you are currently in.

## Only Personal listed?

Then you have not joined a company yet. [Create an organization](/help/business-basics/create-organization), ask someone to [invite you](/help/business-basics/invite-teammates), or send a [join request](/help/business-basics/join-requests).

# Join requests

Approve people who ask to join.

Colleagues can ask to join your workspace, and someone with full access approves or declines.

## How someone requests access

A teammate signs in at [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) with their work email and chooses **Request access** for your company. Their request lands with your admins, and no access is granted until it is approved.

They can be in **10** organizations at once, counting Personal. If they are already at that cap, they need to leave one before they can join yours.

## Approve or decline

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Look for pending join requests.
3. Approve and pick a role, or decline.

Approving adds them straight away with the role you chose. Declining leaves them with no access and no data.

## Before you approve

- Recognise the person and the email address.
- Confirm the address is on your company domain.
- Start with the smallest role that works. You can always raise it later.

Roles are explained in [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions).

## Who can act on requests

Handling join requests needs **Full access** or **Owner**. Teammates with edit, comment, view, or chat access will not see the requests at all.

# Remove a teammate

Take someone off the org.

When someone changes roles or leaves the company, remove them so your workspace stays current.

## Remove them

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Find the person in the member list.
3. Open their row and choose to remove them.
4. Confirm.

Access ends immediately. The next time they load the workspace, it is gone.

## What stays behind

Their work does not disappear. Jobs they posted stay live, notes they left stay on candidates, and the pipeline is untouched. You are removing a person's access, not their contributions.

## Before removing

- Reassign any jobs where they were the only recruiter or hiring manager.
- Check whether interviews or offers were waiting on them.
- If they are just moving teams rather than leaving, changing their role may be a better fit than removing them.

## Removing the Owner

The owner cannot be removed while they hold the role. Transfer ownership to someone else first, then remove the old owner. See [Transfer ownership](/help/business-basics/transfer-ownership).

# Transfer ownership

Hand the org to someone else.

Ownership can move to another teammate when you change roles or leave the company.

## Transfer it

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Find the person who should take over. They must already be a member.
3. Choose to transfer ownership to them.
4. Confirm.

The transfer waits about a minute. They become the Owner. You keep **Full access** afterward unless someone changes your role. See [Why did Full access take a minute?](/help/business-basics/role-change-delay).

## Before you transfer

- Tell the person first, since they inherit billing and member management.
- Pick someone who will still be at the company for a while.
- Make sure at least one other teammate has **Full access** as a backstop.

## Good reasons to do it

- You are leaving the company.
- You set the workspace up on someone else's behalf.
- Recruiting has moved to a different owner internally.

## Who can do it

Only the current Owner. If they have already left and cannot sign in, reach out through the help option and we will work with your team to sort it out.

# Public company profile

What candidates may see.

Your company page is what job seekers see when they come across one of your openings.

## What appears publicly

- Your company name and logo
- Your website link
- Your description
- Your currently published jobs

Internal things stay internal. Candidates never see your pipeline, notes, teammates, or anything about other applicants.

## Edit it

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Update the name, logo, website, or description.
3. Save.

Changes show up on your company page and on job posts shortly afterwards.

## Making it work harder

- Upload a clean logo, since it appears next to every job you post.
- Write two or three sentences about what your company does and why someone would want to work there.
- Keep the website link pointed at a page that loads quickly and explains you well.

## Jobs on your page

Only published jobs appear. Drafts stay private and closed roles drop off automatically. See [Publish, close, or delete a job](/help/hiring/publish-close-job).

# Post a job

Write and publish an opening.

Posting a job puts your opening in front of candidates on Worklittle and on your own company page.

## Create the post

1. Go to [Post a job](https://worklittle.com/business/post-job), or open **Jobs** on [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) and choose **Post a job**.
2. Give it a title, which is the single biggest factor in whether people find it.
3. Write the description.
4. Set location, workplace type, and pay.
5. Choose which questions applicants answer.
6. Publish.

## Details you can set

Add only the fields that matter for this role:

- Location and workplace type
- Department and employment type
- Compensation, benefits, and equity
- Visa sponsorship
- Open and close dates (Close date is when applications stop. The job stays open until then.)
- Number of open positions
- Recruiters and hiring managers
- Language and visibility

## Writing a title people search for

Use the plain title candidates would type. "Customer Success Manager" beats "Client Happiness Ninja" every time. Save the personality for the description, and leave internal level codes out of the title.

## What happens after publishing

- The job appears on your [company page](/help/business-basics/org-profile-public).
- It becomes searchable on Worklittle.
- Applicants land in your pipeline at the **Applied** stage.
- You can edit or close it whenever you need to.

Next: [Job description editor](/help/hiring/job-description-editor) and [Application fields and screening](/help/hiring/application-fields).

# Job description editor

Format the posting.

The description editor gives you proper formatting so your posting reads well instead of arriving as a wall of text.

## Formatting you can use

- Headings to break the post into sections
- Bold and italic for emphasis
- Bulleted and numbered lists
- Links to your team page or product

The toolbar sits above the editor, and the usual keyboard shortcuts work too.

## A structure that works

1. **About the role** in two or three sentences.
2. **What you will do**, as four to six bullets.
3. **What we are looking for**, split into must haves and nice to haves.
4. **About the team** or the company.
5. **Pay and benefits**, which lifts response rates noticeably.

## Pasting from elsewhere

Pasting from a document usually keeps your headings and lists intact. Give it a quick scan afterwards for stray formatting, especially anything copied out of a PDF.

## Writing tips

- Keep it under about 700 words. Long posts lose readers.
- Write "you" rather than "the successful candidate".
- Cut requirements you would happily waive for a great person, since long lists put good applicants off.
- Say whether the role is remote, hybrid, or on-site right up front.

# Locations, salary, and workplace

Set where and how people work.

These three details are the first things candidates look for, and filling them in gets your job found.

## Location

Add the city or office where the role sits. Locations you create are saved for reuse, so posting your next role in the same office takes one click.

Location powers map search and nearby job alerts on Worklittle, which makes it one of the highest impact fields on the whole form.

## Workplace type

| Option | Means |
| --- | --- |
| **Remote** | Work from anywhere, subject to whatever limits you state in the description. |
| **Hybrid** | A mix of office and home. Say how many days if you can. |
| **On-site** | In the office or on location. |

If remote is limited to certain countries or time zones, spell that out in the description so nobody applies by mistake.

## Compensation

Enter a range rather than a single figure, and pick the right currency and period.

Posting pay is worth doing. It is required in a growing number of places, it cuts out mismatched conversations, and posts with a range consistently draw more applicants. You can also mark whether the role offers equity.

## Employment type and the rest

Choose from full-time, part-time, internship, contract, temporary, or volunteer. Add department, benefits, and visa sponsorship where they apply. Every field you fill makes your job easier to find in filtered searches.

# Application fields and screening

Ask candidates the right questions.

You decide what applicants have to provide, from the basics through to your own screening questions.

## What is included by default

Every application starts with name, email, phone, resume, and cover letter. Name, email, and phone always stay. You can drop the resume or cover letter if they are not useful for this role.

## Questions you can add

On [Post a job](https://worklittle.com/business/post-job), open **Questions** and choose **Add field**:

- LinkedIn profile
- GitHub profile
- Portfolio or personal website
- Visa status
- Language proficiency
- Your own **Custom question**

## Custom questions

Choose **Add field**, then **Custom question**, and pick how it should be answered:

| Type | Good for |
| --- | --- |
| Short answer | Notice period, salary expectations |
| Long answer | Why this role, a short writing sample |
| Multiple choice | Pick one from a fixed list |
| Checkbox | Pick several |
| Number | Years of experience |
| Date | Earliest start date |
| File | Portfolio or work sample |
| URL | A link to something specific |

Turn on **Required** in the question’s **⋯** menu when applicants must answer. That may add an asterisk (*) at the end of the title in the editor as a shortcut - you can delete it, and typing one at the end of a title (then pressing Enter or clicking away) also marks the question required. Applicants see the required marker from the form itself, not as part of your question text.

## Screening answers

On a question you can set the ideal answer, and optionally auto reject applicants who do not meet it. Use this sparingly and only for genuine hard requirements, such as a licence the job legally needs. Over-filtering quietly removes people you would have wanted to talk to.

## Keep it short

Every extra question loses applicants. A good rule is the basics plus two questions you will genuinely read. Anything else can wait for a screening call.

# Publish, close, or delete a job

Control visibility.

A job moves between draft, published, and closed depending on where you are in the process.

## The three states

| State | Who sees it | Can people apply? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Draft** | Your team only | No |
| **Published** | Everyone | Yes |
| **Closed** | Nobody publicly | No |

## Publish

Finish the details and choose **Publish**. The job appears on your company page and in Worklittle search within a few minutes. Editing a live job is fine, and changes appear without republishing.

## Close

Close a job when the role is filled or paused. It stops accepting applications and drops off your public page, while everyone already in your pipeline stays exactly where they are.

Closing is nearly always the right move for a finished role, because it preserves your hiring history.

## Delete

Deleting removes the job and cannot be undone. Save it for genuine mistakes, like a duplicate post or a test entry. If real people applied, close it instead so you keep their applications and your record of the search.

# Jobs board and pipeline

See all your openings.

The Jobs page at worklittle.com/business is the overview of every role your company is hiring for.

## What you see

Each row is one job with its title, location, status, and how many candidates are in play. From here you can spot the role that has gone quiet and the one that needs attention today.

## Finding a job quickly

- Search by title.
- Filter by status to separate live roles from drafts and closed ones.
- Sort by newest, or by candidate count to see where the volume is.

## Acting from the list

Open a row to edit the posting, view its candidates, close it, or duplicate it as the starting point for a similar role. You can also select several jobs at once to source the same candidate into all of them.

## Jobs and candidates together

Every applicant is attached to a job, so opening a role takes you straight to its pipeline. To look across all roles at once, use [Candidates overview](/help/hiring/candidates-overview).

# Candidates overview

Track everyone in your funnel.

The Candidates page brings every person across every job into one place.

## Who shows up here

- People who applied to your published jobs
- People you sourced yourself
- People you imported from a spreadsheet or another tool

Everyone carries their current stage, the job or jobs they are attached to, and when they last moved.

## Finding people

- Search by name or email.
- Filter by job or by stage.
- Sort by newest applicant or by most recent activity.

The layout is a table, so you can rearrange columns to suit how your team works.

## Opening a candidate

Click any row to see their resume, their answers to your application questions, their contact details, the notes your team has left, and their full history through your stages.

## Working in bulk

Select several people to move them together, source them onto another job, or act on them at once. That saves real time after a first pass through a fresh batch of applications.

Next: [Candidate stages](/help/hiring/candidate-stages).

# Candidate stages

Sourced through Offer, and everything after.

Stages are the steps of your hiring process, and every candidate sits in exactly one of them per job.

## The default stages

| Stage | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| **Sourced** | You found them. They have not applied. |
| **Applied** | They submitted an application. |
| **Rejected** | You are not moving forward with them. |
| **Phone screening** | A first conversation with a recruiter. |
| **Technical interview** | A skills or craft interview. |
| **Team match** | Meeting the team they would join. |
| **Offer** | An offer is out or being prepared. |
| **Denied** | They turned you down. |
| **Employee** | They accepted and joined. |
| **Offboarding** | They are on their way out. |
| **Alumni** | They used to work here. |

The last four are the workforce end of the list, which is why your board keeps making sense after someone is hired rather than dropping them.

## Adding your own stages

If your process has a step the defaults do not cover, add a custom stage for it. Custom stages appear in the list just after **Rejected**, and they behave exactly like the built-in ones.

Add one when a step genuinely changes what happens next. Extra stages that everyone skips past just make the board harder to read.

## Where people start

Applicants land in **Applied** on their own. Anyone you add yourself, whether sourced or imported, starts in **Sourced** until you move them along.

## After the offer

When someone accepts and joins, move them to **Employee** and they show up in your workforce records. **Offboarding** and **Alumni** cover what comes after, so your hiring columns stay focused on open searches.

## Using stages well

- Move people the same day something happens, so the board reflects reality.
- Reject clearly rather than leaving people parked, especially if you have [stage emails](/help/hiring/stage-email-templates) set up.
- Someone can sit at a different stage on two different jobs, which is exactly what you want when a candidate is in for more than one role.
page_text./help/hiring/move-candidates:
Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Move candidates between stages

Update progress.

Moving someone forward or out takes a couple of clicks from anywhere you see them.

## Move one person

1. Open **Candidates** or the job's pipeline.
2. Find the person.
3. Open their stage control and pick the new stage.

It saves immediately and everyone on your team sees it.

## Move several at once

Select the people you want, then apply the new stage to all of them. This is the fastest way to clear a first pass, moving your yes pile to phone screening and the rest to rejected in two actions.

## Emails that go with a move

If you have set up a template for a stage, moving someone into it can send that email automatically. Check which stages are wired up before a bulk move so nobody gets a surprise message. See [Stage email templates](/help/hiring/stage-email-templates).

## Fixing a mistake

Move them back. The stage change is not permanent and their history stays intact. If an email already went out, it cannot be recalled, so a quick personal note is the best repair.

## Candidates on several jobs

Stages are per job. Moving someone forward on one role leaves their stage on another role untouched, which is what you want when they are in two processes at once.

Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Notes and bookmarks on candidates

Keep hiring context.

Notes keep interview impressions and decisions attached to the person instead of buried in someone's inbox.

## Add a note

1. Open the candidate.
2. Go to their notes.
3. Write what happened and save.

Notes are shared with your team and stamped with who wrote them and when.

## What is worth writing down

- What you covered in the interview and how it went
- Specific strengths and specific concerns
- Salary expectations and notice period
- What the next step is and who owns it
- Why you decided what you decided

That last one matters most. Six weeks later, nobody remembers why a promising candidate was passed over.

## Marking people to revisit

Bookmark the candidates you want to come back to, so a strong runner up is easy to find when the next similar role opens. It beats scrolling through an old pipeline hoping to recognise a name.

## Who can see notes

Anyone on your team with at least comment access. Notes are never visible to candidates, though the sensible habit is to write everything as if it might one day be read out loud.
page_text./help/hiring/stage-email-templates:
Coding agent documentation index
Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Stage email templates

Auto messages per stage.

Write an email once per stage, and candidates hear from you the moment they move.

## Set one up

1. Open the job, or your organization's email templates.
2. Pick the stage the email belongs to.
3. Write the subject and the body.
4. Save it as a named template.

You can keep more than one template per stage and choose between them, which is handy when a technical role and a sales role need a different tone.

## Personalising with variables

Insert placeholders and they fill in per person, so one template covers everybody:

- The candidate's name
- The job title
- Your company name

Your logo can be attached so the email looks like it came from you rather than from a tool.

## Which stages send on their own

Each stage has a **Notify candidate** switch, and two of them start out on:

- **Applied** is always on and cannot be turned off. Every applicant gets a confirmation that you received their application, which is the one message candidates most notice missing.
- **Sourced** is on by default, so people you add yourself hear from you. You can switch this one off.

Every other stage starts off. Turn on the ones where a message genuinely helps, such as an invitation at **Phone screening** or a kind, brief note at **Rejected**.

## Before you turn one on

- Send yourself a test and read it on a phone.
- Check the tone. Automated does not have to mean cold.
- Remember that a bulk stage move sends the email to everyone in that move.

Coding agent documentation index

# Offers

Send and track offers.

The Offer stage is where you prepare, send, and follow up on an offer without losing track of who is waiting on what.

## Move someone to Offer

Change their stage to **Offer** once you have decided. That signals to everyone on your team that this person is in the final step and nobody else should be moving them along.

## Preparing the paperwork

Offer letter templates are available in your documents area, covering standard employment offers, internships, and volunteer agreements. They fill in the candidate's name, the role, and your company details for you, so you edit the terms rather than retyping the letter.

## Keeping track

- Note the date the offer went out.
- Note the deadline for a response.
- Record any negotiation in the candidate's notes so the next conversation starts from the right place.

If the candidate turns the offer down, move them to **Denied** with a note on why. That is the data that improves your next search. **Rejected** is for the decisions you make.

## When they accept

Move them to **Employee** once they accept and start. They shift from your hiring columns into your workforce records, so your pipeline stays focused on open searches. See [Candidate stages](/help/hiring/candidate-stages).

Coding agent documentation index

# Import candidates

Bring people in from elsewhere.

Move people you are already talking to into Worklittle so your whole pipeline lives in one place.

## Add someone by hand

1. Open [Candidates](https://worklittle.com/business/candidates).
2. Choose to add a candidate.
3. Pick the job they should be attached to.
4. Enter their name, email, and anything else you have.
5. Save.

They land at the **Sourced** stage, ready for you to move along.

## Bringing in a list

Coming from a spreadsheet or another tool? Get your file down to one person per row with clear columns for name and email first. Attach resumes afterwards on each candidate's page.

Clean the list before you import. Duplicates and stale addresses are much harder to untangle once they are in your pipeline.

## What to include

- Name and email at minimum
- Phone number and LinkedIn where you have them
- The job they belong to
- A note on where they came from and what stage the conversation is really at

## After importing

- Move anyone mid conversation to the stage that reflects reality, not **Sourced**.
- Add a note with the history so far, so the rest of your team is not starting blind.
- Watch out for someone who also applied directly, and keep one record rather than two.
