# AI tools and hiring compliance

What Worklittle Business does and does not decide when you use AI in recruiting, and what your organization remains responsible for.

Worklittle Business includes AI that helps draft, organize, and summarize hiring work. It does not decide who to hire. Your organization remains the employer and controller of candidate decisions. This page is a practical map of that split so you can stay defensible under U.S. and EU rules that regulate automated employment tools.

## What Worklittle does

- Drafts job posts, emails, notes, and summaries you ask for in chat.
- Helps organize candidates, stages, surveys, and documents you already control.
- Surfaces information you or your teammates put into Worklittle Business.

Worklittle does **not** automatically screen, score, rank, or reject people for employment without a human on your team making the decision. See also [Business chat assistant](/help/business-basics/business-chat) and our [Terms of Service](https://worklittle.com/terms-of-use) §7.

## What you remain responsible for

As the employer (and data controller for organization data), you are responsible for:

- Having a lawful basis to process candidate and employee information, and giving any notices your local law requires.
- Equal opportunity, anti-discrimination, recordkeeping, and background-screening rules that apply to you.
- Keeping **meaningful human review** over hiring, promotion, discipline, and similar decisions when AI helped prepare materials.
- Not using Worklittle to screen people using characteristics protected by law, or to build a proxy for those characteristics (for example ZIP code as a stand-in for a protected class).
- Notices to candidates or employees when your jurisdiction requires disclosure that AI or an automated decision tool was used.

## Laws teams commonly ask about (2025–2027)

This is not legal advice. Rules change by city and state. Typical obligations employers ask about when using AI in hiring:

| Law / rule | Who it usually binds | What it generally expects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Illinois HB 3773** (in force 2026) | Employers using AI in employment decisions | Effect-based discrimination prohibitions; notice when AI is used in covered employment decisions |
| **California FEHA ADS regulations** (2025) | Employers using automated decision systems | Broad coverage of tools that screen, score, rank, or recommend - even when a human has final say; anti-bias expectations |
| **NYC Local Law 144** | Employers using automated employment decision tools in NYC | Bias audits and candidate notices for covered AEDTs |
| **Colorado ADMT rules** (from 2027) | Developers and deployers of automated decision-making technology | Documentation, point-of-interaction notice, and post-adverse-outcome disclosures for covered employment decisions |
| **EU AI Act Article 50** | Providers and deployers interacting with people in the EU | Transparency when people interact with AI; high-risk employment system duties are on a later timeline after the Digital Omnibus |

If you operate in more than one of these places, follow the strictest rule that applies to that candidate or role.

## Practical checklist inside Worklittle Business

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization) and confirm the right people have hiring access only.
2. Keep pipeline decisions on [Candidates](https://worklittle.com/business/candidates) with a human moving stages - do not treat chat suggestions as a final reject or hire.
3. Tell candidates, in your careers site or outreach, when AI helped evaluate or communicate, if your jurisdiction requires that notice.
4. Keep notes of who decided and why on sensitive steps (offer, reject, promotion).
5. Review [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions) so AI chat cannot surface data to teammates who should not see it.
6. Read [Compliance and security](/help/privacy-safety/compliance-and-security) for how access and infrastructure are handled.

## Data protection roles

For organization data you put into Worklittle Business, you act as the controller (or “business”) and Worklittle acts as the processor (or “service provider”), processing that data on your instructions. Where a data processing agreement is required, email [privacy@worklittle.com](mailto:privacy@worklittle.com). Candidate applications you receive through Worklittle are still your hiring records once they are in your organization.

## Where to go next

- [Candidates overview](/help/hiring/candidates-overview)
- [Application fields and screening](/help/hiring/application-fields)
- [Terms of Service](https://worklittle.com/terms-of-use) (employer responsibilities)
- [Privacy policy](https://worklittle.com/privacy)
- Product questions: [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com)

# Employees overview

Your team roster in one table you can sort, filter, and edit.

**Employees** is the roster of everyone who works at your organization. It looks like a spreadsheet, but every cell saves for your whole team the moment you change it.

## Where to find it

1. Open [Employees](https://worklittle.com/business/employees) on Worklittle Business, or go to [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) and select **Employees** under **HR** in the left sidebar.

If you do not see the sidebar on a phone, tap the menu button in the top left corner.

## What each row shows

Every row is one person. Common columns include:

- **Name**, **Email**, and **Phone**
- **Title** and **Department**
- **Status** and **Start date**
- **Location**, **Job type**, and **Workplace type**
- **Compensation** and any benefits you track

You can add your own columns too, such as "Badge number" or "T-shirt size". Use the **+** button at the right end of the column headers.

## Ways to work with the table

- **Sort** by selecting a column header menu and choosing an order.
- **Edit in place** by clicking a cell and typing. There is no separate save button.
- **Open a profile** by selecting a person's name. See [Employee profiles](/help/team-hr/employee-profiles).
- **Select many rows** with the checkboxes to email, export, or move them at once. See [Bulk employee actions](/help/team-hr/bulk-employee-actions).

## Adding people

- **Add manually** when you want to type someone in yourself.
- **Hire from Candidates** to move an applicant into the roster without retyping their details.

New people appear at the top of the table so you can finish filling in their information right away.

## Related articles

- [Employee profiles](/help/team-hr/employee-profiles)
- [Calendar and attendance](/help/team-hr/calendar-attendance)
- [Documents overview](/help/team-hr/documents-overview)

# Employee profiles

View and update one person's details, pay history, and documents.

A profile is the full page for one person on your team. It gathers their contact details, role, pay history, and paperwork in one place.

## Open a profile

1. Go to **Employees** in the left sidebar.
2. Select the person's name in the table.

The profile opens with their photo, title, and department at the top.

## What you can change

- **Contact details** such as email, phone, and location
- **Role details** such as title, department, job type, and workplace type
- **Dates** such as start date and end date
- **Compensation**, including a history of past changes
- **Links** such as LinkedIn, GitHub, and a personal website
- **Notes** that only your team can see

Edits save as you make them. Anyone else viewing the profile sees the update without refreshing.

## Pay history

Compensation keeps a running history instead of overwriting the old number. Select the compensation field to see previous amounts and when each change took effect. This makes review season and audits much easier.

## Documents on a profile

Offer letters, policies, and signed forms linked to a person show their status right on the profile. To send something new, see [E-sign documents](/help/team-hr/e-sign-documents).

## Who can edit

Editing depends on your role in the organization. If fields look read-only, ask an owner or admin to raise your access on [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization). See [Organization details](/help/business-basics/organization-details).

# Calendar and attendance

Track shifts, time off, and who is present each day.

**Calendar** shows who is working, who is out, and when. You can view the whole team side by side or zoom into one person.

## Two views

| View | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| Roster | Seeing the whole team for a day or week in columns |
| Individual | Planning one person's shifts in detail |

Switch between them from the toolbar at the top of the page. Select a person's name in the roster to jump into their individual view.

## Entry types

Each block on the calendar has a type:

- **In person** and **Remote** for working time
- **Sick** and **PTO** for time off
- **Available** and **Unavailable** for openings and blackouts

Colors match the type so you can scan a week quickly.

## Add or change a block

1. Open **Calendar** in the left sidebar.
2. Drag on an empty part of a day to draw a new block, or select an existing block to edit it.
3. Pick the type, adjust the start and end times, and save.

To repeat a shift, use the repeat option in the editor. You can set a weekly pattern and edit a single day later without breaking the rest of the series.

## Time off and balances

Sick and PTO entries count against a person's remaining balance. If a request would take the balance below zero and the person cannot approve their own time, the entry waits for a manager. See [Approve schedule changes](/help/team-hr/approve-schedule-changes).

## Related articles

- [Approve schedule changes](/help/team-hr/approve-schedule-changes)
- [Automations overview](/help/automations/automations-overview) for auto-filling coverage when someone calls in sick

# Approve schedule changes

Accept or deny time off and shift edits that need a manager.

Some calendar changes wait for approval instead of applying right away. This keeps schedules accurate when people update their own availability.

## What needs approval

A change is queued for review when:

- Someone edits a calendar other than their own without edit access
- Someone books sick time or PTO that would take their remaining balance below zero

Everything else applies immediately.

## Review pending changes

1. Open **Calendar** in the left sidebar.
2. Pending blocks appear with a review banner over the roster.
3. Select the banner to see the requests.
4. Choose **Approve** to apply the change or **Deny** to discard it.

Approved blocks turn into normal calendar entries. Denied blocks disappear and the person's schedule stays as it was.

## Tips

- Check the calendar before approving a day that already looks thin on coverage.
- Approving sick time or PTO updates the person's remaining balance right away.
- If you approve by mistake, open the block and delete it, then let the person know.

## Automate the follow-up

You can build an automation that reacts to a sick day, fills the shift, and sends a message to the team. See [Create an automation](/help/automations/create-automation).

# Surveys overview

Ask your team or candidates questions and collect answers in one table.

**Surveys** let you ask a group of people a set of questions and read every answer in one place. Use them for onboarding checklists, engagement pulses, exit interviews, or candidate screening.

## Where to find it

Open [Surveys](https://worklittle.com/business/surveys) on Worklittle Business, or select **Surveys** under **HR** in the left sidebar at [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).

The page lists every survey you have created, plus a gallery of templates you can start from.

## How a survey works

1. You build the questions. See [Create a survey](/help/team-hr/create-survey).
2. You choose who can answer. See [Invite people to a survey](/help/team-hr/invite-to-survey).
3. People open a link and fill it in.
4. Answers land in a results table. See [View survey responses](/help/team-hr/survey-responses).

## Moving through questions

On the answer form, people can move without using the on-screen arrows:

- **Scroll** down or up, or use the **arrow keys**, to go to the next or previous question
- **Enter** also goes to the next question (or submits on the last one)
- **Delete** (or Backspace outside a text box) goes to the previous question
- For multiple choice, **Tab** moves between options, then **Space** or a click selects

Typing in a text box still works as usual. Delete and Backspace only edit text while the cursor is in that field.

## Anonymous answers

A survey can collect answers without names attached. Anonymous responses show as "Anonymous" in the results table, which is useful for honest feedback. Decide this before you send the link, because it changes what people are willing to say.

## Good uses

- **Onboarding**: confirm a new hire has equipment, accounts, and a buddy
- **Pulse checks**: one or two questions each month
- **Exit interviews**: capture why someone is leaving
- **Candidate screening**: ask the same questions of every applicant

# Create a survey

Build questions, set which ones are required, and save a draft.

Building a survey works like filling out a short form builder. No setup or code is needed.

## Start a new survey

1. Go to [Surveys](https://worklittle.com/business/surveys).
2. Select **New survey**, or pick a template from the gallery to start with questions already written.
3. Give the survey a clear name. People see this at the top of the form.

## Background color

In the survey editor, open the color control to the left of Undo.

| Option | What respondents see |
| --- | --- |
| None | Normal light or dark mode (default for new surveys) |
| Multicolor | Each question type gets its own background color |
| A solid color | That color stays for the whole survey |
| Custom color | Tap **+** at the end of the palette to pick any color. Custom swatches are saved for your organization and show up for everyone on the team. Remove one with the small **×** on the swatch. |

When you pick a color other than None, the editor itself switches to a light-on-color look so you can preview contrast.

## Question types

| Type | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Short answer | Names, job titles, one-line replies |
| Long answer | Feedback and open comments |
| Multiple choice | One option from a list |
| Checkboxes | Several options from a list |
| Yes or no | Simple confirmations |
| Number | Ratings, counts, amounts |
| Date | Start dates, deadlines |
| File upload | Certificates, receipts, IDs |

Open a question’s **⋯** menu and use **Details** to add a short description (good for examples) or **Attach image** (JPG, PNG, WebP, or GIF, up to 5 MB). You can preview the image in the editor right away; it is uploaded when you save the survey. The image shows under the question title for respondents, and they can click it to open a larger preview.

## Required questions

Turn on **Required** in a question’s **⋯** menu for anything you truly need. That may add an asterisk (*) at the end of the title in the editor as a shortcut - you can delete it, and typing one at the end of a title (then pressing Enter or clicking away) also marks the question required. Respondents see the required marker from the form itself, not as part of your question text. Everything else stays optional. Long surveys with many required questions get abandoned, so keep the required list short.

## Reorder and remove

- Drag a question to move it.
- Use the question menu to duplicate or delete it.
- Put the easiest questions first so people build momentum.

## Before you send

- Read the survey out loud once. Awkward wording is easier to hear than to see.
- Open the public link yourself and answer it as a test.
- Then continue to [Invite people to a survey](/help/team-hr/invite-to-survey).

# Invite people to a survey

Who you can share a survey with and how the link works.

Sharing controls two things at once. It decides who is allowed to open the survey and how they receive the link.

## Open Invite responders

1. Go to [Surveys](https://worklittle.com/business/surveys) and open the survey you want to send.
2. Select **Invite people**.
3. In **Invite responders**, choose who can answer under **Invite people**, then copy the link or send invites.

## Choose who can answer

| Setting | Who gets in |
| --- | --- |
| **Only people invited** | Just the people you name. Organization owners, Full access, and Can edit teammates can still open and answer it to preview. Everyone else is turned away. |
| **Anyone with the link** | No sign-in needed, so this is the one for candidate questionnaires and anything public. |
| **Everyone at {your company}** | Any of your teammates who opens the link. |

Changing this later does not delete answers you already collected.

## Who you can invite

Once you have picked the audience, add the people:

- **Employees** from your roster
- **Candidates** in your pipeline
- **Whole departments**, so everyone in that department gets access without naming them one by one
- **Email addresses** typed in directly, including people outside your organization

Mixing these is fine. A new-hire checklist might go to one employee, while an exit survey goes to a whole department.

## Sending the link

- **Copy link** puts the survey URL on your clipboard so you can paste it into email or chat.
- **Invite by email** sends the link directly from Worklittle.

The link stays the same each time, so you can pin it in a group chat or add it to an onboarding checklist.

After someone submits, opening the link again shows **Submitted!** on that browser (and for signed-in teammates, across devices too). They can tap **Edit response** at the bottom to change their answers and submit again.

## Closing a survey

Set the survey status to closed when you are done collecting. People who open the link afterwards see a message saying the survey is no longer accepting answers. Your existing results stay available.

## Related articles

- [Create a survey](/help/team-hr/create-survey)
- [View survey responses](/help/team-hr/survey-responses)

# View survey responses

Read results, spot patterns, and export answers.

Every answer lands in a results table where one row is one person's submission and one column is one question.

## Open the results

1. Go to [Surveys](https://worklittle.com/business/surveys).
2. Select the survey.
3. Choose the **Responses** view.

The name column stays pinned on the left as you scroll sideways through the questions.

## Summary versus individual answers

- The **summary** rolls up counts for choice questions, so you can see at a glance that 18 people picked "Yes" and 4 picked "No".
- The **table** shows each person's full submission, which is what you want when reading open comments.

Anonymous submissions appear as "Anonymous" in the name column but still show their answers.

## Clean up and export

- Select rows with the checkboxes to delete test submissions.
- Export the results to a spreadsheet file when you want to chart them or share outside Worklittle.

Exports include one column per question, matching the table you see on screen.

## Reading results well

- Look for questions many people skipped. That usually means the wording was unclear.
- Read open comments before looking at the numbers so the counts do not bias you.
- Share a short summary back with the people who answered. Response rates go up the next time you ask.

# Documents overview

Keep HR files, policies, and templates in one place.

**Documents** is where you write, store, and send the paperwork your team needs. Offer letters, handbooks, policies, and signed forms all live here.

# Create and edit documents

Write policies, letters, and handbooks in the built-in editor.

The document editor works like a familiar word processor. Type, format, and your work saves automatically.

## Create a document

1. Go to [Documents](https://worklittle.com/business/documents).
2. Select **New document**, or pick a template to start with wording already in place.
3. Give it a title at the top of the page.

## Formatting basics

- **Headings** break a long policy into sections people can scan.
- **Bold** and **italic** for emphasis, used sparingly.
- **Bulleted and numbered lists** for steps and requirements.
- **Tables** for things like pay bands or leave allowances.

Select text to bring up the formatting toolbar.

## Working with others

Share a document with a teammate and you will both see edits as they happen, including each other's cursor. This is faster than emailing versions back and forth.

## Uploaded PDFs

When you upload a PDF instead of writing one, you get a different set of tools. You can add text boxes, draw, place a signature, and erase marks. This is useful for forms you receive from outside your company.

## Download and send

- **Download** saves a copy to your computer.
- **Share** gives specific people access inside Worklittle.
- **Send for signature** starts the signing flow. See [E-sign documents](/help/team-hr/e-sign-documents).

# Document templates

Start from a ready-made HR document instead of a blank page.

Templates give you a complete first draft so you only need to adjust the details that are specific to your company.

## Browse the gallery

1. Go to [Documents](https://worklittle.com/business/documents).
2. The template gallery appears above or alongside your existing documents.
3. Hover a template to preview what is inside before you commit.

## Use a template

1. Select the template you want.
2. A new document is created from it, already filled with the standard wording.
3. Replace the placeholder details such as company name, role, dates, and amounts.
4. Rename the document so it is easy to find later.

The original template is untouched, so you can use it again for the next person.

## Make your own reusable starting point

Write a document once with your standard wording, then duplicate it each time you need a new copy. Naming it clearly, for example "Offer letter master copy", keeps your list tidy.

## A quick warning

Templates are starting points, not legal advice. Have a lawyer review any document that creates an obligation, especially offer letters, contracts, and separation agreements.

# E-sign documents

Send a document for signature and track who has signed.

You can collect a signature on a document without printing anything. The signer opens a link, signs on screen, and you get the completed copy back.

## Send for signature

1. Open the document in **Documents**.
2. Select **Share** and choose the signature option.
3. Add the email address of each person who needs to sign.
4. Send.

Each signer gets their own link. They do not need a Worklittle account to sign.

## What the signer sees

- The full document, exactly as you wrote or uploaded it
- A place to draw or type their signature
- A confirm button that records their name and the date

Once they confirm, the document is locked for them and you get the signed version.

## Track status

The document list shows where each signature stands, so you can see who still needs a nudge. Employee profiles also show the signing status of documents linked to that person. See [Employee profiles](/help/team-hr/employee-profiles).

## Common questions

- **Can I fix a typo after sending?** Cancel the request, correct the document, and send it again.
- **Can two people sign the same document?** Yes. Add every signer when you send it.
- **Where is the signed copy?** It stays in **Documents**, and you can download it at any time.

# HR notifications

The alerts you may get about people, schedules, and paperwork.

Worklittle tells you when something needs attention so you do not have to keep checking every page.

## Where notifications appear

Select the bell icon in the top bar of Worklittle Business. The panel lists recent activity grouped by how recently it happened. See [Notifications center](/help/business-basics/notifications-center) for the full tour.

## HR alerts you may see

- A schedule change is waiting for your approval
- Someone booked sick time or PTO
- A document you sent was signed
- A survey received new responses
- A teammate joined or was invited to your organization
- A candidate moved into your employee roster

## Keeping the noise down

- Clear items you have handled so the list stays short.
- If a type of alert is not useful to you, ask an owner or admin whether that workflow can be routed to a different person.

# Bulk employee actions

Update, email, or export many people at once.

When a change affects a whole department, you do not need to edit one row at a time. Select several people and act on all of them together.

## Select people

1. Go to **Employees** in the left sidebar.
2. Use the checkbox at the start of each row to select people.
3. Use the checkbox in the header row to select everything currently shown.

A small action bar appears once you have at least one row selected.

## What you can do in bulk

| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Email | Opens a new message with everyone selected in the blind copy field |
| Export | Downloads the selected rows as a spreadsheet file |
| Move stage | Sets the same workforce stage for everyone selected |
| Bookmark | Flags people so you can find them again quickly |

Deselect everything by selecting the header checkbox twice or pressing Escape.

## Exports

The export includes the standard columns plus any custom columns you added. The file name includes the date and your time zone so downloads do not overwrite each other.

Treat exported files carefully. They contain personal information about your team.

## Before a large change

- Filter or sort first so you are certain the right people are selected.
- Start with a small batch to confirm the result looks right.
- Bulk changes are not undone with a single click, so a quick export beforehand is a cheap safety net.

# Automations overview

Repeat your hiring and HR workflows without doing them by hand.

An automation is a set of steps that runs on its own. Something happens, such as a new application arriving, and Worklittle does what you told it to do next.

## The shape of an automation

Every automation has:

1. **One trigger**, which is the thing that starts it
2. **Steps**, which are the actions that follow in order
3. **An end**, which is where the flow stops

You build this on a canvas, which is a visual board where each step is a card connected by a line.

## Two kinds of trigger

| Trigger | Starts when |
| --- | --- |
| Event | Something happens, such as a candidate applying or someone calling in sick |
| Time | A schedule you choose, such as every Monday morning |

You can narrow an event trigger to a specific company, department, job, title, or person so it does not fire for everyone.

For **Jobs** events, open [Automations](https://worklittle.com/business/automations) and use **Company** to pick your organization (selected by default), other organizations you belong to, popular employers from Worklittle's index, or any company you search. Department and Job filters appear when your own company is selected. Title includes works for every Jobs event. You can also ask Business chat to build the automation - the assistant searches Worklittle's company index for real employers (and will suggest close matches if a name is not listed).

## Steps you can add

- **Email** to send a message
- **Chat** to post a message in Worklittle
- **Delay** to wait before the next step
- **Share document** to send paperwork
- **A/B test** to split people between two paths
- **Grant org access** to give someone access
- **Text** to leave a note on the canvas for your teammates, which never runs

## Everyday examples

- A candidate applies, so send a confirmation email and post to the hiring chat
- Someone books a sick day, so fill the shift and notify the team
- A job is created at your company, so email the hiring team
- A role appears at a company you watch, so run a Chat step to summarize it
- Every Monday, email managers a summary of open roles
- A new hire starts, so share the handbook and the equipment survey

## Next

Ready to build one? See [Create an automation](/help/automations/create-automation).

# Create an automation

Build your first workflow on the canvas, step by step.

You do not need to write anything technical. You pick a starting event, then add the steps that follow.

## Start a new automation

1. Open **Automations** in the left sidebar.
2. Select **New**.
3. On the empty canvas, select the **+** button.
4. Choose **Event** or **Time** as your trigger.
5. Configure the trigger, including any filters such as a company, department, title, or a specific job.

## Add steps

1. Select the **+** below the trigger card.
2. Pick a step such as **Email**, **Chat**, **Delay**, or **Share document**.
3. Fill in the details for that step, such as the recipient and the message.
4. Repeat for each step you want.

Each new step connects automatically to the one above it. The ghost **End** marker moves down as the flow grows.

For Jobs triggers, your current organization is selected under **Company** by default. The dropdown also lists popular employers from Worklittle's index, and you can search any company in the database. Department and Job stay available when your own company is selected.

## Save and turn it on

Select **Save** when the flow looks right. Nothing runs until you save, so you can leave a half-finished automation and come back to it.

Test it by triggering the event yourself, for example by creating or publishing a job on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/business/jobs), or by submitting a test application to your own job posting.

## Splitting the path

Use the **A/B test** step when you want to try two versions of a message. Give each branch a percentage, and the percentages must add up to 100. Each branch then continues with its own steps.

## Let the assistant build it

On [Automations](https://worklittle.com/business/automations), select **Create with AI** to drop a starter prompt into the chat composer already on the page (bottom bar, or sidebar/floating if that is already open). Stay on Automations, edit the prompt, and send. You can also open the automation editor and ask in chat. Review the result and select **Save** yourself. See [Business chat assistant](/help/business-basics/business-chat).

## Tips

- Start small. One trigger and two steps is a complete, useful automation.
- Add a **Text** note on the canvas explaining why the automation exists. Your future self will thank you.
- Filters matter. An unfiltered trigger fires for every job and every department.

# Plugins and connectors

Extend Worklittle Business with the tools your team already uses.

Plugins connect Worklittle to other services so the assistant can act on your behalf in those tools.

## Browse plugins

1. Open **Plugins** in the left sidebar at [Plugins](https://worklittle.com/business/plugins).
2. Use the category chips under the description, or select **See all** on a category, to show the full list on the same page.
3. Select any plugin to read what it does before connecting.

A verified badge means the connector is published and maintained rather than added by hand.

## Connect one

1. Open the plugin.
2. Select **Connect**.
3. Sign in to that service and approve the access it asks for.
4. Return to Worklittle. The plugin now shows as connected.

Only connect plugins you recognize, and read what access is being requested.

## Custom MCP apps

You can also connect your own MCP server as a Custom app from [Plugins](https://worklittle.com/business/plugins). When you're signed in to Worklittle Business, use **Custom app** in the top right, or the Custom apps tile on the All view. After Worklittle checks the server, it shows whether the connection worked. If the app needs you to sign in to that service, follow the prompts on screen.

Developers who need the technical OAuth details can start from the [Plugins](https://worklittle.com/business/plugins) page and the API docs.

## Disconnect

Open the plugin, use its menu, and choose to disconnect. Worklittle stops using that service right away. Anything already saved inside Worklittle stays where it is.

## Something not working

Each plugin has a report option in its menu. Use it to tell us what went wrong, and include what you were trying to do. You can also email [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com). See [Contact support](/help/privacy-safety/contact-support).

# Search in Business

Find jobs, people, chats, and tools from anywhere in the app.

# Logo, banner, and brand color

Make your organization profile and job board look like your company.

Your brand assets appear on your public job board, on shared job links, and inside Worklittle Business for your team.

## Where to change them

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Find the **Logo**, **Banner**, and **Brand color** fields near the top of the profile section.
3. Click the logo or banner to choose **Create with AI...** or **Upload photo**, or drag an image onto the field (from your computer or from a chat image in the floating or sidebar chat). Brand color can be picked from the swatch. Changes appear on your public profile shortly after saving.

## What each one is for

| Asset | Where it shows |
| --- | --- |
| Logo | Job listings, your job board header, shared links |
| Banner | The wide image across the top of your public profile |
| Brand color | Buttons and accents on your public pages |

A square logo works best. Banners are wide, so keep important detail near the center.

## Other profile fields

- **Brand name** is the public-facing name people see, which can differ from your legal name.
- **Overview** is a one-sentence summary of what your company does.
- **Social links** appear as small icons on your profile.

See [Organization details](/help/business-basics/organization-details) for the rest.

## No design file handy

Click the empty logo or banner and choose **Create with AI...**. The chat composer fills with a starting prompt such as “Make a distinctive and recognizable logo for your brand name in a square aspect ratio” or “Make a company banner for your brand name in a 4:1 aspect ratio.” You can also ask the assistant to adjust an existing logo or banner. See [AI brand images](/help/business-basics/ai-brand-images).

# AI brand images

Create or edit your logo or banner by describing what you want in chat.

If you do not have a designer available, you can create a logo or banner from scratch, or describe a change to an existing one, and the assistant will produce a new version.

## Create from Organization

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Click the empty **Logo** or **Banner** field.
3. Choose **Create with AI...**. The chat composer gets a draft prompt using your brand name (or legal name if brand name is empty).
4. Send the message. The assistant generates via the brand image tool, then shows a preview and a confirmation card to apply it to your organization.

If you already have a logo or banner, click it and choose **Edit with AI...** instead.

## How to ask in Chat

1. Open **Chat** in Worklittle Business, or start from Create/Edit with AI on [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Describe what you want created or changed.
3. Review the preview it returns.
4. Accept the confirmation card to apply it to your organization, or ask for another round if it is not right.

Keep asking in the same conversation. The assistant works from the latest version it produced, so follow-up changes build on each other.

## Prompts that work well

```text
Take our current banner and make the background a deeper navy blue.
Keep the logo in the same position and the same size.
```

```text
Create a square version of our logo with a transparent background,
suitable for a profile picture. Do not add any text.
```

```text
Our banner feels crowded. Give it more empty space on the left side
so the headline text on our job board is easy to read.
```

## What to include in your request

- The exact color, in words or as a hex code such as `#0B2545`
- What should stay the same, not just what should change
- Where the image will be used, for example a job board header
- Whether text should appear at all

## Good practice

- Keep an original copy of your real logo outside Worklittle.
- Check the result on both light and dark backgrounds before applying it.
- If your company has brand guidelines, run the result past whoever owns them.

# Organization details

Legal name, job board address, website, and headquarters.

The **Organization** page holds the facts about your company. Some of it is public on your profile and job board, and some is internal.

## Open the page

Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).

## Public profile fields

- **Brand name**, the name candidates see
- **URL slug**, which sets your job board address, for example `worklittle.com/your-brand`

- **Website**
- **Contact email** and **Phone number**

Filling these in makes your listings look more credible to candidates.

## Changing your slug

# Privacy and terms links

Show your own policies on your public organization profile.

You can point candidates at your own privacy policy and terms of service. These links appear alongside your public profile and job board.

## Add the links

1. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).
2. Scroll to **Privacy policy** and **Terms of service**.
3. Paste the full web address for each, starting with `https://`.
4. The links save as you type.

Example values look like `https://company.com/privacy-policy` and `https://company.com/terms-of-service`.

## Why it matters

- Candidates are more comfortable applying when they can see how their information is handled.
- Some regions expect a privacy notice at the point where you collect applicant data.
- It saves your team from answering the same question over email.

## Do not confuse these with Worklittle's policies

These fields are for **your company's** policies. Worklittle's own Privacy policy and Terms of service are at the bottom of [Settings](https://worklittle.com/business). See [Terms and policies](/help/privacy-safety/terms-and-policies).

# Business chat assistant

Ask the employer assistant to do the work for you.

Chat is the first item in Worklittle Business sidebar. You can ask it questions about your data and ask it to make changes for you.

## What you can ask for

- **Posting jobs**: draft a description and publish it
- **Candidates**: summarize applicants, compare them, move them between stages
- **Surveys**: build questions and share the result
- **Documents**: write a policy or an offer letter
- **Automations**: lay out a workflow on the canvas
- **Reports**: pull a table of jobs, candidates, or employees

## Getting better answers

- Say who the output is for, such as a hiring manager or a candidate.
- Give the constraints up front, such as the location, the level, and the pay range.
- Ask for a specific format, such as a table or five bullet points.
- If the first answer is close, reply with one correction rather than starting over.

## Ready-made prompts

Copy-and-paste prompts for common employer tasks are collected in the [Business prompt guide](/help/prompt-guides/business-prompt-guide).

## Check before you send

The assistant drafts quickly, but you are the one publishing. Read job descriptions, offer letters, and candidate messages before they go out. If an answer looks wrong or unsafe, report it. See [Chat reports](/help/privacy-safety/chat-reports).

# API keys

Create a key when an app or an AI agent needs to connect to Worklittle.

An API key is a long password that lets a program use Worklittle on your behalf. Most people never need one. You only need a key if a developer or an AI tool asks for it.

## Do you actually need a key

You do **not** need a key to use the Worklittle apps in your browser. See [When to use the API vs the apps](/help/api/when-to-use-api) if you are unsure.

## Create a key

1. Open [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).
2. Select **API keys** in the left sidebar.
3. Select **Create API key**.
4. Name it after where it will be used, for example "Careers page" or "Slack bot".
5. Copy the full key **now**. It is shown once and never again.

## Keep it safe

- Treat a key like a password. Anyone who has it can act as your organization.
- Paste it into a password manager or hand it to your developer through a secure channel.
- Do not put it in a public document, a spreadsheet shared by link, or a screenshot.
- Never paste it into a chat message with someone you do not know.

## Revoke a key

On the **API keys** page, open the menu on a key's row and choose **Revoke**. It stops working immediately and cannot be brought back.

To replace a key without downtime, create the new one first, give it to whoever is using it, then revoke the old one. More detail is in [Share or rotate an API key](/help/api/share-or-rotate-api-keys).

## Costs

Keys themselves are free. What a key is used for may cost money. See [How does API usage get billed?](/help/api/api-usage-and-billing), [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview), and [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage).

## Related

- [Why is my API key not working?](/help/api/api-key-not-working)
- [How do I give a developer access?](/help/api/hand-off-api-to-developer)
- [What can my API key do?](/help/api/api-permissions-plain)

# When to use the API vs the apps

Who needs keys and who can just use the website.

Worklittle has two front doors. Most people should walk through the app. The API is for building something custom. For a short tour first, see [What is the Worklittle API?](/help/api/what-is-worklittle-api).

## Use the apps if

- You want to search and apply for jobs
- You are hiring and want to post a role, review candidates, or manage your team
- You want to run surveys, send documents, or track attendance
- You want to ask an AI assistant to help with any of the above

None of this needs an API key. Just sign in at [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) or [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business).

## Use the API if

- You want jobs to appear on your own website
- You want Worklittle data inside another system you own
- You are building an AI agent that needs live job data
- You want to sync candidates into another tool automatically

This work is done by a developer, and it needs an API key. See [How do I give a developer access?](/help/api/hand-off-api-to-developer).

## A middle option

MCP lets AI tools connect to Worklittle without anyone writing code. It is a good fit if you use an AI assistant and want it to look up real jobs. See [Connect an AI tool without writing code](/help/api/connect-ai-without-code) and [REST vs MCP in plain English](/help/api/rest-vs-mcp-plain).

## Where the developer docs live

Hand your developer the [Jobs docs](/jobs/get-started/overview) or the [Business docs](/business/get-started/overview). See also [Help Center vs API reference](/help/using-docs/help-vs-api-docs).

# Billing overview

Pay as you go, manage your card, and review invoices for your organization.

Each organization (including your Personal workspace) has its own bill. Usage adds to amount owed. We charge your card on the 1st of each UTC month if you owe at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20. Balances under $0.50 wait. Manage everything on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).

## Open billing

Go to [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), or choose Manage billing under Account in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings#account) (that link opens your Personal workspace Billing).

At the top you will see **Current balance** and your payment method. **Organization credit** (company) or **Credit** (Personal) always shows **Credit balance**. A history table (From, Amount, Reason, Date) appears under that box when this organization has credit events. Use **Buy credit** in that box to buy usage credit for this organization, or **Send a gift** to send credit to someone else. **Accept gift** (or **Accept gifts** if more than one) only appears when you have a gift waiting to Accept. Plan shows Instant if you subscribe.

Before metered chat or API usage, accept the pay-as-you-go checkbox and keep a valid card on file (credit is used first when you have any).

Spend caps live under [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits).

## Personal vs company billing

Each organization has its own wallet and card.

- Personal bills Instant and job-seeker AI on worklittle.com, plus Personal plugins and your own API usage. It does not unlock hiring tools by itself.
- A company organization is where jobs, candidates, teammates, and employer APIs are billed. Company workspaces include **$0.10** of free monthly AI credit, plus any organization credit (bonuses) under **Organization credit** on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). That credit is used before your card is charged. The history table columns are From, Amount, Reason, and Date. Worklittle rows use the Worklittle logo. Gift credit shows the sender's full name. Instant referral From the friend shows their first name and photo. Referral concern links to [Referral Terms](https://docs.worklittle.com/help/account/referral-terms).

Switch to the right workspace before you check the bill. See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization).

## When we charge

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1st of each UTC month | We charge the card for amount owed (if at least $0.50) |
| Amount owed reaches $20 | We charge that day (checked about once an hour) |
| Under $0.50 unpaid | Waits until the next charge window |

Charges are in USD. Instant’s $9.99 is separate and renews on your subscribe anniversary. See [Payment methods](/help/account/payment-methods), [Find past invoices](/help/account/find-invoices), and [When Worklittle charges your card](/help/account/when-we-charge).

## What you can do there

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Accept billing terms | Required once per organization before metered usage |
| Manage payment method | Opens Stripe to add or replace the card |
| View invoices | Past monthly and interim charges |
| Limits | Optional monthly hard cap and budget alert emails |

Use **Buy credit** on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) to buy usage credit for the selected organization ($1 to $500). See [Can I buy prepaid credits?](/help/account/no-prepaid-credits).

## What you are charged for

Charges can come from Worklittle Business AI, public API usage, and (on Personal) worklittle.com AI after Instant credit or free allowances. The Instant $9.99 monthly fee is charged by Stripe on Billing. Browsing jobs or hiring pages does not bill.

See [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage) and [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).

## When a charge fails

If a card charge fails, metered chat and API usage pause until you update the payment method. See [Payment required messages](/help/account/payment-required).

## Related articles

- [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant)
- [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits)
- [Spend limits](/help/account/spend-limits)
- [Pricing basics](/help/account/pricing-help)
- [Donate to Worklittle](/help/account/donations)

# Worklittle Instant

The $9.99 plan with $20 of AI credit for Apply with AI, resumes, headshots, and chat on worklittle.com.

Worklittle Instant is the paid plan for AI help while you job hunt on worklittle.com. It costs $9.99 per month and includes $20 of AI credit for each Instant billing period.

## What you get

- $9.99 charged each Instant billing period to the card you add at checkout (renews on the anniversary of the day you subscribed)
- $20 of AI credit for that Instant period for Apply with AI, resumes, headshots, chat, and similar AI on worklittle.com
- Everything in the free plan still applies (jobs, alerts, saved jobs, and similar)
- After that credit is used up, more AI bills to your Personal card at normal rates

Credit is for usage only. It is not cash, does not roll over, and cannot be refunded or moved to someone else. Instant does not pay for a company hiring workspace. Worklittle Business uses a work email and its own company bill. See [Does Instant pay for my company?](/help/business-basics/instant-not-company-plan).

## How to subscribe

1. Open [Get Instant](https://worklittle.com/instant), [Plans](https://worklittle.com/plans), or [Adjust plan](https://worklittle.com/plans?=adjust) from your account menu (Upgrade plan). You can also open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and choose **Upgrade plan** under **Try upgraded features**. When you are signed out, **Log in** sits above that row. Upgrade plan is hidden once you already have Instant.
2. Choose Upgrade to Instant.
3. Finish checkout in Stripe.

That card is also used for pay as you go if you go past the included credit.

After checkout we email a receipt with **Try new features** and a grey **Refer a friend** button to [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer). See [Invite friends and earn credit](/help/account/refer-friends).

## How to cancel

You can cancel anytime from [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), from Manage billing under Account in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings#account), or from [Adjust plan](https://worklittle.com/plans?=adjust) in the Stripe customer portal.

Cancellation takes effect at the end of the period you already paid for. You keep Instant until then. Step-by-step: [Cancel Worklittle Instant](/help/account/cancel-instant).

## Where to check your plan and credit

Select your Personal organization, then open:

- [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) for your plan and remaining credit
- [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) for a banner of Instant credit left

The $9.99 monthly charge appears on Billing through Stripe. It is not a Usage fee row.

## Free limits without Instant

Without Instant, you go back to the free monthly AI amount unless you keep a card for extra AI use. People who are not logged in have limited access until they create an account. Details: [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits).

## Related

- [Get Instant](https://worklittle.com/instant) for the public Instant page

# Invite friends and earn credit

Share your invite from Refer. Instant members earn $5 when a friend buys Instant. Signed-in free accounts earn $0.50 when a friend joins, up to $20.

Open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) while signed in. It is a full-screen overlay, same as [Plans](https://worklittle.com/plans). Close it with the X in the top right. Worklittle Instant members share a checkout invite. Signed-in accounts without Instant share a join invite. Full rules are in [Referral Terms](/help/account/referral-terms).

## Who can invite

You need to be signed in. Guests who open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) are asked to log in with **Sign in to invite friends and earn up to $20**.

**Worklittle Instant.** Share a referral link or email an invite. Your friend gets $5 bonus Instant credit on top of the usual first-month $20 ($25 total) when they subscribe, and you earn $5 back. The Instant purchase email also has a grey **Refer a friend** button to this page.

**Signed in without Instant.** The same [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) page is titled Invite and earn $20. You get **$0.50** in usage credit for each friend who **creates a Worklittle account** through your link, up to **$20** (40 friends). Your friend does not receive join bonus credit.

If you run out of free AI and still have no credit two days later, we send **Refer and earn $20 from Worklittle**. We skip that send if you already have Instant or credit again. Turn it off from Manage emails or Unsubscribe.

You get one reusable link per program. It lasts 30 days. After it expires, Share creates a new one. You can email the same address at most once every 30 days per invite type.

Invite emails include **Manage emails** and **Unsubscribe** at the bottom. Unsubscribe stops future invites. Turning job alerts, local events, and announcements off does not. We do not send more invites to an address that unsubscribed.

## What your friend gets

**Instant invite.** Their page offers $25 in credit for signing up for Instant (Instant’s included $20 plus $5 referral bonus). They claim it by upgrading from a valid invite.

**Join invite.** Their page is an invitation to join Worklittle. They create an account. You earn $0.50 when that new account is created.

Invalid or expired links show Referral no longer available.

## What you earn

**Instant.** You earn $5 Instant usage credit when your friend finishes Instant checkout, not when they only create an account. Up to 10 successful Instant referrals ($50 max). Progress shows on [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) as Rewarded X of 10 after your first success.

**Join.** You earn $0.50 usage credit when your friend creates an account through your join invite, up to $20. Progress shows as Rewarded X of 40 after your first success.

Remaining credit appears under Credit on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).

## Send a gift

Anyone signed in can also [send a gift](/help/account/gifting-credits) from [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer). That is paid credit for a friend, not a referral reward.

# Gifting credits

Buy usage credit for a friend. Unclaimed gifts refund after 30 days. Claimed credit expires after 365 days.

You can gift Worklittle usage credit to a friend. They open the claim link, pick which Worklittle account the gift belongs to, then Accept it on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) onto whichever organization they want. This is separate from [referral rewards](/help/account/refer-friends).

## How to send a gift

**From Refer.** Open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer), choose **Or send a gift**, enter the amount, email, and an optional message, then continue to checkout. That charge uses the card on your **Personal** workspace. Instant is not required.

**From Billing.** Open [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) for the organization that should pay. In the Credit balance box, choose **Send a gift**. The left sidebar shows which organization is selected. That organization’s card is charged.

Amounts are whole dollars from **$1** to **$500**. You can send a gift to your own email. That still charges the selected card, emails you the claim link, and you can share that link or Accept the credit yourself.

## How to claim a gift

We email the recipient **Name sent you a $X gift on Worklittle** with **Claim your $X gift**.

That link opens [Log in](https://worklittle.com/login). If you are not signed in, the heading is **Log in to claim this gift**. After you sign in, you get the same account picker as ChatGPT MCP. Choose which Worklittle account the gift belongs to, or **Add an account**. Close with the **X**. Clicking the background does not close it. Closing without picking leaves the gift unclaimed.

You can have more than one gift waiting. On [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), pending gifts show under **Accept gift** (or **Accept gifts** if more than one), above **Organization credit** or **Credit**. That section only appears when you have a gift to Accept. Each gift has its own Accept and Deny.

Picking an account **reserves** the gift for that account only. Someone else who opens the same link cannot take it.

Then open [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). Switch to the organization that should receive the credit, then **Accept**. **Deny** releases the gift from your account so the claim link can be used with a different account.

Credit is not added until you Accept. Unused gifts refund to the sender after 30 days even if they were reserved and then denied, as long as nobody Accepted.

## Refunds if unclaimed

If the gift is not **Accepted** within **30 days** of payment, Worklittle refunds the original Stripe charge to the sender. We never add credit until Accept, and we do not refund a gift after it is accepted.

## Expiry after claim

Claimed gift credit is usage credit on the organization you accepted onto. Unused remainder expires **365 days** after the claim date. Expired gift credit is not paid out as cash and is not refunded to the sender.

Grants and expiries show in the credit history table on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).

# Referral Terms

Eligibility, rewards, limits, and clawback rules for Worklittle Instant referrals and join invites.

These Referral Terms apply to Worklittle referral programs on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com). By creating referral links, sending invites, or claiming referral credit, you agree to these terms. For a short how-to, see [Invite friends and earn credit](/help/account/refer-friends).

## Two programs

Worklittle runs two referral programs from [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer). Which one you use depends on whether you have an active Instant plan.

1. **Instant referrals.** For Worklittle Instant subscribers. Rewards when a friend successfully completes Instant checkout.
2. **Join invites.** For signed-in accounts that are not on Instant. Rewards when a friend creates a new Worklittle account.

The programs use separate links, reward counters, and invite emails. A friend can later subscribe to Instant through an Instant invite even if they first joined through a join invite, subject to Instant eligibility below.

## How Instant referrals work

1. Subscribe to [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).
2. Open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) and share your **one** reusable Instant link, or email that same link as an invite.
3. Your friend signs up for Instant through that invite while the link is still valid (**30 days** from when it was minted).
4. After they successfully complete Instant checkout, you each receive **$5** in Instant usage credit. Their **$5** is on top of Instant’s included **$20** for the first month (**$25** total for them).

## How join invites work

1. Sign in to Worklittle without Instant.
2. Open [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) (**Invite and earn $20**) and share your **one** reusable join link, or email that same link.
3. Your friend creates a **new** Worklittle account through that invite while the link is still valid (**30 days** from when it was minted).
4. You receive **$0.50** in usage credit. The friend who joined does **not** receive join bonus credit.

Existing accounts that open a join link do not generate a join reward. Self-referrals are not allowed.

## Eligibility

You must be signed in to create a referral link or send invite emails.

Instant rewards are available only to Worklittle Instant subscribers, and only when the friend completes a qualifying Instant checkout through an Instant-program link.

Join rewards are available only to signed-in users who are not on Instant, and only when the friend creates a new account through a join-program link.

## Your referral link

Each program has **one** active referral link at a time. Sharing or emailing reuses that same link. The link expires after **30 days**. Opening [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) and sharing again after expiry mints a replacement. Expired links no longer grant referral credit for that program.

## Rewards

**Instant.** When a friend you invite successfully subscribes to Worklittle Instant through your Instant link, you each receive **$5** in Instant usage credit. Their **$5** is added on top of the standard Instant included credit for the first month.

**Join.** When a friend creates a new account through your join link, you receive **$0.50** in usage credit. They do not receive join bonus credit.

Credit is usage credit, not cash. It has no cash value and is not transferable.

## Reward limits

**Instant.** Each Instant subscriber can earn Instant referral rewards for up to **10** successful Instant checkouts (**$50** max), counted across Instant links. After 10 rewarded Instant referrals, further Instant checkouts through your link do not grant bonus credit.

**Join.** Each eligible referrer can earn join rewards for up to **40** new accounts (**$0.50** each, **$20** max). After that, further signups through your join link do not grant bonus credit, and a new join link will not mint under these terms.

Progress shows on [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) after your first success for that program.

## Self-referral

Self-referrals are not allowed. You cannot earn rewards by inviting yourself, using alternate accounts you control, or otherwise attempting to refer your own account or subscription. Instant subscribers who open someone else’s Instant invite go to their own [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) page instead. Signed-in users who open a join invite go to their own [Refer](https://worklittle.com/refer) page.

## Refunds and chargebacks

If a referred Instant subscription is refunded, charged back, or canceled in a way that voids the qualifying purchase, Worklittle may claw back the Instant referral credits granted to both parties.

Join rewards are granted when a new account is created. Worklittle may withhold or reverse join credit in cases of abuse, duplicate or fake accounts, or other violations of these terms.

## Where to see bonus credit

Bonus usage credit remaining appears under **Credit** on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) when you have any left.

Each grant and expiry also appears under **Credits** on [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) for that organization. A monthly Instant or free allotment that comes back after you used it up is **Usage limit reset**. Instant monthly credit is the first Instant grant. Gifts show the sender’s name. Worklittle Instant and Worklittle show a verified badge.

## Changes

Worklittle may update these Referral Terms, reward amounts, or eligibility rules. Continued use of a referral program after changes means you accept the updated terms.

## Questions

Questions about referrals: [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com).

Related: [Invite friends and earn credit](/help/account/refer-friends) · [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant) · [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview)

# Usage dashboard

See what you used and what it cost.

The Usage page shows where your organization's amount owed came from, so you can understand the bill.

## Open it

# Spend limits

Cap your monthly spend and get an email before you hit it.

A spend limit is a ceiling you set for the month. It protects you from a runaway script or an unexpectedly busy week.

## Set a monthly limit

1. Open [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits).
2. Find **Monthly limit**.
3. Enter the maximum you want to spend in a month for this organization.
4. Select **Save**.

Once the hard cap is reached, metered chat and paid API requests stop until you raise the limit or the **UTC calendar month** changes. In chat you may see a billing block card with **Open Billing**.

## Add budget alerts

Under **Budget alerts**, choose **Add alert** and set the amount you want to be warned at. You can also:

- Set **Email when budget exceeds** to a threshold such as 80
- Add **Additional emails to alert** so a finance teammate is copied

Alerts are a warning, not a stop. The monthly limit is what actually stops spending. Each percentage can only have one alert.

## Picking a number

- Look at last month on the [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage) and add some headroom.
- If you are just starting, set a small limit deliberately. It is easy to raise later.
- Set alerts below the limit so you have time to react.

## If you hit the limit

Metered usage stays blocked until you raise the limit or the UTC calendar month changes. See [Payment required messages](/help/account/payment-required).

# Payment required messages

What a payment error means and how to clear it.

A payment error means Worklittle received your request but cannot complete it until the billing side is sorted out. There is nothing to "add credit" for. Fix the card or the monthly limit.

## The usual causes

| Cause | What you see | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Payment failed (`payment_failed`) | Chat shows a billing block with **Open Billing** | Update the card via **Manage payment method** on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) (Stripe Customer Portal) |
| Monthly limit reached | Same billing block, different title | Raise or clear the cap under [Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits), or wait for the new month |
| Card declined | Collection fails on Billing | Update the payment method in the Stripe Customer Portal |
| No payment method on file | Amount owed cannot be collected | Add a card on Billing before the next collection |

## Clear it in three steps

1. Open [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). Use **Manage payment method** if collection failed, or **Limits** if you hit a monthly cap.
2. Confirm you are in the right organization (Personal vs company). See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization).
3. Retry once. Do not retry in a tight loop while billing is still blocked.

Requests usually start working again within moments after the card or limit is fixed.

## Stop it happening again

- Keep a valid card on file for each organization. See [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview).
- Add a budget alert below your limit. See [Spend limits](/help/account/spend-limits).
- Review the [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage) after any change that increases traffic.

## Still stuck

If billing looks healthy and the error continues, check [Service status](/help/api/status-page), then email [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com) with the time the error happened.

# Pricing basics

Where to read what things cost.

Prices are published in the docs so you can check them before you build anything. This article points you to the right page.

## Where prices live

- [Jobs pricing](/jobs/get-started/pricing) for AI token rates on the Jobs API and Jobs MCP tools
- [Business pricing](/business/get-started/pricing) for AI token rates on Work / Business Platform
- [Jobs rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits) and [Business rate limits](/business/resources/rate-limits) for free monthly quotas (job search, email, sandbox, and similar)

Pricing pages cover paid rates. Free quotas live on Rate limits. Usage accrues as amount owed on the organization wallet. We charge your card on the **1st of each UTC month** if owed is at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20. For higher free quotas, email business@worklittle.com.

## What is free vs what accrues

Job search, raw job detail, map, companies, emails, and most ATS tools are free within monthly quotas on Rate limits. First-time AI job-description generations include 100 free per organization per UTC day, then bill AI token rates. Platform AI chat and other AI token usage accrue amount owed on the active organization.

On the Jobs API, Apply with AI bills as AI token usage (typically about $0.01–$0.03 per application). Resumes and cover letters are typically under $0.01. Chat messages are typically under $0.005. First-time AI job descriptions after the free daily allowance are typically under $0.01. Hosted apply is **$0.01 per successful submit**. Business Platform is mainly AI tokens. See [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview), [Jobs pricing](/jobs/get-started/pricing), and [Business pricing](/business/get-started/pricing).

## Estimating a monthly bill

1. Read the token rates on the Jobs or Business pricing page.
2. Estimate how many model-backed calls you will make.
3. Add a margin for retries and testing.
4. Set a monthly limit slightly above that figure. See [Spend limits](/help/account/spend-limits).

## Checking real numbers

Once you are live, the [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage) shows what you actually spent, which is always better than an estimate.

# REST vs MCP in plain English

Two ways developers and AI tools connect to Worklittle.

You may hear these two words from a developer or an AI tool. Here is what they mean without the jargon.

## REST, in one line

REST is the way a program asks Worklittle for something directly. A developer writes code that says "give me software jobs in Austin" and gets a structured answer back.

Choose REST when someone is building software, such as a careers page, a dashboard, or a sync into another system.

## MCP, in one line

MCP is a way to plug Worklittle into an AI assistant so the assistant can look things up itself. You connect it once, then ask the assistant questions in normal language and it fetches real Worklittle data.

Choose MCP when you use an AI assistant and want it working from real job data instead of guessing.

## Side by side

| | REST | MCP |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who sets it up | A developer | Often you, in your AI tool's settings |
| Who uses it | Your software | Your AI assistant |
| Needs code | Yes | Usually no |
| Needs an API key | Yes | Usually yes |

## Learn more

- [MCP guide](/jobs/mcp) for setup instructions
- [REST vs MCP](/use-cases/rest-vs-mcp) for the deeper comparison
- [When to use the API vs the apps](/help/api/when-to-use-api) if you are not sure you need either

# Prompt guides overview

Ready-to-copy prompts for the Jobs app and Worklittle Business.

A prompt is just what you type to the assistant. These guides give you wording that works, so you can paste it in and edit the details.

## How to use these guides

1. Find the prompt closest to what you want.
2. Select the copy button on the code block.
3. Paste it into chat.
4. Replace anything in square brackets with your own details.
5. Send.

Nothing here is magic wording. It works because it is specific.

## Pick your guide

- [Jobs prompt guide](/help/prompt-guides/jobs-prompt-guide) for job search, resumes, and applications
- [Business prompt guide](/help/prompt-guides/business-prompt-guide) for posting jobs, candidates, and surveys
- [Chat feature prompts](/help/prompt-guides/chat-feature-prompts) for headshots, whiteboards, and docs
- [Apply with AI prompt tips](/help/prompt-guides/apply-prompt-tips) for smoother applications
- [Keep answers honest](/help/prompt-guides/grounding-tips-everyday) for sticking to real job data

## Four habits that improve any prompt

- **Be specific.** "Remote data analyst roles in Canada paying over 90k" beats "find me a job".
- **Say the format.** Ask for a table, five bullets, or a short paragraph.
- **Give context once.** Mention your experience, location, and constraints at the start of the chat.
- **Correct rather than restart.** One follow-up sentence usually fixes a near-miss answer.

# Jobs prompt guide

Prompts for searching jobs, improving your resume, and getting apply help.

Copy any of these into chat at [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) and swap the bracketed parts for your own details.

## Find roles that fit

```text
I am looking for [job title] roles.

About me:
- Experience: [number] years in [field]
- Location: [city], and I am open to [remote / hybrid / on-site]
- Must have: [salary floor, visa sponsorship, no travel, etc.]
- Deal breakers: [night shifts, relocation, etc.]

Show me 10 current openings that genuinely match. For each one give me
the title, company, location, pay if it is listed, and one sentence on
why it fits me. Skip anything that does not meet my must-haves.
```

## Compare two openings

```text
Compare these two jobs for me:
1. [paste first job link or title and company]
2. [paste second job link or title and company]

Put it in a table with rows for pay, location and remote policy,
seniority, day-to-day work, and anything that looks like a red flag.
Finish with one paragraph on which one suits someone with my background
in [your background].
```

## Understand a job description

```text
Here is a job description: [paste it]

Explain it to me in plain language:
- What would I actually do every day
- Which requirements are genuinely required and which are wishlist
- What experience I appear to be missing
- Three questions I should ask in an interview
```

## Tailor your resume to one job

```text
Here is my resume: [paste or attach]
Here is the job I want: [paste the description]

Rewrite my experience section so it lines up with this job.
Rules:
- Do not invent anything I did not do
- Keep every bullet to one line
- Lead each bullet with a strong verb and include a number where I gave you one
- Mirror the wording the job description uses for skills I actually have

Then list anything the job asks for that my resume does not cover.
```

## Write a cover letter

```text
Write a cover letter for [job title] at [company].

Use these facts about me: [two or three things you have actually done]
Keep it under 250 words.
Open with why this company specifically, not a generic line.
Plain, direct language. No buzzwords, no flattery.
End with a simple closing sentence.
```

## Prepare for the interview

```text
I have an interview for [job title] at [company] on [date].

Give me:
- 8 questions they are likely to ask for this kind of role
- For each, a two-sentence outline of how I should answer given my
  background in [your background]
- 5 questions I should ask them
- One thing about this company or role I should research beforehand
```

## Understand the market

```text
What does the market look like for [job title] in [location] right now?

Tell me:
- Roughly how many openings there are
- The typical pay range being advertised
- Which companies are hiring most
- Which skills show up again and again in the listings

Base this on real listings, and say so if the data is thin.
```

## Related

- [Apply with AI prompt tips](/help/prompt-guides/apply-prompt-tips)
- [Keep answers honest](/help/prompt-guides/grounding-tips-everyday)

# Business prompt guide

Prompts for posting jobs, reviewing candidates, and running surveys.

Paste these into chat at [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business). Replace the bracketed parts with your own details.

## Write a job posting

```text
Draft a job posting for a [job title] at my company.

Details:
- Team: [team name and what it does]
- Location: [city] and [remote / hybrid / on-site]
- Level: [junior / mid / senior]
- Pay range: [range]
- Must-have experience: [two or three things]
- Nice to have: [one or two things]

Write it in plain language. No corporate filler.
Structure it as: what the role is, what you will do, what we are looking
for, and what we offer. Keep requirements to six bullets maximum.
```

## Tighten a posting you already have

```text
Here is our current job posting: [paste it]

Rewrite it to be shorter and clearer.
- Cut anything that would be true of any job at any company
- Turn vague requirements into concrete ones
- Flag any wording that might discourage good candidates from applying
- Keep the same meaning and the same pay range
```

## Summarize your candidates

```text
Give me a summary of the candidates for [job title].

As a table with one row per candidate:
- Name
- Current or most recent role
- Years of relevant experience
- The single strongest thing in their favour
- The single biggest gap

Sort by how well they match the posting. Do not guess at anything that is
not in their application.
```

## Screening questions

```text
Write 5 screening questions for [job title].

Rules:
- Each should be answerable in two or three sentences
- Each should tell me something a resume cannot
- No trick questions and nothing that touches on protected characteristics
- Include what a strong answer looks like for each one
```

## Candidate messages

```text
Write two short emails for [job title]:

1. Inviting [candidate name] to a first interview. Warm, specific about
   why we liked their application, offer two time slots.
2. Declining a candidate we are not moving forward with. Kind, honest,
   short, no false hope, no generic filler.
```

## Build a survey

```text
Create a survey called "[survey name]" for [who will answer it].

Goal: [what you want to learn]

Give me 8 questions:
- Mix of multiple choice and short open questions
- Put the easy ones first
- Mark which ones should be required
- Keep every question to one sentence

Avoid leading questions. I want honest answers, not confirmation.
```

## Draft an HR document

```text
Draft a [policy name] policy for a company of [size] people in [country].

Cover: [the two or three things it must address]
Use short sections with headings.
Write it so a new employee can understand it on the first read.
Mark anywhere I need to fill in a company-specific detail with [brackets].

Remind me at the end that this needs legal review.
```

## Sketch an automation

```text
I want an automation that does this:

When [trigger, for example a candidate applies to any engineering role],
then [first action], wait [time], then [second action].

Lay it out on the canvas for me. Explain each step in one line before you
build it so I can correct you first.
```

# Chat feature prompts

Prompts for headshots, whiteboards, and documents.

Chat can do more than answer questions. These prompts trigger the built-in tools for images, drawing, and writing.

## AI headshots

```text
Turn this photo into a professional headshot.

- Plain neutral background
- Business casual
- Natural lighting, nothing overly retouched
- Keep my face exactly as it is
- Square crop suitable for a LinkedIn profile picture
```

Attach your photo in the same message. If the first result is close, reply with one change rather than starting again:

```text
Same photo, but make the background a light grey instead of white
and warm the lighting slightly.
```

## Whiteboard

```text
Open a whiteboard and map out my job search.

Three columns: applied, interview, offer.
Add a card for each of these roles: [list them]
Leave space at the bottom for notes.
```

```text
On the whiteboard, sketch our hiring process as a flow:
application, screen, technical interview, team interview, offer.
Show where a rejection can happen at each stage.
```

## Documents

```text
Create a document called "[title]".

Contents:
- A short intro paragraph explaining [topic]
- Three sections with headings: [section one], [section two], [section three]
- A checklist at the end

Keep the tone plain and direct. I will edit it after.
```

Typing `/` in chat opens a menu of skills and tools. It is often faster than describing what you want, and it shows you what is available.
