# Apply with AI prompt tips

How to describe yourself so applications go through smoothly.

Upload your resume, tap Apply, and Worklittle fills out and sends the application in a cloud browser in chat. You can watch and take control anytime. Looking first is only if you turn Always submit off.

## Start with a good resume

Upload a current resume before you start applying. Almost everything on an application form comes from it. A resume that is thin on dates, titles, and locations forces the assistant to leave fields blank.

## Fill the gaps resumes never cover

Application forms ask things a resume does not. Give these once, up front:

```text
Details to use whenever you apply for me:

- Full name: [name]
- Location: [city, state or country]
- Phone: [number]
- Work authorization: [for example, authorized to work in the US without sponsorship]
- Willing to relocate: [yes / no / for the right role]
- Earliest start date: [date or notice period]
- Salary expectation: [range]
- Preferred work setup: [remote / hybrid / on-site]
- Links: [LinkedIn, portfolio, GitHub]
```

## Give a reusable about-me paragraph

Many forms ask why you want the role or to describe yourself. Write it once in your own voice:

```text
Use this as my standard summary when a form asks about my background:

I am a [role] with [number] years of experience in [field]. I have spent
most of that time [what you actually did], most recently at [company]
where I [one concrete achievement with a number]. I am looking for
[what you want next] because [honest reason].
```

## Set your boundaries

```text
When applying on my behalf:

- Never invent experience, degrees, or certifications I do not have
- If a form asks something you do not know about me, ask me instead of guessing
- Do not agree to relocation or a salary below [amount]
- Show me the answers before submitting anything
```

## Reviewing before submit

- Read the free-text answers. Those are what a human actually reads.
- Check that the location and work authorization fields are right, because those get filtered on hardest.
- If something looks generic, replace one sentence with a specific detail from your own history.

## Related

- [Jobs prompt guide](/help/prompt-guides/jobs-prompt-guide)
- [Keep answers honest](/help/prompt-guides/grounding-tips-everyday)

# Keep answers honest

Ask chat to stick to real job data instead of guessing.

AI assistants can sound confident about things they do not know. A few words in your prompt push the assistant to use real Worklittle data and admit when it has none.

## Ask for real listings

```text
Only use real job listings from Worklittle for this answer.

For every role you mention, include the company name, the location, and
the link. If you cannot find enough real matches, tell me how many you
found rather than filling the list out.
```

## Make uncertainty visible

```text
When you are not sure about something, say so in the answer.

Mark anything you are inferring rather than reading directly from a
listing. I would rather have a short accurate answer than a long
confident one.
```

## Pin down numbers

```text
For any salary, headcount, or date you give me, say where it came from.

If it is listed in the posting, quote it. If it is an estimate based on
similar roles, label it as an estimate.
```

## Warning signs in an answer

- Company names you cannot find anywhere
- Salary ranges given with no source
- Every result being a perfect match for you
- Links that do not open, or open a search page rather than a real posting
- Exactly the round number of results you asked for, every time

## What to do when something looks wrong

Ask directly:

```text
Check that job again. Give me the direct link to the posting and confirm
it is still open. If you cannot confirm it, remove it from the list.
```

If the assistant repeatedly gives wrong or unsafe information, report it. See [Chat reports](/help/privacy-safety/chat-reports).

# Privacy overview

How we talk about your data in plain words.

This is a plain-language summary of how your information is used in Worklittle. The full detail lives in the privacy policy.

## What Worklittle holds

- **Your account**, such as your email address and display name
- **Your profile**, such as your resume, desired role, and preferences
- **Your activity**, such as jobs you saved, applications you started, and chats you had
- **Your organization's data**, if you use Worklittle Business, such as candidates, employees, documents, and surveys

## What it is used for

- Showing you jobs that match what you asked for
- Filling in applications when you ask Apply with AI to help
- Sending job alert emails if you turned them on
- Running the employer features your organization uses

Your resume is not published to employers unless you apply to them. Some directory-style features may be limited or unavailable depending on product rollout.

## Your choices

- Update or clear your profile at any time
- Turn email alerts on or off in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings)
- Turn **Marketing measurement** and **Personalized marketing** on or off in Privacy in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) or [Business Settings](https://worklittle.com/business)
- Export or delete your account data

See [Marketing and ads privacy](/help/privacy-safety/marketing-privacy-toggles), [Data you control](/help/privacy-safety/data-you-control), and [Privacy rights requests](/help/privacy-safety/privacy-rights).

## Security and team access

Privacy is not only about personal accounts. On Worklittle Business, roles limit who can see hiring and employee data, including inside chat. See [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions) and [Compliance and security](/help/privacy-safety/compliance-and-security).

## The full policy

Read the complete [Privacy policy](https://worklittle.com/privacy). Full policy list: [Where are Worklittle’s legal policies?](/help/privacy-safety/legal-policies-list). Privacy requests: [privacy@worklittle.com](mailto:privacy@worklittle.com). Product questions: [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com).

# Compliance and security

How Worklittle protects accounts, company data, and everyday access.

Worklittle is built so people and companies can trust what they put in the product. This page is the plain-language version of how we think about security and responsible use.

## What we care about protecting

- **Accounts and sign-in**, so only you can open your workspace
- **Job seeker data**, such as resumes, chats, and applications
- **Company data** on Worklittle Business, such as candidates, employees, documents, surveys, and billing
- **API keys and payments**, so developers and finance stays locked down to the right people

## How access is kept tight inside a company

On Worklittle Business, every teammate has a role. The role is not just a label - it changes which pages appear and what chat is allowed to know.

- **Can chat** teammates get a personal experience. Hiring pages stay hidden, and chat will not surface pipeline or other people's private records.
- Higher roles unlock more of the workspace only as needed.
- Billing, usage, and spend limits stay with **Full access** and **Owner**.

That least-access model is one of the main ways company information stays private day to day. Full detail: [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions).

## Sign-in and keys

- Sign-in uses Google, a one-time email code, or an optional password you set. See [Trouble signing in](/help/account/trouble-signing-in).
- Sessions and API keys are required for protected actions.
- API keys inherit what their creator's role can do, so a limited teammate cannot mint a key that outranks them.
- Public traffic to the site and API runs over HTTPS.

## Infrastructure and monitoring

- Production services run on modern cloud infrastructure with secrets kept out of source code.
- Operational issues are monitored so problems can be spotted and fixed quickly.
- Suspected security incidents are triaged, contained, and remediated. When the law requires it, affected people are notified.

For the formal write-up, read the [Information security policy](https://worklittle.com/information-security-policy). Worklittle does not advertise HIPAA or FedRAMP badges in Help. See [Is Worklittle HIPAA or FedRAMP certified?](/help/privacy-safety/compliance-claims).

## Your part as a customer

Security is shared. A few habits go a long way:

- Invite people with the smallest role that still works for their job.
- Remove teammates when they leave.
- Keep API keys in safe places and rotate them if someone who had access leaves.
- Do not paste secrets, government IDs, or card numbers into chat.
- Verify a work email before publishing jobs. See [Verify a work email](/help/business-basics/work-email).

## Policies and where to ask

| Document | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Privacy policy](https://worklittle.com/privacy) | What we collect and why |
| [Terms of service](https://worklittle.com/terms-of-use) | The agreement for using Worklittle |
| [Information security policy](https://worklittle.com/information-security-policy) | How we protect systems and data |
| [Access controls policy](https://worklittle.com/access-controls-policy) | How access is granted and removed |
| [Data retention and disposal](https://worklittle.com/data-retention-and-disposal-policy) | How long data is kept |

Vulnerability reports: [contact@worklittle.com](mailto:contact@worklittle.com). Everyday product help: [Contact support](/help/privacy-safety/contact-support). Which inbox: [Who do I email?](/help/privacy-safety/who-to-email).

# Contact support

# Chat reports

Report an AI answer that is unsafe, wrong, or inappropriate.

If the assistant says something harmful or clearly incorrect, tell us. Reports are reviewed by the team.

## How to report

1. Open the chat containing the message.
2. Use the message or chat menu and choose the report option.
3. In Report a concern, pick the reason that fits best.
4. Submit.

You can report while signed out on worklittle.com.

## Reasons you can choose

- Not relevant to me
- Privacy violation
- Intellectual property
- Age-inappropriate content
- Bullying & harassment
- Spam, fraud & deception
- Something else

Pick the closest match. If nothing fits, choose Something else.

## Reporting a merely unhelpful answer

You do not need the full report flow for a bad but harmless answer. Use the thumbs-down option on the message. That feedback still reaches us and it is quicker.

## Urgent situations

If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services. Worklittle reports are reviewed, but not in real time.

Also see [Report harmful AI or a bad job](/help/privacy-safety/report-harmful-content).

# Report a job

Flag postings that look like scams, spam, or closed roles.

Worklittle collects jobs from many sources. If one looks wrong, reporting it helps everyone who searches after you.

## When to report

- The posting asks for money, bank details, or identity documents up front
- The company does not appear to exist
- The role has clearly been filled or withdrawn
- The description is unrelated to the job title
- The link goes somewhere unrelated or unsafe
- The content looks abusive or exploitative

## How to report

1. Open the job on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs).
2. Use the menu on the job and choose the report option.
3. In Report a concern, pick the reason that fits best.
4. Submit.

Reasons in the picker include Not relevant to me, Job no longer active, Spam, fraud, & deception, Age-inappropriate content, Sexual exploitation & abuse, Child/teen exploitation, and Something else.

You do not need to be signed in. If you cannot find a report option, email [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com) with the job link.

## What happens next

Reported jobs are reviewed. Postings confirmed as closed or fraudulent are removed from search results. You will not usually get an individual reply, but the report is not ignored.

## Protect yourself first

Before reporting, make sure you have not shared anything sensitive. See [Safety tips for job seekers](/help/privacy-safety/safety-tips).

# Safety tips for job seekers

Spot job scams before they cost you money or data.

Real employers do not ask for money. Almost every job scam breaks that one rule somewhere in the process.

## Clear warning signs

- You are asked to pay for training, equipment, or a background check
- You are offered the job without a real interview
- The pay is far above the going rate for that work
- All contact happens over a messaging app and never by video or phone
- The email address is a free personal account rather than a company domain
- You are asked to receive money and forward it on
- You are pressured to decide immediately

## Never share these early

Wait until you have a written, signed offer from a company you have verified:

- Bank account or card details
- Social security or national identity numbers
- Photos of your passport or driving licence
- Copies of documents "for payroll setup"

Legitimate onboarding paperwork comes after an offer, through a proper system.

## How to verify a company

1. Search for the company independently rather than using links in the message.
2. Check whether the same job is posted on the company's own careers page.
3. Look up the recruiter on a professional network and see whether the profile is established.
4. Call the company's published main number and ask whether the role is real.

## If you think you have been scammed

- Stop all contact
- Contact your bank immediately if you sent money or shared card details
- Report identity theft to your local authority
- Report the posting on Worklittle. See [Report a job](/help/privacy-safety/job-reports)

# Data you control

Your profile, your preferences, and deleting your account.

Most of what Worklittle knows about you is something you can see and change yourself.

## Your profile

In Settings you can update:

- Your name and photo
- Your resume, including replacing or removing it
- The **Job title** you are looking for, which is what job alerts are based on
- Your contact details, links, work authorization, skills, and interests

Removing your resume stops it being used to fill in applications.

## Email preferences

Turn each type of email on or off in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings):

- **Job alerts** for new matching roles
- **Local events**
- **Announcements**

Every email also has an unsubscribe link at the bottom.

## Marketing and ads

Privacy in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) and [Business Settings](https://worklittle.com/business) has two switches:

- **Marketing measurement** (Google Analytics and Clarity)
- **Personalized marketing** (ads)

Both default on except in the EEA, UK, and Switzerland, where they default off until you turn them on. Signed-in choices save to your account. Details: [Marketing and ads privacy](/help/privacy-safety/marketing-privacy-toggles).

## Recents

You can delete a conversation from Recents in the sidebar. Deleting a chat removes it from your account.

## Deleting your account

Account deletion is in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings). You are signed out and have three days to sign in again and cancel. After that it is permanent. Export first if you want a copy.

Step-by-step: [Delete my account for privacy](/help/privacy-safety/delete-account-privacy).

## Organization data

If you use Worklittle Business, your organization's data belongs to the organization rather than to your personal account. Teammates who can open Organization can download an organization export JSON (profile and members). Leaving an organization does not delete its records. See [What happens to data when someone leaves?](/help/business-basics/leaving-data-access).

# Browse the docs site

Pills at the top, sidebar on the left, search everywhere.

This site holds several different sets of pages. The navigation is built so you can tell which one you are in.

## The pills at the top

| Pill | What is inside |
| --- | --- |
| Home | The starting point across all products |
| Jobs | Everything about job search, applications, and job data |
| Business | Everything about Worklittle Business |
| Use cases | Worked examples and patterns |
| What's new | Release notes |
| Help center | Everyday how-to articles |

Selecting a pill switches the whole left sidebar to that area.

## Install on Home

Above Jobs, Business, and MCP on [Home](https://docs.worklittle.com/), there is a copy chip for `npm install worklittle`. Select it to copy the command. That is the TypeScript SDK on npm (also published as `@worklittle/sdk`). Python is `pip install worklittle`.

## Agent Quickstart on Home

The Home page **Agent Quickstart** card is the starting point for coding agents. In a browser it opens the [Agent Quickstart](/use-cases/agent-quickstart) page under Use cases, Agent patterns. That page covers Jobs and Business together so an agent can pick from what you asked for. Agents fetching the same card URL get `https://docs.worklittle.com/agent-onboarding/SKILL.md`.

The curl [Jobs Quickstart](/jobs/get-started/quickstart) and [Business Quickstart](/business/get-started/quickstart) stay in each product's Get started sidebar.

## The left sidebar

On [Home](https://docs.worklittle.com/), the left sidebar lists **Jobs**, **Business**, and **Use cases**. Each section title is a button that opens the first page in that area. The rows under a section are also buttons to those pages.

On Jobs, Business, Use cases, and Help, the sidebar lists the pages for that area, grouped into sections such as Get started, Libraries, API, and Resources. On a narrow screen it is hidden behind the menu button.

## Search

Press **Command K** on a Mac or **Control K** on Windows to open search from anywhere. Type a few letters and select a result. On a phone, use the search button in the header.

## Other shortcuts

- **Command I** or **Control I** focuses the docs chat input. See [Docs chat](/help/using-docs/docs-chat).
- Each page has a copy button for sharing the page as text. See [Copy a whole page](/help/using-docs/copy-page).

# Copy code blocks

Grab an example without selecting text by hand.

Every code example on this site has a copy button, including the prompt templates in the prompt guides.

## How to copy

1. Hover over the code block. On a touch screen, the button is always visible.
2. Select **Copy** in the top right corner of the block.
3. The button confirms with **Copied**.
4. Paste wherever you need it.

The copy takes the whole block exactly as written, with no line numbers or extra characters.

## After you paste

- Replace anything in square brackets, such as `[your city]`, with your own value.
- Replace placeholder keys such as `YOUR_API_KEY` with a real key. See [API keys](/help/api/api-keys).
- For prompts, edit the details before sending so the answer is about your situation.

## Copying more than one block

If you need a whole page rather than one snippet, use the page copy button instead. See [Copy a whole page](/help/using-docs/copy-page).

# Copy a whole page

Share a full docs page with a teammate or an AI assistant.

**Copy page** puts the entire page on your clipboard as plain text, which makes it easy to hand to someone else or paste into an AI assistant.

## How to use it

1. Open the page you want.
2. Select **Copy page** near the top of the page.
3. The button confirms with "Copied".
4. Paste it wherever you need it.

## Good uses

- Paste a page into an AI assistant, then ask a question about it
- Send the steps to a colleague who cannot open the site right now
- Keep a copy in your own notes alongside your setup details

## What's new

[What's new](/resources/release-notes) does not include **Copy page**, and the page cannot be selected with ⌘A / Ctrl+A. Read it on the site, or ask docs chat about a release.

## Pairing it with a question

Pasting a page and then asking something specific works better than asking from memory:

```text
[paste the copied page]

Based only on the page above, tell me the exact steps for my situation:
I am [describe your situation] and I want to [what you want to do].
```

# Docs chat

Ask questions without leaving the page you are reading.

Docs chat answers questions about Worklittle using the documentation. You do not need to sign in to use it.

## Open it

On the [docs home](https://docs.worklittle.com/) and the [Help Center](https://docs.worklittle.com/help) home, the composer sits under the intro, above the first section. Send a question and the bar animates into the chat panel. Open a Help Center collection or article and the bar moves to the bottom of the page.

On other docs pages, select the chat input at the bottom of the page, or press **Command I** on a Mac or **Control I** on Windows to jump straight to it.

## What to ask

- "How do I create an API key"
- "What is the difference between REST and MCP"
- "Which page explains job alert emails"
- "Show me an example of searching jobs by location"

Questions grounded in the docs get the best answers. Questions about your specific account do not, because docs chat cannot see your data.

## What it cannot do

- It cannot look up your account, your balance, or your organization
- It cannot make changes on your behalf
- It cannot see private information

For anything account-specific, use the assistant inside the app, or email [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com).

## Getting a better answer

- Mention which product you mean, Jobs or Business.
- Say whether you are using the app or writing code.
- If the answer points at a page, open it and confirm before acting.

# What's new

Release notes for every product update.

The release notes page lists what changed and when, newest first, across the job search app, Worklittle Business, the API, and the docs.

## Where to read it

Open [What's new](/resources/release-notes), or select the **What's new** pill at the top of any docs page.

Each release has a date and a short title, then two groups:

- **New features** for things you could not do before
- **Improvements and bug fixes** for things that got better

Skim the titles first and read only what applies to you.

- Something in the app looks different from yesterday

# Help Center vs API reference

Everyday help on one side, developer pages on the other.

Both live on this site, and they are written for different readers. Picking the right one first saves time.

## Help Center

Written for anyone using Worklittle in a browser.

- Step-by-step instructions with buttons and menus named
- No code
- Covers job search, Apply with AI, hiring, HR, billing, and safety

Reach it with the **Help center** pill at the top of the page, or **Help center** under Resources in the [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business) left sidebar.

## API reference

Written for developers building software.

- Endpoints, parameters, and responses
- Authentication and API keys
- SDKs, the CLI, MCP, and webhooks

Reach it through the **Jobs** or **Business** pills, then the **API** section of the sidebar.

## Which one for a given question

| Question | Section |
| --- | --- |
| Does Worklittle apply to jobs for me | Help Center → [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) |
| How do I post a job | Help Center |
| Why is my card declining | Help Center |
| What fields does a job object have | API reference |
| How do I paginate results | API reference |
| Should I even need an API key | [When to use the API vs the apps](/help/api/when-to-use-api) |

## Also worth knowing

**Use cases** sits between the two. It shows complete worked examples, which helps when you know what you want to build but not which pieces to use. See [Use cases](/use-cases/overview).

# What is the Worklittle API?

The programming door into Worklittle jobs, hiring, and MCP tools.

The Worklittle API lets software and AI tools use the same jobs and hiring data you see in the apps. Most people never need it. You only need it when someone is building a custom integration.

## The short version

Worklittle has apps you click through in a browser, and an API that programs talk to.

- [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com) and [worklittle.com/business](https://worklittle.com/business) are for people
- The API at api.worklittle.com is for developers and AI tools
- MCP at mcp.worklittle.com is a way for AI assistants to use the same capabilities without writing much code

If you are just searching jobs or hiring in the product, stay in the apps. See [When to use the API vs the apps](/help/api/when-to-use-api).

## What people usually build

- A careers page that lists your company’s Worklittle jobs
- A search or matching tool on top of the Jobs index
- An agent that looks up real jobs or helps apply
- A sync that moves candidates or hiring events into another system

Those projects need an API key. See [API keys](/help/api/api-keys).

## Jobs API vs Business API

- The Jobs side is market-wide job search, company pages, apply tools, and related agent features
- The Business side is your own hiring workspace: postings, candidates, employees, surveys, documents, and webhooks

One key can cover both, depending on what the key is allowed to do. See [What can my API key do?](/help/api/api-permissions-plain).

## Where to send a developer

- [Jobs overview](/jobs/get-started/overview)
- [Business overview](/business/get-started/overview)
- [MCP guide](/jobs/mcp)
- [Help Center vs API reference](/help/using-docs/help-vs-api-docs)

# Share or rotate an API key

Keep keys private, give each system its own key, and replace a key safely.

An API key is like a password for your organization. Share it carefully, and replace it if it might have leaked.

## Do not share a key casually

Do not paste a key into chat, email, a shared spreadsheet, or a public GitHub repo. Anyone with the key can act as your organization within what that key is allowed to do.

If a teammate needs access, create a separate key for them or for their system, or have an owner create one and hand it over through a password manager.

## One key per place

Name keys after where they are used, for example "Careers site" or "Internal agent". That makes it easier to revoke only the key that was exposed without breaking everything else.

## Rotate a key safely

1. Create a new key on [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys).
2. Put the new key into your app or AI tool.
3. Confirm the new key works.
4. Revoke the old key.

Do not revoke the old key first if the system is live, or traffic will fail until the new key is installed.

## If a key leaked

Revoke it immediately on [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys), then create a replacement. Check [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) afterward for unexpected activity. See [Why is my API key not working?](/help/api/api-key-not-working) if something still fails.

# Why is my API key not working?

Fixes for invalid key, wrong organization, revoked keys, and missing permissions.

When a key fails, the problem is usually a typo, a revoked key, the wrong organization, or a missing permission. Work through the checklist below before assuming the API is down.

## Quick checklist

1. Confirm you copied the full key when it was created. Keys are shown once and start with `sk-wl-api01-`.
2. Check that the key was not revoked on [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys).
3. Confirm you are using the organization that owns the key. See [Which organization does my API key belong to?](/help/api/which-org-for-api).
4. Make sure the call includes an Authorization Bearer header with the key.
5. If the error mentions permissions or forbidden, the key may not be allowed to do that action. See [What can my API key do?](/help/api/api-permissions-plain).

## Common messages

| What you see | Likely cause | What to try |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Invalid or missing API key | Typo, truncated key, or revoked key | Create a new key and replace it |
| Unauthorized / 401 | Same as above | Confirm Bearer header and key value |
| Forbidden / 403 | Key lacks the needed capability | Use a key from a role that can do that action, or change the integration |
| Too many requests / 429 | Rate limit or free quota | See [Too many requests and rate limits](/help/api/rate-limits-and-429) |
| Payment required / 402 | Billing block or spend limit | See [Payment required messages](/help/account/payment-required) |

## Still stuck

Check [Service status](/help/api/status-page). If the service looks healthy, send the exact error text and timestamp to [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com). Do not include the full API key in that email.

# Which organization does my API key belong to?

Keys and API bills follow the Business organization where the key was created.

Every API key belongs to one organization. Usage and billing for that key go to that same organization, not to a different workspace you happen to have open later.

## How to tell

Open [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys) and look at which organization is selected in Worklittle Business. Keys listed there belong to that organization.

If you switch organizations, you see a different key list and a different bill. See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization).

## Personal vs company

- A Personal organization is for individual API usage and consumer-related billing
- A company organization is where hiring, candidates, teammates, and employer APIs usually live

Create the key in the organization that should own the integration and pay for its usage.

## Related

- [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview)
- [Usage dashboard](/help/account/usage)
- [How does API usage get billed?](/help/api/api-usage-and-billing)

# What can my API key do?

Scopes and roles in plain English: what a key is allowed to access.

An API key can only do what it is allowed to do. In Worklittle, that usually follows the permissions of the person who created the key in that organization.

## Think in capabilities, not jargon

Common capabilities include:

- Read jobs and company data
- Apply or submit applications
- Post jobs for your organization
- Manage candidates and hiring pipeline data
- Manage webhooks
- Work with employees, surveys, or documents on the Business side

If a call returns forbidden, the key does not have that capability.

## Who can create powerful keys

Owners and people with enough edit access can create keys for the organization. A key from a limited role cannot suddenly unlock owner-only actions.

If your developer needs more access, an owner may need to create the key or raise the teammate’s role. See [Roles and permissions](/help/business-basics/roles-permissions).

## Where the full lists live

Developers should read the scope tables in the [Jobs API keys docs](/jobs/get-started/api-keys) and [Business API keys docs](/business/get-started/api-keys). This Help article stays at the everyday level on purpose.

# Too many requests and rate limits

What a 429 means, the default per-key limit, and what to do next.

A 429 or “too many requests” response means Worklittle asked your integration to slow down, or a free monthly quota was used up. It is a guardrail, not a permanent ban.

## Two different slows

- Per-minute rate limits stop a burst of calls that is too fast
- Monthly free quotas stop some free routes after the month’s allowance is used

Both can look like “too many requests,” but the fix is different.

## Default key limit

Authenticated API keys default to about 60 requests per minute per key. Public job-board pages have their own per-IP limits.

If your developer is looping too quickly, they should wait and retry with backoff, cache results, or reduce how often the integration polls.

## What to do

1. Pause and retry after a short wait.
2. Confirm you are not creating a new connection for every tiny request.
3. Check [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) and [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits).
4. Read the detailed tables in [Jobs rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits) or [Business rate limits](/business/resources/rate-limits).

If you believe you are under the limit and still see errors, see [Common API errors](/help/api/common-api-errors).

# Common API errors

Plain-English meanings for 401, 402, 403, 429, and similar failures.

API errors look technical, but most of them point to a simple fix: key, permission, billing, or speed.

## Error map

| Code | Everyday meaning | First fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 401 | Worklittle did not accept the key | Check the key, Bearer header, and whether it was revoked |
| 403 | The key is recognized but not allowed to do that | Use a key with the right capabilities |
| 402 | Billing is blocking metered usage | Update the card or raise the spend limit |
| 429 | Too fast, or a free quota is used up | Slow down, wait, or review quotas |
| 5xx | Something failed on our side | Check [Service status](/help/api/status-page), then retry |

REST bodies keep `error.code` and `error.message`. For 401, 402, 403, and 429 they also include `error.documentation_url` pointing at the matching Help article so an agent or script can open the fix without guessing.

- [Why is my API key not working?](/help/api/api-key-not-working)

- [Payment required messages](/help/account/payment-required)

# How does API usage get billed?

Keys are free. AI token usage accrues to the organization wallet.

Creating an API key does not cost money. Some API actions are free within monthly quotas. AI-powered actions add to amount owed on the organization that owns the key.

## The basic rules

- Keys themselves are free
- Many search and ATS-style routes are free within published monthly quotas
- AI token usage accrues as amount owed on that organization (including Apply with AI)
- Hosted apply is $0.01 per successful submit
- We charge the org card on the **1st of each UTC month** if owed is at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20

See [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview) and [Pricing basics](/help/account/pricing-help).

## Instant is not API credit

Worklittle Instant is the job-seeker plan for AI on worklittle.com. It does not pay for public API traffic on an `sk-wl-api01-` key. API usage bills the organization wallet instead. See [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).

## Where to watch spend

- [Usage](https://worklittle.com/business/usage) for what ran and what it cost
- [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) for amount owed and the card
- [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits) for a monthly cap

Make sure the right organization is selected first. See [Which organization does my API key belong to?](/help/api/which-org-for-api).

# What is free on the API vs what costs money?

Free monthly quotas versus AI token charges, without the full pricing tables.

A lot of API traffic is free within monthly quotas. Paid meters are AI token usage, plus $0.01 hosted apply submits on Jobs. This page points you to the right docs instead of reprinting every number.

## Usually free within quotas

Job search, many job detail and map reads, emails within quota, and most ATS-style actions are free up to the published monthly limits on the Rate limits pages.

## Usually paid

AI token usage accrues as amount owed. That includes model-backed features your integration calls on purpose, including Apply with AI (typically about $0.01–$0.03 per application). Resumes and cover letters are typically under $0.01. Chat messages are typically under $0.005. First-time AI job descriptions after the free daily allowance are typically under $0.01. Hosted apply is $0.01 per successful submit. Business Platform is mainly AI tokens.

Exact rates live on [Jobs pricing](/jobs/get-started/pricing) and [Business pricing](/business/get-started/pricing). Quotas live on [Jobs rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits) and [Business rate limits](/business/resources/rate-limits).

# REST, SDK, CLI, or MCP?

Pick the right way in based on who is calling Worklittle.

One Worklittle key works across the main ways in. The choice is about convenience, not a different account.

## Quick picker

| Situation | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| A developer is building an app or backend | REST or the official SDK |
| Someone wants shell scripts or quick tests | CLI |
| You use Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or another MCP client | MCP |
| You only need the website | Neither. Use the apps |

## Plain English

- REST is direct HTTP calls
- The SDK wraps REST with helper methods in TypeScript or Python
- The CLI is the same API from a terminal
- MCP lets an AI assistant call Worklittle tools for you

See also [REST vs MCP in plain English](/help/api/rest-vs-mcp-plain) and the deeper [REST vs MCP](/use-cases/rest-vs-mcp) page.

## Docs for each path

- [Jobs libraries](/jobs/libraries/overview)
- [Business libraries](/business/libraries/overview)
- [MCP guide](/jobs/mcp)

# Connect an AI tool without writing code

Use MCP or the Jobs app in ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code when you do not want a custom integration.

You do not always need a developer. Some AI tools can connect to Worklittle through MCP or a built-in Jobs experience, including ChatGPT, Claude, VS Code, and your own applications.

## MCP

MCP lets an AI assistant look up real Worklittle data after you connect it once. You usually still need an API key. Start with the [MCP guide](/jobs/mcp) and [REST vs MCP in plain English](/help/api/rest-vs-mcp-plain).

## ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code

Worklittle also has a Jobs experience inside ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code for swiping and browsing roles. You can search, save, open Maps, and apply. See [Worklittle in ChatGPT, Claude, and VS Code](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-app). For a product you build, use [Search jobs](/jobs/api/search-jobs) or [Jobs MCP](/jobs/mcp).

## When you still need a developer

If you want Worklittle data inside your own website, ATS, or internal tool, that is a custom integration. Hand your developer [What is the Worklittle API?](/help/api/what-is-worklittle-api) and [How do I give a developer access?](/help/api/hand-off-api-to-developer).

# What are webhooks?

How Worklittle can notify another system when hiring events happen.

A webhook is a message Worklittle sends to your other software when something important happens, such as a candidate moving stages. You only need webhooks if another system should react automatically.

## When webhooks help

- Your ATS or CRM should update when a candidate applies
- An internal tool should open a task when someone is hired
- You want event-driven sync instead of constant polling

If your team only works inside Worklittle Business, you may not need webhooks at all.

## What you need

Webhooks are a Business feature. A developer sets up an HTTPS URL that can receive events, and an API key with webhook management access. Details are in the [Business webhooks overview](/business/webhooks/overview).

## Related

- [Automations overview](/help/automations/automations-overview) if you want workflows inside Worklittle instead
- [What can my API key do?](/help/api/api-permissions-plain)

# How do I give a developer access?

Create a key, share it securely, send the right docs, and set a spend limit.

You can stay non-technical and still unblock a developer. Create the key in the right organization, hand it over safely, and point them at the docs.

## Steps

1. Switch to the organization that should own the integration. See [Switch organizations](/help/business-basics/switch-organization).
2. Create a named key on [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys).
3. Copy it once into a password manager or secure channel. Do not put it in Slack forever or in a ticket that many people can see.
4. Send your developer [Jobs overview](/jobs/get-started/overview) or [Business overview](/business/get-started/overview), plus [MCP](/jobs/mcp) if they are building an agent.
5. Set a monthly spend limit on [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits) so surprises stay small.

## What to tell them

- Base URL: https://api.worklittle.com
- MCP URL when needed: https://mcp.worklittle.com
- Key format starts with `sk-wl-api01-`
- Default authenticated rate limit is about 60 requests per minute per key
- Billing follows the organization that owns the key

## Related

- [Share or rotate an API key](/help/api/share-or-rotate-api-keys)
- [How does API usage get billed?](/help/api/api-usage-and-billing)

# Why does the API feel slow?

Practical checks for latency, retries, AI calls, and outages.

Slow responses usually come from the integration pattern, AI-heavy calls, retries, or an incident, not from a secret speed setting you forgot to flip.

## Checks that help

1. Look at [Service status](/help/api/status-page).
2. See whether the call is doing AI work. Model-backed routes take longer than a plain job search.
3. Ask whether the client is retrying too aggressively and creating a pile-up. See [Too many requests and rate limits](/help/api/rate-limits-and-429).
4. Confirm the integration is not refetching the same data on every page view when a short cache would do.
5. Compare a simple health-style call with the heavy call your product is making.

## What Worklittle does not promise here

Help Center does not publish a latency SLA for each route. If something is unusually slow and status looks fine, send the route, time, and region to [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com).

# Cancel Worklittle Instant

How to cancel Instant, what happens to your credit, and when the last charge applies.

You can cancel Worklittle Instant anytime. Cancellation takes effect at the end of the period you already paid for, so you keep Instant until then.

## How to cancel

1. Select your Personal organization.
2. Open [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing), or Manage billing under Account in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings#account).
3. Or open [Adjust plan](https://worklittle.com/plans?=adjust) from Upgrade plan.
4. Use the Stripe customer portal to cancel Instant.

You can also start from [Get Instant](https://worklittle.com/instant) or [Plans](https://worklittle.com/plans). See [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).

## What happens after you cancel

- You keep Instant until the end of the current paid period.
- After that, you leave Instant. You go back to free monthly AI unless you keep a Personal card for pay as you go.
- Unused Instant credit does not roll over and is not cash.
- Referral rewards already earned stay as Instant usage credit while they still apply. New referrals need an active Instant plan.

See [AI usage limits](/help/account/daily-ai-limits) and [Refer friends](/help/account/refer-friends).

## EEA, UK, and Switzerland

If you are in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you have 14 days to withdraw from Instant without giving a reason. Email [contact@worklittle.com](mailto:contact@worklittle.com), or cancel from [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) / [Adjust plan](https://worklittle.com/plans?=adjust). If you start using paid AI during that period, you owe a proportionate amount for what you used before withdrawing.

## Related

- [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant)
- [Refunds and withdrawals](/help/account/refunds)
- [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview)

# Add, change, or remove a payment method

Manage the card or bank account Stripe uses for Instant and pay-as-you-go billing.

Payment methods are managed through Stripe on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). Each organization (including Personal) has its own payment method.

## Open payment settings

1. Switch to the organization whose bill you want to fix. See [Which organization am I paying for?](/help/account/which-org-am-i-billed).
2. Open [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing).
3. Choose Add payment method or Manage payment method.
4. Finish the steps in the Stripe customer portal.

You can also open Manage billing under Account in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings#account).

## What you can use

Stripe may offer cards, Link, and U.S. bank account (ACH) depending on what is available for your account. Billing is in USD.

You can also add usage credit on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) with **Buy credit**. See [Can I buy prepaid credits?](/help/account/no-prepaid-credits).

## Remove a payment method

Open Manage payment method on Billing and remove or replace the method in Stripe.

If you still owe money, or Instant is active, keep a valid method on file until the bill is clear and Instant is canceled. Removing the only method can block metered chat and API usage. See [Payment required messages](/help/account/payment-required).

## Related

# Refunds and withdrawals

What Instant credit means for refunds, and how EEA/UK/Switzerland withdrawal works.

There is no self-serve refund button in the app. Instant AI credit is for usage only. It is not cash and is not refundable as spending money.

## Gift credits

If you pay to [gift credits](/help/account/gifting-credits) and the recipient does not claim within 30 days, Stripe refunds that charge automatically. Claimed gift credit is usage credit. It is not refunded as cash, and unused remainder expires 365 days after the claim.

## Added credit

Credit you buy with **Buy credit** on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) is usage credit on that organization. It is not paid out as cash. See [Can I buy prepaid credits?](/help/account/no-prepaid-credits).

## Instant credit

The $20 monthly Instant credit (and referral bonus credit) is usage credit. It does not roll over, cannot be moved to another account, and is not paid out as cash. See [Worklittle Instant](/help/account/worklittle-instant).

## Canceling vs refunding

Cancel Instant to stop future renewals at period end. That is different from a refund of a past charge. See [Cancel Worklittle Instant](/help/account/cancel-instant).

## EEA, UK, and Switzerland withdrawal

If you are in the EEA, UK, or Switzerland, you have 14 days to withdraw from Instant without giving a reason. Email [contact@worklittle.com](mailto:contact@worklittle.com), or cancel from [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing) / [Adjust plan](https://worklittle.com/plans?=adjust). If you used paid AI during that period, you owe a proportionate amount for what you used before withdrawing.

## Other billing questions

For an unrecognized charge, start with [I see a charge I do not recognize](/help/account/unrecognized-charge). For other billing help, email [support@worklittle.com](mailto:support@worklittle.com) with the invoice date and amount.

If a referred Instant purchase is refunded or disputed, the referral bonus can be removed. See [Referral Terms](/help/account/referral-terms).

# Connect with AI (voice)

Talk with Worklittle using the Live AI voice orb, separate from typing dictation.

Connect with AI starts a spoken conversation with Worklittle. A Live AI orb appears while you talk. This is different from the microphone that turns speech into text in the message box.

## Start a voice conversation

1. Open [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com).
2. Choose Connect with AI near the composer (wording can vary by screen size).
3. Allow microphone access when the browser asks, unless you are out of AI credit. Then Connect behaves like Send: **Log in for higher usage** (guest) or Plans (signed in), and the mic does not start.
4. You can start talking right away, even while the Live AI orb is still connecting. The first thing you say is kept and sent when you finish that sentence, not cut off when the session comes up.
5. Speak normally after that. The orb shows that the session is active.
6. End the session when you are done, or start a new chat to tear it down.

On [About](https://worklittle.com/about), [Research](https://worklittle.com/research), and research articles, Connect with AI opens the consumer app and starts Live there.

Live AI is mic-only. It does not use your camera for a video call.

## Dictation vs Connect with AI

| Feature | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Microphone dictation | Turns speech into text in the message box. You review and send. About 3 minutes per take. See [Voice dictation](/help/chat-ai/dictation). |
| Connect with AI | A live spoken conversation with the assistant. |

Pick dictation when you want to edit before sending. Pick Connect with AI when you want to talk back and forth.

## Limits and troubleshooting

Voice sessions use AI allowance the same way other chat features do. See [Chat and AI limits](/help/chat-ai/chat-and-ai-limits).

If the mic will not start, check browser permission in the address-bar padlock, close other apps holding the mic, and try another browser. Same checklist as [Voice dictation](/help/chat-ai/dictation).

# Do we buy seats for Business?

No. Worklittle Business bills as you go, not named seats.

No. There are no Business seats to purchase. Each company has its own bill and payment method.

## How billing works

AI and other paid usage for a company adds to that company’s amount owed. We charge on the **1st of each UTC month** if you owe at least **$0.50**, or **sooner when amount owed reaches $20**.

Manage the card and invoices on [Billing](https://worklittle.com/business/billing). Cap spend under [Billing > Limits](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits).

Details: [Billing overview](/help/account/billing-overview) and [When Worklittle charges your card](/help/account/when-we-charge).

## Teammates are not seats

# When is my company charged?

On the 1st of each UTC month (if you owe at least $0.50), or sooner at $20 owed.

Usually on the 1st of each month (UTC). Usage during the month adds to amount owed. We charge the company card on the 1st of each UTC month if you owe at least $0.50, or sooner when amount owed reaches $20.

## When we charge

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| 1st of each UTC month | We charge amount owed if it is at least $0.50 |
| Amount owed reaches $20 | We charge that day (checked about once an hour) |
| Under $0.50 unpaid | Waits until the next charge window |

UTC means Coordinated Universal Time, not your local calendar day. Collection runs on an hourly schedule, so the charge starts on that UTC day rather than at one fixed bank time.

Only Full access and Owner can open Billing. See [Who can see Usage and Billing?](/help/business-basics/who-sees-usage).

# Leave an organization

How to leave a company workspace and what happens to your access.

You can leave a company organization from the Organization page when other people are still on the team. You lose access right away. The organization’s jobs and records stay with the company.

## How to leave

1. Switch to that company organization.
2. Open [Organization](https://worklittle.com/business/organization).

If you need to pick a specific new Owner first, use [Transfer ownership](/help/business-basics/transfer-ownership) (that transfer waits about a minute).

# Marketing and ads privacy

How Marketing measurement and Personalized marketing work in Settings.

Worklittle does not show a cookie popup. You control Google Analytics, Clarity, and ads from Privacy in Settings.

## Where to change it

Open [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) or [Business Settings](https://worklittle.com/business). Privacy sits under Account. There are two switches:

- **Marketing measurement** — Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity
- **Personalized marketing** — Google ads personalization, and hiding your profile from People Search when that product is on

Guests can change them on this device. When you are signed in, the choice saves to your account and follows you. Turning **Marketing measurement** off stops new Google Analytics hits and Microsoft Clarity session recordings on worklittle.com, marketing pages, and Worklittle Business. Marketing pages pick up the change on the next page load.

## Defaults

Both switches default **on**, including in California and the rest of the United States. If we see you in the EEA, the UK, or Switzerland, both default **off** until you turn them on. Defaults follow country (and US state when we have it). A browser Global Privacy Control signal does not flip the switches.

Turning **Personalized marketing** off also removes you from the recruiter People Search directory (paid unlocks included). It does not turn off Marketing measurement (Analytics and Clarity). Employer ATS records for jobs you already applied to stay with that company.

How long account data and chat files stay, and how you can delete things yourself.

# What is Worklittle Maps?

See nearby jobs on a map, then open a company or a role.

Maps is how you look at jobs the way you look at a neighborhood. It plots roles that have a real place you can travel to, across **150+ countries**, and it is built for state-of-the-art speed when those results appear.

## Open Maps

Go to [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps), choose **Maps** in the sidebar, or tap **Maps** in the bottom navigation on a phone. On [home](https://worklittle.com/) you can also tap **Open jobs map** on the Near you preview.

## What you will see

You get a street map of the area you are looking at, company logos with a number of nearby openings, and a job list for that same area. On a computer the list sits on the left. On a phone it lives in a sheet you pull up from the bottom.

Drag to move around, and pinch or use the zoom buttons to go from a few blocks to a whole country. The list and logos follow the part of the map that is on screen.

Remote-only roles live on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) and in search. Maps stays focused on work you can commute to. See [Search for jobs on a map](/help/worklittle-maps/search-for-jobs-on-a-map) and [What Maps leaves out](/help/worklittle-maps/what-maps-leaves-out) for the rest of that split.

## How it fits with the rest of Worklittle

| You want | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One job at a time | [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) and [Swipe to apply](/help/finding-jobs/jobs-deck) |
| Commute and neighborhood | [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) |
| Every role at one employer | A [company page](/help/finding-jobs/company-pages), including over Maps |
| Saved pipeline | [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) |

Date, experience, type, and visa chips stay in sync with the homepage while you stay in the same browser tab. Reloading the page restores the usual defaults.

# Open Maps and move around

Center the map, then pan and zoom to the commute you want.

The jobs on screen belong to the part of the map you are looking at. Pan and zoom to the commute you would actually take, and the list and logos follow.

## Start near you

Open [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps). If the browser already allowed location, the map starts near you. Otherwise tap **current location** and allow it when the prompt appears. If you skip that prompt, Worklittle still starts from an approximate location so you can look around right away.

Location is used to center the map and to estimate walk or drive time on nearby cards. To refresh it later, tap current location again. Maps is where you grant that permission. [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings) keeps the rest of your profile.

## Pan and zoom

Drag to move. Pinch, scroll, or use the **+** and **−** buttons on a computer. Zoom in for a neighborhood and zoom out for a metro or a whole country. Country jumps from search go farther out than city jumps.

On a computer the job list stays on the left. On a phone the map fills the screen and the list sits in a sheet. Leaving Maps and coming back in the same tab keeps the view until you reload.

# Search jobs and jump to a place

Use the Maps search box for a title, a city, or a company.

The Maps search box can find a role, jump the map to a place, or open a company. Coverage includes **150+ countries**, so you can go from your neighborhood to another country in the same box.

## Search a job title

Type a title or keyword, for example **nurse** or **software engineer**. Short abbreviations expand the way homepage suggestions do, so typing **swe** also matches Software Engineer.

On a computer and on a phone, the Maps box shows the same suggestions (titles, recent searches, places, and companies). On a phone, the list only shows as many rows as fit under the box and above the keyboard. If the keyboard is not covering the screen, you get the same maximum as on a computer.

That search stays in the Maps link so you can copy it later. It is separate from the **Job title** field in [Settings](https://worklittle.com/settings), which is for alerts and matching.

## Jump to a city, campus, or country

Type a place, including school names like Texas A&M or Penn State, then press **Enter** or pick a suggestion. The map jumps there and the search box clears so you can type a title next if you want.

Recent place jumps are remembered on this device. Copy the address bar when you want to send someone that view. Short city codes work too, which is useful on a poster QR. Examples: [worklittle.com/maps?=sf](https://worklittle.com/maps?=sf) and [worklittle.com/maps?=Japan](https://worklittle.com/maps?=Japan).

## Type a company name

If the query matches an employer, Maps opens that [company page](/help/finding-jobs/company-pages) over the map. Nearby jobs follow the area you are looking at. A shared link looks like [worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe](https://worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe). Full walkthrough: [Companies on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/companies-on-maps).

- **Roles outside your chips** stay available once you widen date, type, experience, visa, or the words in the search box. See [Filter jobs on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/maps-filters).

In a busy city, Maps shows a fast first set of company logos. Pan or zoom a little and more employers come into view.

# The job list next to the map

Nearby roles, estimated commute, and opening a posting.

The list is the nearby jobs for the area you are looking at, closest first, then newest. It is meant to pair with the map so you can read titles while you still see the neighborhood.

## What a row shows

Each row shows the title, the company, how recently it was posted, visa sponsorship when we know it, and an estimated **walk** or **drive** time when the job is close to you. Walk time appears for short nearby trips. Farther jobs may show drive minutes. Those minutes are estimates you can compare at a glance.

## Open a job

Tap a card to read the posting on top of the map. Apply, save, and press-and-hold actions work the same as elsewhere. See [Open a job from Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/jobs-from-maps).

If the list looks quiet, pan to a denser area, zoom out, or loosen [filters](/help/worklittle-maps/maps-filters). Remote-only roles stay on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs). # Filter jobs on Maps

Narrow the logos and the nearby list by title, date, type, experience, visa, and sort.

Filters help you keep the map on the roles you actually want. The same date, experience, type, visa, and Sort by chips also sit above Near you on [worklittle.com](https://worklittle.com/).

## The filters you can set

| Filter | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Search | Matches a job title or keyword in the Maps search box. Short abbreviations expand like search suggestions. Company names open that employer’s [company page](/help/finding-jobs/company-pages). |
| Date posted | Past 24 hours, Past 3 days, Past 7 days (the usual start), Past 14 days, or Past 30 days |
| Type | Full-time, Part-time, Contract. You can pick more than one. |
| Experience | Intern, Entry level, Senior, Manager, or Director / Executive. You can pick more than one. |
| Visa | Opens a Sponsors visa switch. When it is on, the chip reads **Visa only** |
| Sort by | Relevance (the usual list), Distance, Salary, or Newest. Salary uses listed annualized pay. Roles without pay sit last. Distance, Salary, and Newest keep that order as you scroll for more. |

Filters stack, so a title plus an experience level gives you a tighter view. Clear one chip to bring more jobs back. On Experience and Type, tap outside the menu to close it.

Chips you set on the homepage or Maps stay in sync while you move between those screens in the same tab. Reloading the page restores the usual defaults.

## The map is your area

Pan and zoom to the patch you would travel to, and the list follows that view. Zooming out shows a larger area. Start broad, then add one filter at a time so you can see what each one does. Save roles as you go with [Heart and save a job](/help/finding-jobs/heart-save).

# Companies on Maps

Open an employer over the map, nearby roles first.

A company page over Maps is the same employer hub as [worklittle.com/company/…](https://worklittle.com/), with extra nearby context from the area you are looking at.

## How to open it

Tap a [company logo](/help/worklittle-maps/company-chips) on the map, type the company name in Maps search and choose the suggestion, or open a shared link such as [worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe](https://worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe).

## Nearby, then anywhere

The board lists jobs near the map first, then the rest of that employer’s openings in other cities. You can search inside the board for a title. If you already typed a role in Maps search, matching titles can float up.

# Open a job from Maps

Read the posting, apply, or save, while the map stays behind.

Opening a listing from Maps keeps the map behind the posting so you can jump back to nearby roles when you are done.

## Open the posting

Tap a job in the [nearby list](/help/worklittle-maps/job-list) or on a company board. You stay on Maps while you read it. The same job is also available from [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs).

## Apply, save, and similar roles

**Apply** starts [Apply with AI](/help/apply-with-ai/what-is-apply-with-ai) when that job supports it. Heart or **Save** sends the role to [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved). A company logo opens the company. A job in the list is where you apply.

# Share a Maps link

Send someone a place, a search, a company, or a job on Maps.

Once the map shows the view you want, copy the link from the top of the page and paste it to a friend.

## What they will open

| Example | What it opens |
| --- | --- |
| [worklittle.com/maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) | Maps, starting near you or your last view |
| [worklittle.com/maps?=Austin](https://worklittle.com/maps?=Austin) | Jumps to that place |

| [worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe](https://worklittle.com/maps/company/stripe) | That company over Maps |
| A job link from Maps | That posting over Maps |

You can combine a place and a title when both are set. If you jump to a city and then pan a long way, copy the link again after you settle so it matches the view you actually have.

# Maps and the homepage

Near you, shared chips, and Open jobs map.

Home and Maps share the same nearby jobs idea. Filters you set on one follow you to the other in that tab.

## Near you on home

While you are signed in, the homepage can show a map preview with company logos and an **Open jobs map** control. That opens [Maps](https://worklittle.com/maps) at the same kind of nearby view. Location comes from Maps when you have allowed it, and otherwise from an approximate location. While you are signed out, home still shows that map preview from an approximate location. The job list is **Explore jobs** from your US state (or your country outside the US) until you choose Distance or set a job title. [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs) stays a swipe-first screen, so location permission lives on Maps.

## Shared chips

Date, experience, type, visa, and Sort by chips above Near you are the same controls as [Filter jobs on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/maps-filters). Changing them on home updates Maps until you reload the page.

Fetch the complete documentation index at: https://docs.worklittle.com/docs-agent-manifest.json Use this file to discover all available pages before exploring further.

# Maps looks empty or in the wrong place

What to try when the list is quiet or the city looks off.

A quiet view is usually a tight filter, a zoomed-in patch, or remote-only search. The wrong city is usually location permission.

## Bring more jobs into view

1. Zoom out, or type a city. Maps covers **150+ countries**, so a quiet countryside view is common until you move.
2. Clear the search box and widen date, experience, type, or visa chips. See [Filter jobs on Maps](/help/worklittle-maps/maps-filters).
3. Check [What Maps leaves out](/help/worklittle-maps/what-maps-leaves-out). Remote-only roles live on [Jobs](https://worklittle.com/jobs). Skipped and saved roles live on [Saved](https://worklittle.com/saved) when you are signed in.
4. Tap **current location** and allow the browser prompt. If you turned location off earlier, open the site settings for worklittle.com and allow it, then try again.

Reload the tab to restore the usual filters. If the map itself stays blank, try another browser or email [hello@worklittle.com](mailto:hello@worklittle.com).

# Overview

Jobs API for searching millions of open roles, public company boards, apply flows, and AI document tools.

Low-cost data for millions of jobs with a combined worth of $10 billion, updated hourly. Each job includes geocoded location data so you can build map search, radius filters, and local discovery.

## What Jobs docs cover

Use these docs when you are building **job discovery** or **candidate-facing apply** on top of Worklittle's market index - not when you are running your company's ATS inside Worklittle.

Typical Jobs integrations:

1. **Market job search** - `GET /jobs` and `GET /jobs/:id` (or MCP `search_jobs` / `get_job_details`) with location, salary, and company filters.
2. **Company discovery** - `GET /companies` and `GET /jobs/map` for employers with open roles.
3. **Public career boards** - Unauthenticated `/job-boards/:company/…` listings and apply for jobs the employer published on Worklittle.
4. **Apply and documents** - Hosted apply (`jobs:apply`), Apply with AI, and `POST /v1/resumes` / `POST /v1/cover-letters`.

For posting jobs, moving candidates, surveys, documents, attendance, or webhooks, switch to [Business docs](/business/get-started/overview).

## Base URLs

| Surface | Base URL |
| --- | --- |
| REST Jobs API | `https://api.worklittle.com` |
| MCP | `https://mcp.worklittle.com` (POST `/`) |
| Public job boards | `https://api.worklittle.com/job-boards/:company/jobs` |
| Health | `GET https://api.worklittle.com/health` |

AI token pricing is on [Pricing](/jobs/get-started/pricing). Free quotas and per-minute limits are on [Rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits).

## Authentication

Paid Jobs routes expect a **Bearer API key**:

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk-wl-api01-...
```

Create keys under [**API keys**](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys). Common Jobs scopes: `jobs:read`, `jobs:apply`, `agent:tools`. Details: [API Keys](/jobs/get-started/api-keys).

**Public job board** GETs and public board apply do not require a key. They are rate limited per IP.

Export the key as an environment variable. The SDK and CLI read `WORKLITTLE_API_KEY` automatically.

export WORKLITTLE_API_KEY="sk-wl-api01-..."

curl -s "https://api.worklittle.com/jobs?q=software+engineer&limit=5" \

# API Keys

API keys for Jobs search, apply, and document tools. Create and revoke them in Worklittle Business.

## Create a key

In the [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business), go to [**API keys**](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys) and select **Create API key**. Name the key for your environment (for example "Production backend"). The response shows the full `sk-wl-api01-...` secret **once**.

Store it in a secrets manager or environment variable. Worklittle never shows the full secret again, only a prefix for identification.

## Revoke a key

On the same [**API keys**](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys) page, open the menu on a row and choose **Revoke**. The key stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.

To rotate, create a new key, deploy the new secret, then revoke the old key.

## Key format and scopes

Keys use the `sk-wl-api01-` prefix. Default rate limit is **60 requests per minute** per key. View per-key limits on [**Limits**](https://worklittle.com/business/limits) in Worklittle Business.

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `jobs:read` | `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/:id`, `GET /jobs/map`, `GET /stats`, `GET /account` |
| `jobs:apply` | `POST /jobs/:id/apply`, MCP `submit_job_application` |
| `people:read` | Reserved - public People Search is temporarily unavailable |
| `agent:tools` | `POST /v1/resumes`, `POST /v1/cover-letters`, `POST /v1/agent/tool` |

New keys receive the default scopes for your account. Agents in Worklittle Business can also call `list_api_keys` and `revoke_api_key` when you approve those actions.

## Session routes (Worklittle Business backend)

When you are signed in, the Worklittle Business calls these routes on `api.worklittle.com` with your session (not your `sk-wl-api01-...` secret):

| Method | Path | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api-keys` | List your keys |
| POST | `/api-keys` | Create a key |
| DELETE | `/api-keys/:id` | Revoke a key |

Use the [**API keys**](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys) UI unless you are building your own session-authenticated client.

# Pricing

Jobs API and MCP bill for AI token usage. Add a payment method for higher access to AI features.

## AI usage

| What bills | When | Price |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AI tokens** | Model-backed Jobs API / MCP tools, including Apply with AI | **$2.50** per 1M input tokens and **$15.00** per 1M output tokens |

**The cost of AI features varies based on token usage:**

- **Apply with AI (`POST /v1/apply-with-ai` / MCP `start_apply_with_ai`):** about $0.01–$0.03 per application
- **Resume (`create_resume`):** about <$0.01
- **Cover letter (`create_cover_letter`):** about <$0.01
- **Chat messages:** about <$0.005 per message
- **First-time AI job-description generation (`GET /jobs/:id` / MCP `get_job_details`):** typically <$0.01 after the free daily allowance (see [Rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits))

[Worklittle Instant](https://worklittle.com/instant) subscribers have access to up to 2,000 included Apply with AI applications per month. The subscription is $9.99/month and provides $20 in monthly AI credit to your Personal organization. All users have access to API features available to Personal organizations. If you have no credits, billing is charged pay as you go. You can create a [Spend limit](https://worklittle.com/business/billing#limits) to cap your usage and billing.

## Free quotas and rate limits

Monthly free quotas (job search, companies, map, soft AI detail generations) and the **60 requests/minute** key limit live on [Rate limits](/jobs/resources/rate-limits).

## Free without an API key

| Surface | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **Public job boards** | `GET /job-boards/:company/*`, `POST .../apply` - IP rate limits |
| **Docs assistant** | Chat on [docs.worklittle.com](https://docs.worklittle.com). No API key |

## Support

Inquire at [business@worklittle.com](mailto:business@worklittle.com) for custom pricing and higher rate limits. We charge at the end of each UTC month for accrued usage (if at least $0.50), and earlier when amount owed reaches $20.

## Looking for Business Platform pricing?

Platform agent chat and Work AI live under [Business pricing](/business/get-started/pricing). ATS and posting routes stay free with an API key.

# Libraries overview

Official Worklittle SDK and CLI for job search, boards, apply, and document tools.

## Overview

The SDK and CLI call the same Jobs API as curl. Use them to search the market index, read company maps, drive public boards, submit hosted applications, and generate résumés from a script or agent.

For posting jobs and ATS automation, see [Business libraries](/business/libraries/overview).

## Base URL

```text
https://api.worklittle.com
```

## Authentication

Bearer token. Create a key in the [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business) under [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys).

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk-wl-api01-...
```

For the SDK and CLI, set `WORKLITTLE_API_KEY`. Prefer the env var over `--api-key` so the key does not appear in process lists. Do not point `--base-url` at hosts you do not trust. Public board GETs and public survey submit do not require a key.

## Clients

**CLI**

```bash
brew install worklittle/tap/worklittle
```

| Client | Install |

| TypeScript SDK | `npm install worklittle` ([docs](/jobs/libraries/sdk#typescript)) |

Published packages:

```bash
npm install worklittle
pip install worklittle
```

The TypeScript package is also on npm as `@worklittle/sdk` (same code). The CLI binary is `worklittle` (`npm install -g worklittle`). Homebrew remains the recommended CLI install.

## Quickstart

```bash
export WORKLITTLE_API_KEY="sk-wl-api01-..."
brew install worklittle/tap/worklittle
worklittle jobs search --q="software engineer" --limit 3 --pretty
```

Or call the API directly:

  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKLITTLE_API_KEY"

## Surfaces

| [SDK](/jobs/libraries/sdk) | In-process client |
| [MCP](/jobs/mcp) | JSON-RPC tools for MCP clients |

# SDK

TypeScript and Python clients for api.worklittle.com. Same key, same resources. Language tabs below.

## Install

```bash
npm install worklittle
export WORKLITTLE_API_KEY="sk-wl-api01-..."
```

Import as `worklittle`. To work from the monorepo instead: `cd packages/sdk-js && npm install && npm run build`.

## Authentication

Bearer token. Create a key in the [Worklittle Business](https://worklittle.com/business) under [API keys](https://worklittle.com/business/api-keys).

```http
Authorization: Bearer sk-wl-api01-...
```

For the SDK and CLI, set `WORKLITTLE_API_KEY`. Prefer the env var over `--api-key` so the key does not appear in process lists. Do not point `--base-url` at hosts you do not trust. Public board GETs and public survey submit do not require a key.

## Quickstart

```ts
import { createWorklittle } from "worklittle";

const wl = createWorklittle(); // reads WORKLITTLE_API_KEY
const page = await wl.jobs.search({ q: "software engineer", limit: 3 });
```

Filters match `GET /jobs`. Title exclusions use a leading dash in `title` / `q` (`-Senior`). Employer exclusions use the same pattern on `company` (`-lucid-motors`):

```ts
await wl.jobs.search({
  title: "software engineer, -senior",
  company: "-lucid-motors,-tesla",
  limit: 10,
});
```

Equivalent HTTP:

```bash
curl -s "https://api.worklittle.com/jobs?q=software+engineer&limit=3" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKLITTLE_API_KEY"
```

## Search > detail

```ts
const page = await wl.jobs.search({ q: "software engineer", limit: 3 });
const rows = (page as { data?: Array<{ job_id?: string; id?: string }> }).data ?? [];
const id = rows[0]?.job_id || rows[0]?.id;
const detail = await wl.jobs.get(String(id));
```

**Response** (`GET /jobs`):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "job_id": "…",
      "title": "Software Engineer",
      "company_name": "Example Co",
      "location": "Remote"
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "next_cursor": "…" }
}
```

List rows are snippets. Use `GET /jobs/:id` for the full posting. See [Search jobs](/jobs/api/search-jobs).

## Board > apply

`YOUR_ORG_SLUG` is the employer board slug (same as careers URLs).

```ts
import { createWorklittle, jobCareersPath } from "worklittle";

const wl = createWorklittle();
const company = "YOUR_ORG_SLUG";
const board = (await wl.boards.get(company)) as {
  jobs: Array<{ id: string; slug?: string }>;
};
const jobRef = board.jobs[0]!.slug || board.jobs[0]!.id;
const job = await wl.boards.getJob(company, jobRef);
// job.application_fields = form schema
await wl.boards.submitApplication(company, job as never, {
  name: "Alex Rivera",
  email: "alex@example.com",
});
jobCareersPath(board.jobs[0]!); // /careers/{slug}
```

See [Apply for jobs](/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs).

## Candidates > profile

Requires a key with `jobs:applications` for your org.

```ts
const listed = await wl.candidates.list({ limit: 10 });
const detail = await wl.candidates.get("CANDIDATE_ID");
```

```bash
curl -s "https://api.worklittle.com/candidates?limit=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKLITTLE_API_KEY"
curl -s "https://api.worklittle.com/candidates/CANDIDATE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $WORKLITTLE_API_KEY"
```

See [Manage candidates](/jobs/api/manage-candidates).

## Resources

| Method | HTTP | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wl.jobs.search` / `get` | `GET /jobs`, `GET /jobs/:id` | [Search jobs](/jobs/api/search-jobs) |
| `wl.companies.search` | `GET /companies` | [Search companies](/jobs/api/search-companies) |
| `wl.boards.get` / `getJob` / `apply` | `/job-boards/:company/…` | [Apply for jobs](/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs) |
| `wl.apply.submit` | `POST /jobs/:id/apply` | [Apply for jobs](/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs) |
| `wl.apply.startWithAi` / `getWithAiSession` / `continueWithAi` / `approveWithAiSubmit` / `stopWithAi` | `/v1/apply-with-ai` | [Apply for jobs](/jobs/api/apply-for-jobs) |
| `wl.candidates.list` / `get` | `GET /candidates`, `GET /candidates/:id` | [Manage candidates](/jobs/api/manage-candidates) |
| `wl.employees.*` | `/employees` | [Manage organization](/jobs/api/manage-organization) |
| `wl.jobListings.*` / `wl.employerJobs.*` | `/job-listings`, `/jobs/post` | [Post a job](/jobs/api/post-a-job) |
| `wl.surveys.*` | `/platform/surveys` | [Surveys](/jobs/api/surveys) |
| `wl.documents.*` | `/platform/documents` | [Documents](/jobs/api/documents) |
| `wl.attendance.*` | `/attendance` | [Attendance](/jobs/api/attendance) |
| `wl.webhooks.*` | `/webhooks` | [Webhooks](/jobs/webhooks/integration) |
| `wl.resumes.*` / `wl.coverLetters.*` | `POST /v1/resumes`, `POST /v1/cover-letters` | [Create resumes](/jobs/api/create-resumes) |

## Webhooks

```ts
import { verifyWebhookSignature } from "worklittle";

const ok = verifyWebhookSignature({
  signatureHeader: req.headers["worklittle-webhook-signature"] as string,
  timestamp: req.headers["worklittle-webhook-timestamp"] as string,
  rawBody,
  secret: process.env.WORKLITTLE_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
});
```

See [Webhook integration](/jobs/webhooks/integration).

## Errors

Throws `WorklittleError` with `status`, `code`, `message`, and `requestId` when present.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **429** | Rate limited; client retries using `Retry-After` |
| **402** | Payment required (failed card or monthly limit) - do not retry |
| **401 / 403** | Invalid key or missing scope |
